title: Prepaid recharge plans
text: Sarovan Telecom prepaid recharges, effective 1 June 2026. All three main recharges include unlimited local and national calls and 100 SMS per day. Daily 1.5 costs ₹299 for 28 days and gives 1.5 GB of high-speed data per day. Daily 2 costs ₹349 for 28 days and gives 2 GB per day. Long 84 costs ₹859 for 84 days and gives 2 GB per day. Daily data resets at midnight, and unused daily data does not carry forward to the next day. Once the daily quota is used, speed drops to 64 kbps until midnight. Data boosters can be added at any time: ₹19 for 1 GB valid until midnight, or ₹49 for 3 GB valid for 3 days. 5G: customers on Daily 2 and Long 84 who are in a 5G area with a 5G phone get unlimited 5G data at no extra cost; on Daily 1.5, 5G usage counts against the daily quota. Stacking: a recharge made before the current plan ends is queued and starts automatically when the current plan expires; up to 3 plans can be queued. Expiry: when a plan expires, outgoing calls, SMS and data stop immediately, while incoming calls continue for 15 days. A number with no recharge for 90 days is permanently disconnected. Prepaid recharges are non-refundable once applied, except where a recharge fails to apply but the amount is debited, in which case it is reversed within 5 working days.

title: Flex 499 postpaid plan
text: Flex 499 is the entry postpaid plan from Sarovan Telecom. Monthly rental is ₹499 plus 18% GST. Each bill cycle includes 75 GB of data, unlimited local and national calls, and 100 SMS per day. Data rollover on Flex 499: unused data rolls over to the next bill cycle only. Rolled-over data is used before the new cycle's allowance, and any rolled-over data left at the end of that next cycle expires. It does not keep accumulating from month to month, and there is no rollover bank. Extra data: after the 75 GB allowance and any rollover are used, data is charged at ₹10 per GB, billed in 1 GB blocks, up to a maximum of ₹500 per bill cycle. Once ₹500 of extra data has been billed, speed is reduced to 256 kbps for the rest of the cycle at no further charge. Add-on family lines are not available on Flex 499. Your bill cycle starts on the 1st, 8th, 15th or 22nd of the month, chosen at activation. International roaming is switched on by default, as on all postpaid connections. You can move up to Flex 549 at any time; the change applies from the next bill cycle and any rolled-over data carries across.

title: Flex 549 postpaid plan
text: Flex 549 is the family-ready postpaid plan from Sarovan Telecom. Monthly rental is ₹549 plus 18% GST. Each bill cycle includes 100 GB of data, unlimited local and national calls, 100 SMS per day, and one free add-on family line that shares the main line's data. Up to 3 more add-on lines can be added at ₹199 per month each. Data rollover on Flex 549: unused data rolls over and keeps accumulating from cycle to cycle, up to a maximum rollover balance of 200 GB. Rollover data is lost only if you move to a different plan or close the connection. Extra data: after the 100 GB allowance and any rollover are used, speed is reduced to 1 Mbps for the rest of the bill cycle, with no extra charge. If you need full speed again, a 10 GB top-up costs ₹99 and lasts until the end of the cycle. Your bill cycle starts on the 1st, 8th, 15th or 22nd of the month, chosen at activation. International roaming is switched on by default, as on all postpaid connections. Moving down to Flex 499 takes effect from the next bill cycle; the accumulated rollover balance is lost, and add-on lines must be removed or moved to their own plans first.

title: International roaming and IR packs
text: International roaming for Sarovan mobile customers. Postpaid: international roaming is switched on by default on every postpaid connection, from the day of activation. You do not need to request it before travelling. Without a pack, pay-as-you-go rates apply: data ₹55 per MB, outgoing calls ₹90 per minute, incoming calls ₹45 per minute and SMS ₹25 each. To avoid these charges, buy a pack, or switch roaming off in the Sarovan app under Manage Services or by sending ROAM OFF to 54321. Bill-shock cap: when pay-as-you-go roaming charges in one bill cycle reach ₹5,000, roaming data is paused and we send an SMS; reply YES to continue. Calls are not paused. Prepaid: roaming is off by default. Activate it in the app at least 2 hours before departure; prepaid customers can use roaming only with a pack. IR packs, valid in 42 countries including the UAE, Singapore, Thailand, the UK and the USA: IR 7 days, ₹1,999: 2 GB data, 100 minutes of calls and 20 SMS, valid for 7 days. IR 30 days, ₹3,999: 6 GB data, 250 minutes of calls and 50 SMS, valid for 30 days. Pack minutes cover incoming calls, calls to India and local calls in the country you are visiting. A pack starts when you first connect to a partner network abroad, not when you buy it. When pack data runs out, data stops; a 1 GB top-up costs ₹599.

title: Porting your number to Sarovan
text: Moving your mobile number to Sarovan Telecom. Step 1: from the number you want to move, send an SMS with the word PORT followed by your 10-digit mobile number to 1900. You will receive a Unique Porting Code (UPC). Step 2: visit a Sarovan Experience Store or book doorstep SIM delivery in the app, with your UPC and your Aadhaar for e-KYC. There is no porting fee. Timeline: Sarovan completes port-in requests within 7 working days of KYC verification. This is longer than many operators because every port-in is manually checked by our fraud-prevention team before the switch is scheduled. We will send an SMS with your switch date. Until then, keep using your old SIM; it works as normal. On the switch night, service may be unavailable for up to 4 hours between 11 pm and 3 am; once your old SIM shows no network, insert the Sarovan SIM and restart the phone. Common reasons for rejection are unpaid dues with your current operator, an expired UPC, or a name mismatch between the UPC request and your KYC. If a request is rejected, generate a new UPC and apply again. Postpaid port-in customers get 50% off the first month's rental. Porting out of Sarovan is allowed once your number has been active with us for 90 days. We do not charge for porting out, but postpaid dues must be cleared first.

title: Lost SIM, replacement SIM and eSIM
text: Lost, stolen or damaged SIM. If your phone or SIM is lost or stolen, block your number immediately in the Sarovan app or by calling 1800 210 4455 from any phone, so the number cannot be misused. Replacement SIMs are issued only at Sarovan-owned stores (Sarovan Experience Stores), not at franchise retailers or mobile shops that sell our recharges. The connection holder must come in person with original ID. If the number is registered to a family member, that person must visit; for company connections, an authorisation letter on company letterhead is needed. Charge: ₹50 for a replacement physical SIM. It is free if the SIM developed a fault within 6 months of issue. eSIM: postpaid customers can convert to eSIM in the app at no charge; prepaid customers must visit a Sarovan Experience Store. eSIM works on most recent phones; check the compatibility list in the app. Security hold: after any SIM replacement or eSIM conversion, incoming and outgoing SMS, including OTPs, are blocked for 24 hours. Calls and data start working within 2 hours of activation. Your number, plan, balance and rollover data are not affected by a SIM replacement.

title: Documents for a new connection (KYC)
text: Documents needed for a new Sarovan connection. Indian citizens, prepaid or postpaid: Aadhaar biometric e-KYC is enough on its own. No photocopies or photographs are needed, and activation usually takes about 30 minutes. Without Aadhaar: bring your original passport, voter ID or driving licence plus one passport-size photograph. Activation takes up to 24 hours after document verification. For postpaid connections taken without Aadhaar e-KYC, a refundable security deposit of ₹500 is collected. Outstation customers, whose ID address is in a different state from where the connection is bought, must also give a local address and a local reference whose number will receive a verification call. Foreign nationals: original passport with a valid visa, proof of local address in India, and a local reference. Foreign nationals can take prepaid connections only, and the connection is valid until the visa expiry date. Minors under 18 cannot hold a connection in their own name; a parent can take the connection and register the minor as the user. Business connections need the company's GST certificate, an authorisation letter and the authorised signatory's Aadhaar e-KYC. The name on bills and all communication will match the KYC document exactly.

title: Home Fibre plans
text: Sarovan Home Fibre plans. Prices are monthly rentals plus 18% GST. Fibre 100: ₹699 per month, 100 Mbps download and upload, fair usage limit of 3,300 GB per bill cycle, after which speed drops to 10 Mbps. Fibre 300: ₹999 per month, 300 Mbps, fair usage limit of 3,300 GB, then 20 Mbps. Fibre 1G: ₹3,999 per month, 1 Gbps, fair usage limit of 5,000 GB, then 50 Mbps. After crossing the fair usage limit, full speed returns automatically at the start of the next bill cycle, or immediately with a ₹199 top-up that adds 500 GB. All plans include a landline number with unlimited local and national calls through the router's phone port; you need a regular landline handset. Speeds are the maximum line speed to the router; Wi-Fi speeds on your devices depend on the device and its distance from the router. Advance rental: pay 6 months in advance for 5% off, or 12 months in advance for 10% off. Plan upgrades take effect within 4 hours; downgrades apply from the next bill cycle. Fibre 300 and Fibre 1G include a basic video streaming bundle at no extra cost.

title: Home Fibre installation, commitment and relocation
text: Installing Sarovan Home Fibre. After you book, a technician visits within 48 hours if your building is already connected. New buildings may need a feasibility survey of up to 7 working days. The one-time installation fee of ₹1,000 covers a dual-band Wi-Fi 6 router, which is yours to keep, and up to 30 metres of fibre cable inside your premises; extra cable costs ₹20 per metre. Waiver: the ₹1,000 installation fee is waived if you pay 6 or 12 months of rental in advance, or if you choose monthly billing with a 12-month commitment. Leaving early: if you close a connection on a 12-month commitment before 12 months, the waived ₹1,000 installation fee is added to your final bill. There is no other exit fee on Home Fibre. Unused full months on advance rental plans are refunded on closure. Relocation: moving within the same city costs ₹500 and is completed within 5 working days of your request, if the new address is serviceable. If the new address is not serviceable, you can close the connection without the installation fee being recovered, even within a 12-month commitment. Moving to another city is handled as a closure followed by a new connection, and the commitment carries over without charge.

title: Router warranty and technician visits
text: Your Home Fibre router and technician visits. The Wi-Fi router supplied at installation belongs to you and comes with a 12-month warranty from the installation date. Hardware faults within the warranty are fixed with a free replacement, usually within 2 working days. After the warranty, a replacement router from Sarovan costs ₹1,200, or you can use your own compatible router and we will set it up remotely at no charge. The warranty does not cover physical damage, liquid damage or damage from power surges and lightning. Before booking a visit: switch the router off for 30 seconds and back on, check that the thin fibre cable is not bent or pinched, and look at the LOS light. A red LOS light means the fibre signal is not reaching your router, so restarting will not help; please report it. Technician visits for faults in our network, or in our fibre line up to the router, are free. If the technician finds the problem is in your own devices, your internal LAN wiring, a third-party extender or Wi-Fi settings you have changed, a ₹300 visit charge is added to your next bill. The technician will tell you before starting work if the charge applies. Visit slots run from 9 am to 7 pm, seven days a week.

title: Home Fibre outage credit
text: Outage credit for Sarovan Home Fibre. If your Home Fibre service is completely down because of a fault in our network or our fibre line, you receive an automatic credit of ₹30 per full day of outage beyond the first 48 hours. The outage is counted from when the fault is logged, either by you or by our network monitoring, until service is restored. You do not need to apply: the credit appears on your next bill. The credit is capped at ₹600 per bill cycle. Example: an outage lasting 4 full days earns 2 days of credit, which is ₹60. The credit does not apply to faults in your own devices or wiring, power cuts at your premises, planned maintenance announced by SMS at least 24 hours in advance, or damage from floods, fires and other natural disasters. Repair targets: we aim to fix 90% of faults within 24 hours. Fibre cable cuts take longer, because the break has to be located and every fibre spliced, and are usually repaired within 48 hours. Mobile network outages are not covered by this credit; if you lost mobile service, contact us and we will review your case.

title: Late payment policy, effective 1 April 2024
text: Postpaid late payment and reconnection policy, effective 1 April 2024. This applies to Sarovan postpaid mobile and Home Fibre bills. Your bill is due 15 days after the bill date. A grace period of 7 days applies after the due date. If the full amount is still unpaid when the grace period ends, a late payment fee of ₹100 is added to your next bill. Barring: outgoing calls, SMS and data are barred 15 days after the due date; incoming calls continue for mobile connections. Disconnection: the connection is fully disconnected 45 days after the due date. Reconnection: a reconnection fee of ₹100 is charged whenever services are restored after barring or disconnection. Services are restored within 24 hours of payment being received. Payments made by UPI or in the app reflect within 4 hours; cheques take up to 3 working days. Autopay customers are not charged a late fee if autopay fails because of a technical error at our end. Customers facing difficulty can request a one-time extension of 10 days by calling customer care before the due date.

title: Late payment policy, effective 1 July 2026
text: Postpaid late payment and reconnection policy, effective 1 July 2026. This replaces the April 2024 version. It applies to Sarovan postpaid mobile and Home Fibre bills. Your bill is due 15 days after the bill date. There is no grace period: if the full amount has not been received by the due date, a late payment fee of ₹250 is added on the day after the due date. Partial payments do not avoid the fee. Barring: outgoing calls, SMS and data are barred 10 days after the due date; incoming calls continue for mobile connections. Disconnection: the connection is fully disconnected 30 days after the due date. Reconnection while barred: there is no reconnection fee. Pay the full outstanding amount, including any late fee, and services are restored within 2 hours. Reconnection after full disconnection: a reconnection fee of ₹200 applies, and your number is held for 60 days after disconnection. Payments made by UPI or in the app reflect within 2 hours; cheques take up to 3 working days, so pay early if you use a cheque. Autopay customers are not charged a late fee if autopay fails because of a technical error at our end. The one-time 10-day extension offered under the earlier policy has been withdrawn.

title: Closing a postpaid or Home Fibre connection
text: Closing a Sarovan postpaid mobile or Home Fibre connection. You can request closure in the Sarovan app, at any Sarovan Experience Store, or by calling 1800 210 4455. Closure takes effect within 3 working days of the request. If you want to keep your mobile number, port it out instead of closing; closing a mobile connection releases the number. Final bill: your final bill covers usage and pro-rated rental from your last bill date up to the closure date, plus any one-time charges such as a recovered installation fee. Security deposit: any security deposit is refunded within 45 days of the final bill being paid. Refunds are made only to your registered bank account, verified through a cancelled cheque or UPI; there are no cash refunds at stores. Any credit balance on your account is refunded the same way and within the same period. Routers do not need to be returned, as the router belongs to you. Prepaid connections have no closure process or fee; simply stop recharging, and the unused part of a recharge is not refundable. If you close a connection by mistake, it can be restored within 7 days at no cost, after which a fresh connection is needed.

title: Stores, customer care and complaint escalation
text: Sarovan Experience Stores are open Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 8:30 pm, and Sunday 11 am to 6 pm. They are closed on 26 January, 15 August and 2 October. Store counters in shopping malls follow the mall's opening hours. Customer care: dial 199 from a Sarovan mobile, or 1800 210 4455 from any phone. Postpaid and Home Fibre support runs 24 hours; prepaid support runs 8 am to 10 pm. Complaints: call 198 from a Sarovan mobile, or use Help in the app. Every complaint gets a docket number by SMS, and billing complaints are usually resolved within 4 working days. Escalation: if your complaint is not resolved within 7 days, or you are unhappy with the resolution, you can file an appeal with the Sarovan Appellate Authority, using the appeal form in the app or at any Sarovan Experience Store. Appeals must be filed within 30 days, and you should quote your docket number. Appeals are acknowledged within 3 days and decided within 30 days. If the outcome still does not resolve your issue, you can approach a consumer forum or the telecom regulator's complaint portal.

title: Prepaid recharges and Data Bank
text: Tallowood prepaid recharges last 28 days. The $30 recharge includes 20 GB, the $40 recharge includes 45 GB and the $50 recharge includes 80 GB. All three include unlimited standard national calls and texts, and 5G access where available. Data Bank: unused data at the end of a recharge period moves into your Data Bank automatically. The bank limit is 100 GB on the $30 and $40 recharges and 200 GB on the $50 recharge. Banked data is used only after the current recharge's data runs out, oldest banked data first. Each banked amount expires 56 days after it was banked, even if you keep recharging on time. The app shows the expiry date of each banked amount. If your recharge expires before you recharge again, your entire Data Bank is cleared straight away, so turn on auto-recharge to avoid this. Extra data: a 5 GB add-on costs $10 and lasts until your recharge expires. Long-expiry option: the $300 recharge lasts 365 days and includes 300 GB, but it has no Data Bank. Prepaid credit: dollar credit added through vouchers or gift cards is used for international calls, premium numbers and add-ons, and it expires 365 days after it was added.

title: Postpaid mobile plans
text: Tallowood postpaid mobile plans are month to month, with no lock-in contract. Small costs $45 per month with 40 GB of data. Medium costs $55 per month with 100 GB. Large costs $65 per month with 180 GB, and adds unlimited standard calls to 20 international destinations. All plans include unlimited standard national calls and texts, 5G access, and Wi-Fi calling on compatible phones. Once your monthly allowance is used, there are no excess data charges; speeds are capped at 1.5 Mbps on Small and Medium and 5 Mbps on Large until your next bill period. A 10 GB data add-on costs $10. Multi-service discount: each additional postpaid mobile service on the same account gets 10% off its plan fee, for up to 5 services. Plan fees are charged monthly in advance, and usage outside your plan, such as premium texts, is billed in arrears. International roaming is switched on by default for postpaid services, and a Travel Pass starts automatically when you use your phone overseas; you can turn roaming off in the app. Changing plans: moving up applies straight away with a pro-rated charge, and moving down applies from your next bill period. Cancelling a postpaid service requires notice; see our cancellation terms.

title: Travel Pass, Zone 1 countries
text: Travel Pass for Zone 1 countries. Zone 1 covers New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Singapore, Japan, France, Germany, Italy and Spain. A Zone 1 Travel Pass costs $5 per day. Each day includes 2 GB data, unlimited standard calls to Australian numbers and to numbers in the country you're visiting, unlimited texts, and free incoming calls. For postpaid customers, roaming is on by default and the Travel Pass starts automatically the first time you make a call, send a text or use data in a Zone 1 country on a given day. Receiving a text does not start a pass, and days with no use cost nothing. A Travel Pass day runs from midnight to midnight Sydney time, not 24 hours from when it starts, so a pass that starts late in the Sydney day ends at the next midnight Sydney time. If you use more than 2 GB in a day, data slows to 256 kbps until the next Sydney midnight. Prepaid customers have roaming off by default and must buy Travel Pass days in the app before or during travel. To avoid any charges, switch off data roaming and mobile calls in your phone's settings, or turn off roaming in the app.

title: Travel Pass, Zone 2 countries
text: Travel Pass for Zone 2 countries. Zone 2 covers Indonesia (including Bali), Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, the Philippines, India, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates, South Africa, Fiji and Mexico. A Zone 2 Travel Pass costs $10 per day. Each day includes 1 GB data, unlimited standard calls to Australian numbers, unlimited texts, and free incoming calls. Calls to local numbers in the country you're visiting are not included and cost $1 per minute. For postpaid customers, roaming is on by default and the Travel Pass starts automatically the first time you make a call, send a text or use data in a Zone 2 country on a given day. Receiving a text does not start a pass, and days with no use cost nothing. A Travel Pass day runs from midnight to midnight Sydney time, not 24 hours from when it starts, so a pass that starts late in the Sydney day ends at the next midnight Sydney time. If you use more than 1 GB in a day, data slows to 256 kbps until the next Sydney midnight. Countries outside Zone 1 and Zone 2, and cruise ships, are charged pay-as-you-go at $3 per MB, with calls at $2.50 per minute. Prepaid customers must buy Travel Pass days in the app.

title: Bringing your number to Tallowood
text: Bringing your mobile number to Tallowood. You can port a number from any Australian provider. When you sign up online or in store, choose Keep my number and give us your current provider's account number for a postpaid service, or your date of birth for a prepaid service. We send a verification code to the number to confirm you hold it. Most ports complete within 3 hours if requested between 8 am and 7 pm Sydney time on a business day; requests made outside those hours are processed from 8 am the next business day. Your old service is cancelled automatically by your old provider when the port completes, so don't cancel it yourself first, or the number may be lost. Your Tallowood SIM or eSIM will show No Service until the port finishes; restart the phone once you receive our confirmation text. Unused prepaid credit with your old provider does not transfer. Porting away from Tallowood: there is no porting fee. Give your new provider your Tallowood account number, found in the app. For postpaid mobile services, our 30-day cancellation notice still applies when you port away, and phone repayments continue as normal.

title: SIM replacement and eSIM transfers
text: SIM and eSIM help. Replacement physical SIM: free at any Tallowood store, or $10 if we post it to you; posted SIMs arrive in 2 to 5 business days. eSIM: new eSIMs are activated by scanning a QR code or directly in the Tallowood app. eSIM transfers to a new phone are free in the app, up to 3 transfers per calendar month. For a fourth or later transfer in the same calendar month, visit a store with photo ID, where the transfer is also free. When you transfer, the eSIM on your old phone stops working as soon as it is activated on the new one, so keep the old phone handy until the new one shows signal. Swapping between a physical SIM and an eSIM counts as one transfer. Security checks: before any SIM swap or eSIM transfer, we send a one-time code to your account email and your current number. If you've lost your phone, a store can verify you with photo ID instead. If your phone is lost or stolen, suspend the service in the app or by calling us, and we can block the handset's IMEI so it can't be used on Australian networks.

title: ID verification for new services
text: Identity checks for new Tallowood services. Every new prepaid and postpaid service must be identity verified before it is activated. Australian residents can verify online with a driver licence, Australian passport, Medicare card or ImmiCard, and most checks are instant. Visitors and visa holders, including international students: use your foreign passport plus your visa grant number, and give an Australian residential or accommodation address. The online check takes about 10 minutes. If it fails, visit a store with your passport and we will verify you in person. Postpaid services for visa holders need at least 6 months left on the visa and a successful credit check; prepaid has no minimum visa period. You must be 16 or older to activate a prepaid service in your own name, and 18 or older for postpaid. We do not keep a copy of your documents; we record only that verification succeeded and the document type used. Each person can verify up to 5 prepaid services online; more than that needs a store visit.

title: Home internet plans
text: Tallowood home internet plans run over the national wholesale network. There is no lock-in contract and all plans include unlimited data. Home 50 costs $75 per month, with a typical evening speed 48 Mbps. Home 100 costs $90 per month, with a typical evening speed 88 Mbps. Home 250 costs $105 per month, with a typical evening speed 205 Mbps; Home 250 is available only on fibre to the premises and cable connections. Typical evening speed is the average download speed our customers get between 7 pm and 11 pm, when the network is busiest. Upload speeds are up to 20 Mbps on Home 50 and Home 100, and up to 25 Mbps on Home 250. Your actual speed can be lower because of your connection type, your in-home wiring, Wi-Fi and the devices you use. Modem: the Tallowood Wi-Fi 6 modem costs $216 upfront, or $9 per month over 24 months. If you leave before the 24 months are up, the remaining modem payments are added to your final bill. You can bring your own compatible modem instead. A 4G backup stick that keeps you online during outages is available for $5 per month.

title: Moving home and new connections
text: New connections and moving home. New connections: if your address already has an active connection point, self-installed service is usually live within 1 to 3 business days. If a technician is needed, connection takes 5 to 15 business days, depending on wholesale network appointment availability. Moving home: tell us at least 10 business days before your move date, in the app or by phone, so we can book the new connection to start on your move-in day. Relocation is free if your new address can be self-installed, and $99 if a technician appointment is needed at the new address. If the new address can't get your current plan speed, we move you to the fastest available plan at that plan's price. If home internet isn't available at the new address at all, you can cancel without the 30-day notice period. Remember to take your modem with you and reconnect it at the new address. If you give less than 10 business days' notice, we will still try to help, but there may be a gap without service; we can send a 4G backup stick free for up to 14 days while you wait.

title: Service guarantee and outage credits
text: Service guarantee and outage credits. Home internet: if a fault you report isn't fixed within 2 business days, we credit $10 per day for each extra day until it is fixed. The credit is applied automatically and shows on your next bill as Outage credit. Total credits are capped at your monthly plan fee. If we miss a technician appointment without 24 hours' notice, you also get a $25 credit. Home internet credits don't apply to faults caused by your own equipment or wiring, scheduled maintenance we told you about at least 3 days ahead, or natural disasters and widespread emergencies. Mobile: there are no automatic credits for mobile network outages, or for coverage gaps in areas outside our coverage map. If a confirmed network outage affects your area for more than 24 hours, you can request a one-off $10 credit within 30 days of the outage, in the app or by phone. Emergency calls: even during an outage or with no Tallowood coverage, your phone may still reach 000 through another network. Check the outage map in the app for current faults and estimated fix times before calling us.

title: Cancellation terms, effective 1 March 2023
text: Cancelling a Tallowood service, effective 1 March 2023. Postpaid mobile and home internet services can be cancelled at any time, with no notice period. Your final bill is pro-rated to the day you cancel, and any plan fee paid in advance for days after cancellation is credited back. Porting your mobile number to another provider cancels your Tallowood service automatically on the day the port completes. Prepaid services can be closed at any time, but unused credit and recharge value are non-refundable on closure. Phone repayments: when you cancel a postpaid service, any remaining phone repayment balance becomes due in full on your final bill. Modem repayments: any remaining modem payments are added to your final bill. To cancel, call us or use the chat in the app; for security we will confirm by text to the account holder. Cancellation requests made in store are processed within 1 business day.

title: Cancellation terms, effective 1 August 2026
text: Cancelling a Tallowood service, effective 1 August 2026. This replaces the March 2023 version. Notice period: postpaid mobile and home internet services now require 30 days' notice. When you ask to cancel, your service stays active and billing continues until the end of the 30-day notice period, followed by a final bill. The notice period also applies when you port a postpaid mobile number to another provider; the service ends when the port completes, but you are charged until the 30 days are up. No notice is needed if you move to an address where we can't provide home internet, if you are on our financial hardship program, or if you cancel within the first 30 days of a new service. Prepaid services can be closed at any time. Any unused dollar credit, not including plan inclusions or banked data, is refundable on request within 60 days of closing, paid to an Australian bank account; the minimum refund is $5. Phone repayments are not affected by cancelling: you can keep paying the phone monthly on the original schedule, or pay it out at any time. Remaining modem payments are added to your final bill. To cancel, call us or use the chat in the app.

title: Bills, payments and overdue accounts
text: Bills and payments. Postpaid bills are issued monthly and are due 14 days after the bill date. You can pay by direct debit from a bank account, credit or debit card, BPAY, or in the Tallowood app. We don't charge card payment surcharges. Late payment: Tallowood does not charge late payment fees. However, if your bill is still unpaid 14 days after the due date, we suspend outgoing calls, texts and data; incoming calls and calls to 000 keep working. If the bill remains unpaid 42 days after the due date, the service may be cancelled and the debt referred to a collection agency. Payment arrangements: if you can't pay on time, contact us before the due date to set up a payment arrangement or extension, and we won't suspend your service while you stick to it. Failed payments: if a direct debit or card payment fails, a $7.50 dishonour fee applies to cover our bank processing costs, and we retry the payment 3 days later. Paper bills cost $2.20 each; email and app bills are free. Pensioners and concession card holders can ask us to waive the dishonour fee once a year.

title: Phone repayments
text: Buying a phone on repayments. You can buy a phone from Tallowood on interest-free repayments over 12, 24 or 36 months, added to your monthly bill. Repayments are separate from your plan. If you cancel or change your plan, or port your number away, you can keep paying the phone monthly on the original schedule; the remaining balance does not become due straight away. You can also pay out the remaining balance at any time, with no fee, in the app or by phone. Upgrading early: once you have made 12 monthly repayments, you can upgrade to a new phone before your term ends by trading in your current phone in working condition, and we waive the remaining repayments. The traded-in phone must power on, hold a charge, have no cracks on the screen and have any account lock removed. If you upgrade without trading in, you keep paying off the old phone as well. Missed repayments: if two repayments in a row are missed, the remaining balance becomes due in full. Device Cover for loss, theft and accidental damage costs $12 per month and can be added only within 30 days of buying the phone.

title: Contact hours and complaints
text: Contacting Tallowood. Phone support is open weekdays 7 am to 10 pm and weekends 8 am to 6 pm, Sydney time, and closed on Christmas Day. Live chat in the Tallowood app is available 24/7. Most Tallowood stores open 9 am to 5:30 pm on weekdays with late trading to 9 pm on Thursday, 9 am to 5 pm on Saturday and 10 am to 4 pm on Sunday; check the store finder for local hours. Complaints: you can complain by phone, chat, email or in store. We acknowledge every complaint within 1 business day and give you a reference number. We aim to resolve complaints within 10 business days, and urgent complaints, such as a total loss of service or financial hardship, within 2 business days. If we need longer, we will tell you why and give you a new date, which will be no more than 20 business days from when you complained. If you're unhappy with our answer, you can ask for a review by our Complaints Review Team. You can also contact the industry ombudsman at any time; it is free and independent, though it will usually ask you to give us a chance to fix the problem first.

title: Standard plan: features, allowances and fees
text: Standard is Quaymark Money's free current account plan, with no monthly fee and no minimum term. It includes a contactless Mastercard debit card, instant spending notifications, savings pots and access to the Easy Access Saver. Spending abroad: card payments in foreign currencies are fee-free up to £1,000 per calendar month; above that, a 1% fee applies to the amount converted. Cash withdrawals: the first £250 of cash withdrawals in any rolling 30 days is fee-free, at home or abroad; after that a 2% fee applies to the amount above £250. This applies at all cash machines, including free-to-use machines in the UK, and is in addition to any fee the machine's operator charges. Daily cash withdrawal limit: £500. Card replacement: a replacement for a lost or stolen card costs £5. Replacements for damaged, faulty or expiring cards are free. Virtual cards: one virtual card for online shopping. Support: in-app chat 24 hours a day in the standard queue. Upgrading: you can move to Plus at any time in the app, and the change takes effect immediately; the Plus minimum term starts on the day you upgrade. Downgrading from Plus back to Standard is possible once the Plus minimum term has ended.

title: Plus plan: price, minimum term, allowances and fees
text: Plus is Quaymark Money's paid plan. It costs £4.99 a month, charged on the same date each month, and has a 6-month minimum term. You can cancel during the minimum term, but the remaining monthly fees up to the end of the 6 months are charged in one go when you cancel. After the first 6 months, Plus rolls monthly and can be cancelled at any time with no further charge. Spending abroad: card payments in foreign currencies are fee-free with no monthly cap. Cash withdrawals: the first £600 of cash withdrawals in any rolling 30 days is fee-free, at home or abroad; after that a 2% fee applies to the amount above £600. This applies at all cash machines and is in addition to any fee the machine's operator charges. Daily cash withdrawal limit: £800. Card replacement: one lost or stolen replacement every 12 months is free, then £5 each. Replacements for damaged, faulty or expiring cards are free. Virtual cards: up to 5 virtual cards for online shopping. Support: in-app chat 24 hours a day in a priority queue. Plus includes everything in Standard. The Easy Access Saver rate is the same on both plans.

title: Using your card abroad: exchange rates, fees and tips
text: Your Quaymark Money card works anywhere Mastercard is accepted, in over 200 countries and territories. You don't need to tell us before you travel; our fraud systems use your phone's location to recognise genuine spending abroad, so keep location services switched on for the app. Exchange rates: foreign currency payments and withdrawals are converted at the Mastercard exchange rate on the day the payment is processed, with no added markup on weekdays or weekends. Fees depend on your plan. On Standard, card payments abroad are fee-free up to £1,000 per calendar month, then a 1% fee applies. On Plus there is no monthly cap. Cash withdrawals abroad count towards the same fee-free cash allowance as UK withdrawals, £250 per rolling 30 days on Standard and £600 on Plus, with 2% charged above that. Some foreign cash machines add their own fee, which we can't refund. If a machine or shop asks whether to pay in pounds or the local currency, always choose the local currency; otherwise the merchant converts the amount at its own rate. Hotel and car hire deposits abroad show as pending holds and are released as described on the pending transactions page. If your card is declined abroad, check that the card isn't frozen, that you haven't reached your daily limit and that the merchant accepts Mastercard, then contact us in the app.

title: Lost, stolen and damaged cards: replacement fees and delivery
text: If your card is lost or stolen, report it in the app under Card, Report lost or stolen. Reporting cancels the card permanently, so it can't be reactivated even if you find it later. If you think you've simply misplaced it, freeze the card instead; freezing is temporary and you can unfreeze it at any time. Replacement fees: on Standard, a replacement for a lost or stolen card costs £5. On Plus, one lost or stolen replacement every 12 months is free, then £5 each. Replacements for damaged, faulty or expiring cards are always free. Delivery: standard delivery takes 3 to 5 working days and is free. Express delivery arrives the next working day for £12 if you order before 4 pm, Monday to Friday; orders after 4 pm or at weekends arrive on the second working day. Express delivery is available to UK addresses only, and we can't send replacement cards abroad. Replacement cards for lost or stolen cards have a new card number, expiry date and security code, so update any subscriptions and saved card details. Your PIN stays the same. While you wait, the new card's details are available in the app as soon as it's ordered, so you can add it to your phone wallet and keep paying.

title: Disputing a card payment, effective 1 June 2023
text: Disputing a card payment, effective 1 June 2023. If you have a problem with a card payment, for example goods that never arrived, a cancelled service you were still charged for, or a payment taken twice, first contact the merchant and give them 14 days to resolve it. If they don't, raise a dispute in the app by opening the transaction and choosing Something's wrong. You must raise a dispute within 120 days of the transaction date. Upload evidence such as receipts, emails and tracking information. We will review the dispute and, where appropriate, raise a chargeback with Mastercard. Temporary credits are not given while a dispute is reviewed. A final decision is usually made within 60 days, but some cases can take longer if the merchant challenges the chargeback. If the dispute succeeds, the money is credited to your account. If it fails, we'll explain why. Unauthorised payments that you didn't make yourself are handled separately as fraud and should be reported immediately; you can report these up to 13 months after the payment.

title: Disputing a card payment, effective 1 March 2026 (replaces the June 2023 version)
text: Disputing a card payment, effective 1 March 2026. This replaces the version effective 1 June 2023. If you have a problem with a card payment, such as goods that never arrived, a cancelled subscription that was still charged, or a duplicate payment, contact the merchant first. If they don't resolve it within 14 days, raise a dispute in the app by opening the transaction and choosing Something's wrong. You must raise a dispute within 30 days from the transaction date; disputes raised later are not accepted. This window is shorter than the previous 120 days, so raise disputes as soon as you notice a problem. Upload evidence such as receipts, emails and tracking details. Temporary credit: if your evidence supports the dispute, we give a temporary credit for the disputed amount within 10 working days while the chargeback is processed. A final decision is made within 45 days. If the merchant successfully defends the chargeback, the temporary credit is reversed and we'll explain why, giving you 7 days' notice before the money is taken back. If the dispute succeeds, the temporary credit becomes permanent. Unauthorised payments you didn't make yourself are handled as fraud, not disputes, and the 30-day window does not apply to them; report them immediately.

title: Bank transfers: limits, new payees and international payments
text: Bank transfers from Quaymark Money are sent by Faster Payments. Limits: a single payment can be up to £10,000, and you can send up to £25,000 per day in total. New payees: when you add a new payee, Confirmation of Payee checks the name against the receiving account. The first payment over £1,000 to a new payee is held for up to 24 hours for fraud checks before it is sent; we may contact you in the app during this time. Payments of £1,000 or less to new payees, and all payments to existing payees, are normally sent immediately and usually arrive within 2 hours. You can't cancel a payment once it has been sent. Standing orders and scheduled payments are sent on the morning of the due date. Direct Debits are collected under the Direct Debit Guarantee. International transfers: sent through our transfer partner in over 40 currencies at the mid-market rate plus a fee of 0.45%, minimum £1.50. They usually arrive within 1 to 2 working days. Receiving money: your sort code and account number are in the app under Account details. To receive international payments, use your IBAN. Incoming international payments cost £2 per payment.

title: Pending card payments, holds and refunds
text: When you pay by card, the merchant first requests an authorisation, and the amount shows as pending and is held from your available balance. The payment normally completes within 1 to 3 days when the merchant collects it. If the merchant never collects the payment, the hold is released automatically. How long holds last: most holds drop off after 7 days. Hotel, car hire and cruise holds can last up to 31 days, because these merchants are allowed to collect later. Pay-at-pump fuel payments may hold up to £99, and the difference is released once the final amount is confirmed, usually within 2 working days. We can't release a hold early ourselves, because the merchant still has the right to collect it. If a merchant confirms in writing that they've cancelled the authorisation, send it to us in the app and we will release the hold within 1 working day. Refunds: when a merchant issues a refund to your card, it usually appears within 5 working days, although some merchants take longer to send it. A refund appears as a separate credit, not as a change to the original payment. If a pending payment disappears and later reappears as completed, the merchant collected the payment after the hold expired, which is allowed.

title: Easy Access Saver and 1-Year Fixed Saver
text: Easy Access Saver: 3.10% AER variable on balances up to £250,000. Interest is calculated daily and paid monthly into the Saver. You can open it in the app with any amount from £1. Withdrawals: you can move money back to your current account instantly, but only 3 withdrawals per calendar year keep the full rate. From the 4th withdrawal in a calendar year, the rate drops to 1.00% AER for the rest of that calendar year, on the whole balance. The count resets on 1 January. Paying in has no limit. 1-Year Fixed Saver: 4.05% AER fixed, minimum deposit £500, maximum £250,000. You have 14 days after opening to add money or cancel; after that, no withdrawals or closures are possible until maturity. Interest on the Fixed Saver is paid at maturity, and the money then moves to your Easy Access Saver unless you choose another option. Savings pots inside your current account don't earn interest; they're for setting money aside. The Easy Access Saver rate is the same on Standard and Plus. We'll give you 14 days' notice before reducing the Easy Access Saver rate. Interest is paid without tax deducted; you may need to pay tax if your interest is more than your Personal Savings Allowance.

title: Overdrafts and going below zero
text: Quaymark Money does not offer unarranged overdrafts. If a payment would take your balance below zero and you don't have an arranged overdraft, we will normally decline it, and we don't charge any fee for declined payments. Occasionally a balance can still go below zero, for example when a merchant collects an offline card payment or an exchange rate moves between authorisation and settlement. In that case no fee or interest is charged, and you should add money as soon as possible. If the balance stays negative for 30 days, we may close the account. Arranged overdraft: you can apply in the app for an arranged overdraft of £50 to £2,000, subject to a credit check. The first £25 of overdraft use is interest-free. Above that, interest is charged at 29.9% EAR variable on the amount overdrawn, calculated daily and charged monthly. Representative example: if you use an overdraft of £1,200, the interest rate is 29.9% EAR variable. There are no monthly or daily overdraft fees. Applying runs a hard credit search, which shows on your credit file. You can reduce or remove your overdraft limit at any time in the app.

title: Identity checks when opening an account and reverification
text: To open a Quaymark Money account, you need to be 18 or over, live in the UK and have a UK mobile number. We verify your identity with a photo of your passport, UK driving licence or biometric residence permit, and a short selfie video that we match to the photo. Verification usually takes under 10 minutes but can take up to 2 working days if we need a manual review. Ongoing checks: we're required to keep your information up to date, so we ask some customers to reverify, for example when an ID document expires, when your details change, or as part of a routine review every 3 years. When we ask, you have 30 days from the request to complete reverification in the app. If you don't, card payments and outgoing transfers are paused until it's done; incoming payments are still accepted. If it's still not done after 60 days, we may close the account with 2 months' notice. Change of name or address: update it in the app; a change of name needs a photo of the new ID or of the marriage certificate or deed poll. We never ask you to verify your identity through an email link or a phone call; reverification only happens inside the app.

title: Reporting fraud and recognising scams
text: If you spot a payment you don't recognise, freeze your card in the app straight away and tell us through in-app chat or by calling our 24-hour fraud line on 0808 157 0436, or +44 20 7946 0436 from abroad. The fraud line is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including bank holidays. Unauthorised card payments are refunded by the end of the next working day after you report them, unless we have reasonable grounds to suspect fraud by the customer. If you were tricked into sending money to a fraudster, report it as soon as possible; you can report these scams up to 13 months after the last payment. Things we will never do: ask you to move money to a safe account, ask for your PIN or full passcode, ask you to read out a code we've sent you, or ask you to install remote access software. Anyone who does is a fraudster. Hang up and contact us using the details in the app. If you want to check whether a call really came from us, open the app: any genuine call from us shows in the app while it's happening. Card payments and transfers can be blocked for gambling, crypto exchanges or all online payments in the app's card settings.

title: Contacting us: chat, phone hours, complaints and cash
text: In-app chat is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, for all customers; Plus customers are placed in a priority queue. Phone support on 0808 157 0400 is open 8 am to 8 pm Monday to Friday and 9 am to 5 pm on Saturdays; the phone line is closed on Sundays and bank holidays, except for the 24-hour fraud line. Calls from abroad: +44 20 7946 0400, charged at your provider's international rate. We don't have branches. You can pay cash into your account at any Post Office using your card, up to £1,000 per day, with a fee of £1 per deposit. Cheques can be paid in by taking a photo in the app, up to £1,000 per cheque. Complaints: raise a complaint in the app or by phone. We send a final response within 15 business days for payment-related complaints, or within 8 weeks for other complaints. If you're unhappy with our final response, you can refer it to the Financial Ombudsman Service free of charge. Accessibility: we offer a text relay service, large-print statements and a bereavement team on 0808 157 0411.

title: Closing your account
text: You can close your Quaymark Money account in the app under Settings, Close account, or by asking in chat. Before closing, your balance must be zero or above, any arranged overdraft must be repaid, Easy Access Saver money must be moved out, and any Fixed Saver must have matured. Outstanding Plus fees for the minimum term are charged at closure. Pending card payments must settle first, so closure completes 7 days after your request; your card stops working immediately. Any remaining balance is sent to a UK account in your name within 2 working days. Direct Debits and standing orders are cancelled, so let the companies you pay know your new details. Statements are available in the app until closure, and you can request statements for up to 6 years after closing by asking in chat or by email. Accounts with no activity for 24 months are marked inactive but not closed; we'll give you 2 months' notice before closing an inactive account. If you change your mind within 14 days of opening, you can cancel and close without any charges.

title: Classic Savings Account: balance rules, interest and benefits
text: The Classic Savings Account is Saffronleaf Bank's standard savings account for individuals aged 18 and above. The minimum balance is measured as an average monthly balance (AMB), which is the sum of your end-of-day balances for each day of the month divided by the number of days in that month. The required AMB depends on the category of your home branch: ₹10,000 for metro and urban branches, ₹5,000 for semi-urban branches and ₹2,500 for rural branches. Metro and urban branches include those in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Pune and Ahmedabad. If you transfer your account to a branch in a different category, the new AMB applies from the first day of the following month. If the AMB is not maintained, a non-maintenance charge of 6% of the shortfall is levied, capped at ₹400 per month plus GST. The charge is never allowed to take your balance below zero. Interest on Classic Savings is 3.00% per annum on balances up to ₹1 lakh and 3.50% per annum on the portion above ₹1 lakh. Interest is calculated on the daily closing balance and credited once a year, on 31 March, for all Saffronleaf savings accounts. It is not credited quarterly. Every Classic account comes with a RuPay Classic debit card and one free cheque book of 25 leaves each financial year. To open the account you need your PAN card or Form 60, Aadhaar or another officially valid address proof, and a recent photograph.

title: Prime Savings Account: balance rules, interest and benefits
text: The Prime Savings Account is Saffronleaf Bank's premium savings account. Unlike the Classic account, Prime is measured on an average quarterly balance, not a monthly one. You must maintain an average quarterly balance of ₹25,000 at every branch, whatever the branch category. The average quarterly balance is the sum of your end-of-day balances for every day of the quarter divided by the number of days in the quarter. Quarters end on 30 June, 30 September, 31 December and 31 March. If the average quarterly balance is not maintained, a flat charge of ₹600 per quarter plus GST is levied. If the shortfall continues for two consecutive quarters, the account is converted to Classic Savings at the start of the next quarter, and the Classic balance rules and debit card then apply. Interest on Prime Savings is 3.25% per annum on balances up to ₹5 lakh, and balances above ₹5 lakh earn 4.00% per annum on the portion above ₹5 lakh. Interest is calculated on the daily closing balance and credited once a year, on 31 March. Prime account holders receive a Visa Platinum debit card, and its annual fee is waived for Prime Savings account holders. Other benefits: unlimited free transactions at Saffronleaf ATMs, two free cheque books of 25 leaves each financial year, free demand drafts up to ₹50,000 per day, and a 25% discount on locker rent at participating branches. The account can be opened by individuals aged 18 and above with the same documents as Classic Savings.

title: Debit card variants, limits and replacement
text: Saffronleaf Bank issues two debit cards. RuPay Classic debit card: issued free with Classic Savings, with an annual fee of ₹150 plus GST from the second year. Daily limits are ₹25,000 for ATM cash withdrawal and ₹50,000 for purchases at shops and online combined. Visa Platinum debit card: issued with Prime Savings and available to Classic customers on request. Annual fee ₹499 plus GST, charged in the card's anniversary month; the fee is waived for Prime Savings account holders. Daily limits are ₹75,000 for ATM cash withdrawal and ₹2,00,000 for purchases. Both cards are contactless, and tap payments up to ₹5,000 do not need a PIN. You can lower your daily limits in the mobile app at any time; increases above the standard limits are not possible. Lost, stolen or damaged cards: block the card first, as described on the fraud reporting page. A replacement card costs ₹200 plus GST for RuPay Classic and ₹300 plus GST for Visa Platinum. Replacement cards are produced centrally and sent by registered post to your registered address, and delivery takes up to 15 working days. We do not offer express delivery or instant cards at branches. While you wait, you can keep using UPI, net banking and cardless cash withdrawal at Saffronleaf ATMs. A new card arrives inactive; set its PIN at any Saffronleaf ATM or in the app. The card PIN is separate from your UPI PIN.

title: ATM free transactions, charges and failed withdrawals
text: Free ATM transactions each calendar month depend on your account. Classic Savings: 5 transactions at Saffronleaf ATMs, plus 3 at other banks' ATMs in the six metro centres (Mumbai, New Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad) or 5 at other banks' ATMs elsewhere. Prime Savings: unlimited at Saffronleaf ATMs and 5 at other banks' ATMs anywhere. Both cash withdrawals and balance enquiries count as transactions. Beyond the free limit, each cash withdrawal costs ₹23 plus GST and each non-financial transaction, such as a balance enquiry or mini statement, costs ₹11 plus GST. Withdrawals declined because of insufficient balance cost ₹25 plus GST. Failed ATM withdrawals: if your account is debited but no cash is dispensed, the amount is automatically reversed within 5 working days of the transaction. You don't need to raise a complaint for this to happen. If the reversal takes longer than 5 working days, Saffronleaf Bank credits compensation of ₹100 for every day of delay, without you having to ask. Keep the ATM slip or the SMS alert, and if the money hasn't come back by the sixth working day, report it in the app under Help, ATM issue, or call the helpline. Cardless cash withdrawal is available at all Saffronleaf ATMs up to ₹10,000 per day using a code generated in the app.

title: Using your debit card abroad: activation and foreign currency charges
text: International usage on all Saffronleaf debit cards is switched off by default. This covers payments at shops and ATMs outside India and online payments to merchants based abroad. You can enable it in the mobile app under Cards, Manage usage, through net banking, or at your branch. Important: for security reasons, an international usage request becomes active only 48 hours after you submit it. We cannot speed this up, including through the helpline, so please enable it at least 48 hours before you travel. When enabling, you choose the countries, or all countries, and an end date of up to 180 days; usage switches off automatically after the end date. Charges: every transaction in a foreign currency attracts a foreign currency markup of 3.5% on the RuPay Classic card and 2% on the Visa Platinum card, plus GST on the markup. The markup also applies to online payments in rupees to merchants registered abroad. ATM withdrawals abroad cost ₹150 plus GST each, in addition to the markup and any fee charged by the ATM owner. Balance enquiries abroad cost ₹25 plus GST. International daily limits are the same as your domestic limits. If a card payment abroad is declined, first check that international usage is active for that country and that the 48 hours have passed. When a terminal abroad offers to charge you in rupees, choose the local currency instead to avoid the merchant's conversion rate.

title: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 April 2024
text: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 April 2024. UPI: you can send up to ₹1,00,000 per day across up to 10 UPI transactions per day from each Saffronleaf account. A single UPI payment can be up to ₹1,00,000. For UPI payments to verified merchants for tax, hospital and education payments, the limit is ₹5,00,000 per transaction. New device or new registration: when you register UPI on a new phone, or re-register on the same phone after changing your SIM, transfers are capped at ₹5,000 for the first 24 hours. Collect requests, where someone requests money from you, are limited to ₹2,000 each. IMPS: through net banking and the mobile app, you can send up to ₹2,00,000 per day. At branches, IMPS has no upper limit but needs a signed form. Charges: UPI is free. IMPS through the app is free up to ₹1,000; above that it costs ₹5 plus GST per transfer. NEFT and RTGS through digital channels are free. Failed UPI payments where your account is debited are reversed automatically within 1 working day; if not, raise a complaint in the app under Help, UPI issue.

title: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 August 2026 (replaces the April 2024 version)
text: UPI and IMPS limits, effective 1 August 2026. This version replaces the limits effective 1 April 2024. UPI: you can send up to ₹1,00,000 per day across up to 20 UPI transactions per day from each Saffronleaf account. A single UPI payment can be up to ₹1,00,000. For UPI payments to verified merchants for tax, hospital and education payments, the limit is ₹5,00,000 per transaction. New device or new registration: when you register UPI on a new phone, or re-register on the same phone after changing your SIM, transfers are capped at ₹5,000 for the first 72 hours, after which the normal daily limit applies automatically. This cooling period cannot be lifted by the helpline or a branch. Collect requests are limited to ₹2,000 each, and collect requests from numbers not in your contacts are blocked by default. IMPS: through net banking and the mobile app, you can send up to ₹5,00,000 per day. At branches, IMPS has no upper limit but needs a signed form. Charges: UPI is free. IMPS through the app is now free for all amounts. NEFT and RTGS through digital channels remain free. What changed in this version: the daily UPI transaction count rose from 10 to 20, the new device cap now lasts 72 hours instead of 24 hours, the IMPS daily limit rose to ₹5,00,000, and IMPS charges in the app were removed. Failed UPI payments where your account is debited are reversed automatically within 1 working day.

title: Fixed deposits: rates, premature withdrawal and renewal
text: Saffronleaf Bank fixed deposits can be opened for any period from 7 days to 10 years with a minimum of ₹5,000. Current interest rates for deposits below ₹3 crore, effective 1 September 2026: 7 to 45 days 3.50%; 46 to 179 days 5.25%; 180 days to less than 1 year 6.25%; 1 year 6.80%; above 1 year up to 3 years 7.00%; above 3 years up to 10 years 6.50%. Senior citizens aged 60 and above get an extra 0.50% on all tenures, so the 1 year rate for senior citizens is 7.30%. Interest can be paid out monthly or quarterly, or reinvested and paid at maturity. Premature withdrawal: a fixed deposit closed before 180 days earns no interest at all; only the principal is returned. For deposits closed after 180 days, interest is paid at the rate applicable for the period the deposit actually ran, minus a penalty of 1%. Tax-saver deposits have a 5-year lock-in and cannot be closed early. Partial withdrawals are not allowed; you must close the whole deposit. Premature closure can be done in the app for deposits opened online, or at your branch. Auto-renewal: unless you instruct otherwise, deposits renew on maturity for the same tenure at the rate then in force. Tax is deducted at source on interest as per income tax rules; submit Form 15G or 15H at the start of each financial year if eligible. Instead of breaking a deposit, you can take a loan or overdraft of up to 90% of the deposit amount.

title: Cheque books, stop payment and Positive Pay
text: Cheque books: Classic Savings includes one free cheque book of 25 leaves each financial year and Prime Savings includes two. Additional cheque books cost ₹4 per leaf plus GST. Request one in the app, through net banking, at an ATM or at the branch; it is delivered by courier to your registered address within 7 working days. Stop payment: you can stop payment of a cheque you have issued, as long as it has not yet been paid. The charge is ₹100 per cheque, or ₹300 for a range of consecutive cheques, plus GST. Requests made through the app or net banking take effect immediately; requests at the branch take effect once processed, usually within 2 hours. A stop payment remains in force until you revoke it in writing. Positive Pay: for cheques of ₹50,000 and above, we recommend submitting the cheque details (date, payee name, amount and cheque number) in the app before handing over the cheque. For cheques of ₹5 lakh and above, Positive Pay confirmation is mandatory, and cheques without it will be returned. Cheque return charges: a cheque you issued that bounces for insufficient funds costs ₹500 plus GST per instance; a cheque you deposited that is returned unpaid costs ₹150 plus GST. Clearing: cheques deposited before 2:00 pm on a working day are usually credited the next working day.

title: Personal loans: rates, prepayment and foreclosure
text: Saffronleaf personal loans range from ₹50,000 to ₹15 lakh for tenures of 12 to 60 months, at fixed interest rates of 11.25% to 19.50% per annum depending on your credit profile. The processing fee is 2% of the loan amount, minimum ₹2,500, plus GST. EMIs are debited on the 5th of each month from your Saffronleaf account. Prepayment rules: part-prepayment is not allowed on personal loans, so you cannot pay a lump sum to reduce your EMI or tenure. You can foreclose, meaning repay the entire outstanding loan, only after 12 EMIs have been paid. A foreclosure charge of 4% of the outstanding principal plus GST applies. To foreclose, request a foreclosure statement in the app or at your branch; it is valid for 7 days, and the loan is closed once the amount is paid. A no-dues certificate is issued within 10 working days. Late payment: a bounced EMI costs ₹550 plus GST, and overdue amounts attract a penal charge of 2% per month. Home loans work differently: floating-rate home loans taken by individuals have no prepayment or foreclosure charges, and part-prepayments of any amount are accepted. Fixed-rate home loans carry a 2% prepayment charge. Applying for any loan involves a credit bureau check, and a minimum credit score of 700 is usually required for personal loans.

title: Reporting fraud, lost cards and unauthorised transactions
text: If you notice a transaction you did not make, or your card, phone or cheque book is lost or stolen, act immediately. Block your card instantly in the mobile app under Cards, Block card, or call the 24-hour fraud helpline on 1800 419 2020, toll-free within India, or +91 22 4419 2020 from abroad. You can also send an SMS saying BLOCK followed by the last 4 digits of your card to 98200 41920 from your registered mobile number. Your liability for unauthorised electronic transactions depends on how quickly you tell us: reported within 3 working days of receiving our alert, zero liability; within 4 to 7 working days, your liability is limited to ₹10,000 for savings accounts; after 7 working days, it is decided under the bank's board-approved policy. Unauthorised amounts are shadow-credited to your account within 10 working days of your report, and complaints are resolved within 90 days. Saffronleaf staff will never ask for your OTP, card PIN, CVV, UPI PIN or net banking password, whether by phone, SMS, email or social media, and we never ask you to install screen-sharing apps. If anyone does, it is a fraud attempt: hang up and report it to us. You can also report cyber fraud on the national cyber crime reporting portal.

title: Branch hours, cash counters and branch services
text: Saffronleaf branches are open Monday to Friday from 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. The cash counter closes earlier, at 3:30 pm, on weekdays; after that, branches handle only non-cash services such as account opening, KYC updates, cheque book requests and demand draft collection. On the 1st, 3rd and 5th Saturdays of the month branches are open from 9:30 am to 1:30 pm, and the cash counter on those Saturdays closes at 12:30 pm. Branches are closed on the 2nd and 4th Saturdays, on Sundays and on public holidays. Cash deposits of ₹50,000 or more in a single transaction need your PAN card or Form 60. In Classic Savings, the first 4 cash deposits at the branch each month are free; from the 5th deposit, each costs ₹50 plus GST. Cash deposit machines at 600 locations accept deposits 24 hours a day, up to ₹49,900 per transaction using your debit card. Demand drafts cost ₹50 for amounts up to ₹10,000, and ₹3 per ₹1,000 above that, with a maximum charge of ₹10,000. Coins and soiled notes are exchanged free of charge at all branches during cash counter hours. Senior citizens and persons with disabilities can request doorstep banking for cash pickup and delivery at ₹100 plus GST per visit.

title: Periodic KYC update and what happens if it is overdue
text: Every Saffronleaf customer must periodically update their KYC (Know Your Customer) records. The interval depends on your risk category: every 2 years for high-risk customers, every 8 years for medium-risk customers and every 10 years for low-risk customers. We remind you by SMS and email at least 60 days before the due date. If there is no change in your details, you can update KYC through a self-declaration in the app, through net banking, by email from your registered email address, or at any branch; no documents are needed. If your address has changed, upload the new address proof in the app or submit it at a branch; address changes are verified within 7 working days. If your identity document has expired or your name has changed, you will need to complete video KYC or visit a branch. If you miss the due date, there is a 30-day grace period, after which debits on the account are blocked. Credits such as salary and interest continue to come in, but withdrawals, transfers, card payments and UPI payments will fail. Full access is restored within 2 working days of completing the update. Accounts with KYC pending for more than 12 months may be frozen completely. Video KYC is available from 9 am to 9 pm on all days except national holidays.

title: Closing an account and inoperative accounts
text: Closing your account: accounts can be closed at your home branch or any branch in the same city by submitting a signed closure form along with unused cheque leaves and your debit card. Closure within 14 days of opening is free; closure after 14 days but within 12 months of opening costs ₹500 plus GST; closure after 12 months is free. The balance is paid by transfer to another account in your name; cash payout is limited to ₹20,000. Standing instructions, loan EMIs and investments linked to the account must be moved before closure. Inoperative accounts: if there are no customer-initiated transactions for 2 years, the account is classified as inoperative. Interest continues to be credited. The debit card, UPI and net banking stop working, and outgoing transactions are not allowed until the account is reactivated. To reactivate, submit a request with fresh KYC at any branch or through video KYC; there is no charge, and reactivation is completed within 3 working days. Balances in accounts that stay inoperative for 10 years are transferred to the regulator's depositor education fund, but you can claim the money back at any time through the bank. Minimum balance charges are not applied on inoperative accounts.

title: DriveGuard Essential comprehensive motor cover
text: DriveGuard Essential is the entry comprehensive motor policy from Liwan Crest Insurance for private cars registered in the UAE. It covers accidental damage, fire and theft of your car, plus third-party bodily injury and third-party property damage up to AED 2,000,000. Repairs are carried out at one of our approved non-agency garages, whatever the age of the car. Depreciation on parts: a flat 15% is deducted from the cost of every replaced part on every claim, from the first day of cover and regardless of the vehicle's age. The only exception is windscreen and window glass, which is replaced in full. Standard excess: AED 500 per claim. Drivers under 25 years old, or who have held a UAE driving licence for less than 1 year, pay an additional excess of AED 1,000 on top of the standard excess. Roadside assistance: up to 2 call-outs per policy year, with towing up to 30 km. Replacement car: not included. Oman cover: available as an add-on for AED 150 per year, covering own damage and third-party liability while driving in Oman. Personal accident cover for the driver: AED 200,000. Personal belongings left in the car are not covered. Natural perils such as flood and hail are covered only if you buy the natural perils add-on for AED 250 per year.

title: DriveGuard Premier comprehensive motor cover
text: DriveGuard Premier is our top comprehensive motor policy for private cars registered in the UAE. It covers accidental damage, fire and theft, natural perils such as flood and hail, and third-party bodily injury and third-party property damage up to AED 3,500,000. Agency repair: cars up to 5 years old from first registration are repaired at the manufacturer's authorised agency workshop. Older cars are repaired at an approved non-agency garage. Depreciation on parts: none for cars up to 3 years old. For older cars, 10% is deducted from the cost of replaced parts for each full year beyond the third, up to a maximum of 40%. Standard excess: AED 350 per claim. Drivers under 25 years old pay an additional excess of AED 750. Roadside assistance: unlimited call-outs, with towing up to 100 km per call-out. Replacement car: a saloon hire car for up to 10 days per claim, or a cash benefit of AED 100 per day if you prefer, while your car is in a garage after an accident covered by the policy. Oman cover: included at no extra cost. Personal accident cover for the driver and each passenger: AED 200,000. Personal belongings in the car: up to AED 3,000 per claim, excluding cash and jewellery. NCD protection can be added for 10% of the premium. Damage caused while driving off-road is excluded.

title: Motor claims procedure, effective 1 March 2024
text: This procedure applies to all motor claims for accidents on or after 1 March 2024. Report the accident to the police, or use the police smart app for minor accidents, and obtain the police report. Your car cannot be repaired under the policy without it. Notify Liwan Crest Insurance within 7 days of the accident, through the app, the claims line or by email. Upload the police report, photos of the damage, your driving licence, the vehicle registration card (mulkiya) and the Emirates ID of the driver. Survey: after notification we arrange an inspection by our surveyor within 3 working days at the Al Quoz survey centre, or at your location for an additional AED 100. Once the survey is done, we send the repair authorisation to the garage within 2 working days. Total loss: a car is treated as a total loss if the estimated repair cost is more than 50% of the insured value. We then pay the insured value less the excess. Repairs at our approved garages are guaranteed for 12 months. If the other driver was at fault, we will try to recover your excess from their insurer and refund it to you once recovered.

title: Motor claims procedure, effective 1 July 2026 (replaces the March 2024 version)
text: This procedure replaces the version effective 1 March 2024 and applies to all accidents on or after 1 July 2026. Step 1: report the accident to the police, or use the police smart app for minor accidents with no injuries, and obtain the police report. No repair can be authorised without it. Step 2: notify Liwan Crest Insurance within 24 hours of the accident, through the app, the 24-hour claims line on 800 5426 or claims@liwancrest.ae. This is a strict condition: late notification without a good reason, such as being in hospital, can lead to the claim being declined. Upload the police report, photos of the damage, the driver's licence, the vehicle registration card (mulkiya) and the driver's Emirates ID. Step 3: survey. Our surveyor inspects the car within 2 working days of notification, at the Al Quoz survey centre or, free of charge, at your home or workplace in Dubai, Sharjah or Abu Dhabi. Step 4: the repair authorisation is sent to the garage within 1 working day of the survey. Total loss: a car is treated as a total loss if the estimated repair cost is more than 60% of the insured value. We then pay the insured value less the excess, and the salvage becomes ours. Repairs at our approved garages are guaranteed for 12 months. If the other driver was at fault, we try to recover your excess from their insurer and refund it once recovered.

title: No-claims discount on motor policies
text: Liwan Crest Insurance gives a no-claims discount (NCD) on motor premiums for each consecutive claim-free year: 10% after 1 year, 15% after 2 years, 20% after 3 years and 25% after 4 or more years, which is the maximum. NCD earned with another UAE insurer is accepted if you provide a no-claims certificate or letter dated within the last 3 months. After an at-fault claim, your NCD drops back two steps at the next renewal; for example, 25% becomes 15%. A not-at-fault claim does not affect your NCD if the other party's insurer has accepted liability and the police report shows you were not at fault. Windscreen claims: unlike many insurers, we treat a windscreen or window glass replacement as an at-fault claim, so it reduces your NCD by two steps in the same way. Only a chip repair, where the glass is repaired and not replaced, has no effect on your NCD. Windscreen replacement has no excess on DriveGuard Premier and an excess of AED 250 on DriveGuard Essential. NCD protection is available on DriveGuard Premier for 10% of the premium. It allows one at-fault claim per policy year without losing NCD, but it does not cover windscreen replacement. NCD belongs to the named policyholder, not the car, and can be transferred to a new car.

title: Roadside assistance
text: Roadside assistance is included with every DriveGuard policy and is available 24 hours a day on 800 5427. Services: battery jump-start, flat tyre change using your spare, fuel delivery of up to 10 litres (you pay for the fuel), help if you are locked out, and towing to the nearest approved garage or a garage of your choice within your plan's towing distance. DriveGuard Essential includes up to 2 call-outs per policy year with towing up to 30 km. DriveGuard Premier includes unlimited call-outs with towing up to 100 km per call-out. Towing beyond the limit is charged at AED 5 per km, payable to the driver by card. Target arrival time is 60 minutes in Dubai, Sharjah and Abu Dhabi cities, and 90 minutes elsewhere in the UAE. Roadside assistance covers paved and public roads only. We do not provide off-road or desert recovery, including cars stuck in sand on unpaved tracks or dunes, even if the car is only a few metres off the road. In that case you would need a private recovery service at your own cost. Roadside assistance is not available in Oman, even where Oman cover has been added to the policy. Please stay with your vehicle, or in a safe place nearby, until help arrives.

title: HomeShield Contents cover
text: HomeShield Contents insures the belongings in your home in the UAE, for owners and tenants, with a contents sum insured from AED 50,000 to AED 500,000. It does not cover the building itself; in a rented home that is the landlord's responsibility, and in an owned flat it is usually covered by the building's own policy.
