Refunds to the original payment method, for refundable fares or cancelled flights, are processed within 10 business days; the time for the money to appear on your statement then depends on your bank. Refunds for bookings made through a travel agent are handled by that agent. Taxes on a non-refundable fare can be claimed for up to 12 months after the date of the unused flight.

title: Infants, children and Young Flyers
text: Infants are children under 2 years old. On flights scheduled to take less than 9 hours, an infant may travel on an adult's lap. Lap infants travel free on domestic flights and pay 10% of the adult fare on international flights. On flights scheduled to take 9 hours or longer, including Brisbane to Vancouver, Brisbane to Los Angeles and Brisbane to Tokyo, infants cannot travel on a lap and must have their own seat with an approved infant car seat, at 50% of the adult fare. This is because the long-haul aircraft used on these routes have no bassinet positions. On shorter international flights, bassinets can be requested for infants under 11 kg at seats in the bulkhead rows. Each adult may travel with only one lap infant. Children aged 2 to 11 pay the child fare and must have their own seat. Unaccompanied minors: children aged 5 to 11 travelling without an adult must use the Young Flyer service, which costs AUD 95 per child per flight on domestic flights and AUD 190 per child per flight on international flights. Children aged 12 to 15 may use the service on request at the same price. Children under 5 cannot travel without an adult aged 16 or older. The Young Flyer service is available on direct Coralwind Airways flights only and must be booked through the contact centre at least 48 hours before departure.

title: Special meals and assistance
text: Special meals: vegetarian, vegan, halal, kosher, gluten-free, diabetic, low-lactose and child meals can be ordered on all international flights and on domestic flights in Business. Special meals must be requested at least 36 hours before departure in Manage Booking or through the contact centre. Requests made later than 36 hours before departure cannot be met, because meals are loaded by our caterers in advance; a special meal cannot be ordered at check-in. Kosher meals need 72 hours' notice. Economy passengers on domestic flights receive a complimentary snack and drink, and the snack range always includes a vegetarian option. Wheelchair assistance: help through the airport and to your seat is free of charge and should be requested at least 48 hours before departure. Passengers bringing their own battery-powered wheelchair or mobility scooter must notify us at least 48 hours before departure; lithium batteries must not exceed 300 Wh, or two batteries of 160 Wh each. Mobility aids are carried free and do not count toward your baggage allowance. Passengers who need a portable oxygen concentrator must use an approved model and tell us at least 72 hours before departure. Assistance dogs travel free in the cabin on all flights with the required documents. Pets are carried only in the hold on domestic flights, through our approved pet transport partner, and are not accepted on international flights.

title: Delays, cancellations and disruption support
text: If your Coralwind Airways flight is delayed for reasons within our control, such as crew or engineering issues, we provide the following. For a delay of 2 hours or more, you receive a meal voucher of AUD 20 per passenger; for a delay of 4 hours or more, the voucher is AUD 40. If the delay is overnight and you are away from home, we provide hotel accommodation and transfers. Weather and air traffic control delays are outside our control and do not attract vouchers, although we will still rebook you. If we cancel your flight, or change its time by more than 2 hours, you can choose to be rebooked free of charge on the next available Coralwind Airways flight, take a travel credit, or receive a full refund to the original payment method. A refund request must be made within 28 days of the cancellation through Manage Booking or the contact centre; if no choice is made within 28 days, the booking is automatically converted into a travel credit. Disruption messages are sent by SMS and email. Passengers who prefer to travel on a different day within 7 days of a cancelled flight can move at no cost, subject to seats. Coralwind Airways does not pay fixed cash compensation for delays, but passengers may claim reasonable costs caused by a cancellation within our control by submitting receipts within 30 days.

title: Connections and minimum connection times
text: When all your flights are on one Coralwind Airways booking, your bags are checked through to your final destination and we are responsible for getting you there if a delay causes you to miss a connection. We will rebook you free of charge on the next available flight and, if you have to wait overnight, provide a hotel. Minimum connection times are the shortest connections we will sell on one booking. At Brisbane: domestic to domestic 40 minutes; international to domestic 90 minutes; domestic to international 75 minutes; international to international 60 minutes. At Sydney, international to domestic connections need 120 minutes because of the transfer between terminals. Separate bookings: if you book two flights on separate bookings, your bags are not checked through and a missed connection is normally your responsibility. Self-connect protection: if both separate bookings are on Coralwind Airways flights and you left at least 3 hours between the scheduled arrival and the next departure, we will rebook you free of charge on the next available flight if a delay to the first flight makes you miss the second. With less than 3 hours between them, standard change fees apply. Connections with partner airlines on separate bookings are never protected. When arriving from overseas into Brisbane, you must collect your bags and clear customs and biosecurity before re-checking them for a domestic flight.

title: Tidewater Rewards tiers, points and upgrades
text: Tidewater Rewards is the Coralwind Airways frequent flyer programme. Members earn points for spending and status credits for flying. Tiers are based on status credits earned in a membership year: Blue on joining, Silver at 250 status credits, Gold at 600 status credits, and Platinum at 1,200 status credits. Silver members get priority check-in and 1 lounge invitation per year. Gold members get lounge access with 1 guest when flying Coralwind Airways, priority boarding and 1 extra checked bag up to 23 kg. Platinum members get all Gold benefits plus 2 guests in the lounge and priority on waitlists. Points expiry: points expire 36 months after the end of the month in which they were earned. Flying or earning more does not extend existing points, unlike programmes where any account activity keeps the whole balance alive; the oldest points always expire first. Points upgrades: members can use points to request an upgrade to Business, but only on Economy Classic and Economy Flex fares; Economy Lite fares cannot be upgraded with points. Upgrade requests must be made at least 72 hours before departure and are confirmed or declined at the latest 24 hours before departure. If an upgrade is not confirmed, no points are deducted. An upgrade from Brisbane to Tokyo costs 30,000 points one way from Economy Flex and 40,000 points from Economy Classic.

title: Shoreline Lounge locations and access
text: Shoreline Lounges are open at the Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne domestic terminals and at Brisbane International Airport. Domestic lounges open from 4:30 am until the last Coralwind Airways departure; the Brisbane international lounge opens 3 hours before each international departure. Entry is allowed up to 3 hours before your flight and is not available on arrival. Who can enter: Business passengers on the day of travel; Tidewater Rewards Gold members with 1 guest and Platinum members with 2 guests when flying Coralwind Airways; and Silver members using a lounge invitation. Economy passengers without status can buy a lounge day pass for AUD 65 at domestic lounges or AUD 90 at the Brisbane international lounge. Day passes are sold in the app up to 1 hour before departure and at the lounge reception if there is space. Children under 2 enter free and children aged 2 to 11 pay half the day pass price. Business passengers on domestic flights may bring 1 guest only if the guest is also travelling that day. The lounges offer hot food, a bar from 11 am, showers at Brisbane international and free Wi-Fi. Dress standards apply, so no swimwear or bare feet.

title: Saver fare: what is included
text: The Saver fare is the lowest fare Saffron Kite Air publishes on every domestic route. It suits passengers who are sure of their plans and travel light. What is included: one cabin bag and one personal item within the cabin baggage limits, and 15 kg of checked baggage in a single piece. Weight above 15 kg is charged at the excess baggage rates. A free seat is assigned at random at web check-in or at the airport; choosing a specific seat in advance is chargeable at the seat selection prices. Meals are not included, but snack combos can be pre-booked for ₹249 or bought on board. Changes: a Saver booking can be changed up to 2 hours before departure on payment of the Saver change fee in the current change and cancellation policy plus any fare difference. Cancellation: a Saver booking can be cancelled up to 2 hours before departure; the Saver cancellation fee is deducted and the balance is refunded. Monsoon Club members earn 3 points per ₹100 of base fare on Saver bookings. Saver fares are not available on group bookings of 10 or more passengers, which are priced by the group desk. A Saver fare cannot be upgraded to Flexi after booking; the passenger would need to cancel and rebook.

title: Flexi fare: what is included
text: The Flexi fare is designed for passengers who may need to change their plans. It is sold on every domestic route alongside the Saver fare. What is included: one cabin bag and one personal item within the cabin baggage limits, and 20 kg of checked baggage in a single piece. Weight above 20 kg is charged at the excess baggage rates. Any standard seat can be chosen free of charge at booking, and Up Front seats and emergency exit seats are available at half the normal seat price. One hot meal or snack combo and a bottle of water are included on every flight. Changes: the first date or flight change on a Flexi booking is free if it is made at least 4 hours before departure; any fare difference is still payable. Later changes are charged at the Flexi change fee in the current change and cancellation policy. Cancellation: a Flexi booking can be cancelled up to 2 hours before departure; the reduced Flexi cancellation fee is deducted and the balance is refunded. Monsoon Club members earn 5 points per ₹100 of base fare on Flexi bookings. Flexi fares are sold to groups of up to 9 passengers on one booking. Priority check-in at Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi is included with every Flexi fare.

title: Cabin baggage allowance and dimensions
text: Every passenger, on both Saver and Flexi fares, may carry one cabin bag weighing no more than 5 kg. This is lower than the 7 kg many domestic airlines allow, so please weigh your bag before leaving home. The cabin bag must not exceed 55 cm x 35 cm x 25 cm including wheels and handles. In addition, each passenger may carry one personal item, such as a handbag, a laptop bag or a small backpack, weighing up to 2 kg and small enough to fit under the seat in front. Passengers travelling with an infant may carry one extra bag of up to 3 kg for baby food and essentials, plus a collapsible stroller that is handed over at the aircraft door. Cabin bags are checked at the bag drop counters and again at the boarding gate. A cabin bag that is over 5 kg or larger than the permitted size is tagged at the gate and carried in the hold, and the airport excess baggage rate applies to the whole weight of that bag. Passengers who need more room can buy the Cabin Plus add-on for ₹600 per flight, which raises the cabin bag limit to 8 kg; Cabin Plus is sold online until 4 hours before departure and is not sold at the airport. Duty-free purchases made at the departure airport are allowed in addition to the cabin bag.

title: Excess baggage and sports equipment
text: Checked baggage above your fare's allowance is charged as excess baggage. Prepaid excess baggage bought on the website or app up to 4 hours before departure costs: 5 kg ₹2,250, 10 kg ₹4,500, 15 kg ₹6,750. Prepaid excess baggage is non-refundable unless the flight is cancelled by Saffron Kite Air. Excess baggage not bought in advance is charged at the airport at ₹600 per kg, payable at the check-in counter by card or UPI. No single checked piece may weigh more than 32 kg, and a passenger may check in a maximum of 3 pieces. Sports equipment: golf bags, boxed bicycles, cricket kits, surfboards up to 2.5 m and diving equipment are carried for a flat ₹1,800 per item per flight in addition to the normal allowance, provided the item weighs no more than 20 kg. Sports equipment must be pre-booked through the contact centre at least 24 hours before departure, as hold space is limited on our aircraft. Bicycles must have the pedals removed and the handlebars turned sideways. Musical instruments larger than the cabin bag size must either be checked in as a sports item at the same rate or travel in a seat bought at the full fare for the instrument. Excess baggage on connecting flights is charged separately for each flight.

title: Airport check-in and boarding times
text: Check-in counters at all airports open 3 hours before departure. For every Saffron Kite Air domestic flight, check-in counters close 75 minutes before the scheduled departure time. This closing time also applies to the bag drop counters used by passengers who have checked in online, and it is earlier than at many other domestic airlines, so plan to reach the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Passengers who reach the counter after it closes cannot be accepted on the flight and are treated as no-shows. Boarding gates open 60 minutes before departure and close 25 minutes before departure. Once the gate has closed, no passenger can board, even if the aircraft is still at the stand. Passengers must carry a valid original photo ID, such as an Aadhaar card, passport, voter ID card or driving licence, and the name must match the booking. Digital ID through the DigiYatra app is accepted at airports where it is available. Airport check-in is free of charge. Passengers with infants, unaccompanied minors, pets, sports equipment or special assistance requests must check in at the counter, not online. At Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi, priority check-in counters are available to Flexi passengers and Monsoon Club Silver and Gold members.

title: Web check-in
text: Web check-in opens 72 hours before departure and closes 60 minutes before departure on the website and app. Passengers who check in online can download their boarding pass, receive it by email or WhatsApp, or save it to their phone wallet; a printed copy is not needed at any airport we serve. Passengers with cabin bags only can go straight to security with their mobile boarding pass. Passengers with checked bags must drop them at the bag drop counter before it closes 75 minutes before departure, even though web check-in itself stays open until 60 minutes before departure. Seats: if you have not bought a seat, a free seat is assigned at random when you check in online. We try to seat passengers on the same booking together but cannot guarantee it, except that children under 12 are always seated next to at least one adult on the same booking at no charge. Web check-in is not available for passengers travelling with an infant, unaccompanied minors, passengers with pets or sports equipment, or passengers who have asked for wheelchair assistance; they must check in at the airport counter. Self-service kiosks at Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi airports can print boarding passes and bag tags. If web check-in shows an error, the contact centre can check you in by phone up to 3 hours before departure.

title: Seat selection prices
text: Choosing a seat in advance is optional. Saver passengers who do not buy a seat receive a free seat assigned at random at check-in. Seat prices per passenger per flight are: middle seats ₹150; standard aisle or window seats ₹350; Up Front seats in rows 1 to 3 ₹900, which include priority boarding; emergency exit seats in rows 12 and 13 ₹1,100, which have extra legroom. Flexi passengers can choose any standard seat free of charge and pay half the price for Up Front and emergency exit seats. Monsoon Club Gold members get a free standard seat on every booking. Emergency exit seats can only be sold to passengers aged 18 or above who are able and willing to assist in an evacuation, are not travelling with an infant or a child, and do not need special assistance; staff may move a passenger who does not meet these conditions, and the seat fee is then refunded. Seat fees are non-refundable if you cancel your booking or do not travel. If Saffron Kite Air changes your aircraft or cancels your flight and you lose the seat you paid for, the seat fee is refunded to the original payment method. Seats can be bought until 2 hours before departure online or at the airport counter.

title: Change and cancellation policy (effective 1 June 2024)
text: This policy applies to bookings changed or cancelled on or after 1 June 2024. Saver fares: change fee ₹2,250 per passenger per flight if the change is made more than 72 hours before departure, and ₹2,750 if made between 72 hours and 2 hours before departure. Cancellation fee ₹3,000 per passenger per flight if cancelled more than 72 hours before departure, and ₹3,500 if cancelled between 72 hours and 2 hours before departure. Flexi fares: the first change is free if made at least 4 hours before departure; later changes cost ₹1,250 each. Cancellation fee ₹1,500 per passenger per flight at any time up to 2 hours before departure. All fares: any fare difference is payable on a change. No changes or cancellations are possible within 2 hours of departure; a passenger who does not travel is treated as a no-show. The cancellation fee will never exceed the base fare plus fuel charge, and statutory taxes are always refunded. Look-in option: a booking can be changed or cancelled without any change or cancellation fee within 48 hours of booking, provided the domestic flight departs at least 7 days after the booking date; any fare difference on a change is still payable. Convenience fees of ₹350 per passenger per flight are not refunded.

title: Change and cancellation policy (effective 1 August 2026)
text: This policy applies to bookings changed or cancelled on or after 1 August 2026 and replaces the policy effective 1 June 2024. Saver fares: change fee ₹2,500 per passenger per flight if the change is made more than 72 hours before departure, and ₹3,000 if made between 72 hours and 2 hours before departure. Cancellation fee ₹3,500 per passenger per flight if cancelled more than 72 hours before departure, and ₹4,000 if cancelled between 72 hours and 2 hours before departure. Flexi fares: the first change is free if made at least 4 hours before departure; later changes cost ₹1,500 each. Cancellation fee ₹1,000 per passenger per flight if cancelled more than 72 hours before departure, and ₹1,500 if cancelled between 72 hours and 2 hours before departure. All fares: any fare difference is payable on a change. No changes or cancellations are possible within 2 hours of departure; a passenger who does not travel is treated as a no-show under the delays and no-show rules. The cancellation fee will never exceed the base fare plus fuel charge, and statutory taxes are always refunded. Look-in option, unchanged from the previous policy: a booking can be changed or cancelled without any change or cancellation fee within 48 hours of booking, provided the domestic flight departs at least 7 days after the booking date. Convenience fees of ₹350 per passenger per flight are not refunded. Refund timelines are set out in the refunds policy.

title: Refund timelines and credit shell
text: When a booking is cancelled, the refundable amount can be returned in one of two ways. Refund to the original payment method: refunds to credit cards, debit cards, UPI and net banking are processed within 21 working days of the cancellation. This is longer than the 5 to 7 working days that many airlines quote, because Saffron Kite Air settles refunds in a weekly batch with its payment partners; please wait the full 21 working days before raising a complaint. Once a refund has been processed, the bank reference number is shown in Manage Booking and sent by email. Credit shell: instead of a refund to your card, you can choose to keep the amount as a credit shell, which is available immediately and can be used for any new Saffron Kite Air booking in the same passenger's name within 12 months of the cancellation date. Credit shell balances cannot be converted back into a card refund. Bookings made through a travel agent or a travel website are refunded through that agent, who sets its own timeline. Bookings paid in cash at an airport counter are refunded by bank transfer to an account in the passenger's name, within the same 21 working days, after the passenger shares bank details through the contact centre. If Saffron Kite Air cancels your flight, you receive a full refund including the convenience fee, on the same timeline. Refund status can be tracked under Manage Booking.

title: Name corrections and partial cancellations
text: Name corrections: Saffron Kite Air does not allow any change or correction to a passenger's name once a booking is confirmed. This includes spelling mistakes, swapped first and last names, missing middle names or surnames, and changes of title. The name on the booking must match the passenger's photo ID at the airport, so please check names carefully before paying. If a name is wrong, the booking must be cancelled under the change and cancellation policy and a new booking made in the correct name; within the 48-hour look-in window this can be done without a cancellation fee. Tickets cannot be transferred to another person under any circumstances. Partial cancellations: if one or more passengers on a booking with several passengers want to cancel while the others keep travelling, the booking must first be split. Partial cancellations can only be done through the contact centre, not in Manage Booking, and carry a split fee of ₹500 per booking in addition to the cancellation fee for each cancelled passenger. The contact centre is open from 6 am to 11 pm every day; the number is listed in the app and on every booking confirmation. Other edits: contact details, meal choices and Monsoon Club numbers can be updated free of charge in Manage Booking until 2 hours before departure. Group bookings of 10 or more passengers are handled only by the group desk.

title: Infants, children and unaccompanied minors
text: Infants: babies from 7 days old up to their second birthday travel on an adult's lap. The infant fee is ₹1,750 per infant per flight, and each adult may travel with only one infant. Infants must be added at the time of booking or through the contact centre at least 6 hours before departure, and proof of age such as a birth certificate must be shown at check-in. An infant who turns 2 during the trip needs a seat of their own for the remaining flights. Children aged 2 to 11 pay the adult fare and must have their own seat. Unaccompanied minors: the unaccompanied minor service is only available for children aged 8 to 14. Children under 8 cannot travel without an accompanying passenger aged 18 or above, even with the service; this differs from many airlines that accept children travelling alone from 5 years. Young passengers aged 15 to 17 may travel alone without the service. The service costs ₹5,000 per child per flight, is available on direct flights only, and is not offered on flights scheduled to depart after 8 pm. It must be booked through the contact centre at least 48 hours before departure. The parent or guardian must stay at the departure airport until the flight has taken off, and the person collecting the child must show the photo ID named on the handover form.

title: Travelling with pets and special assistance
text: Pets in the cabin: small dogs and cats are accepted in the cabin on flights with a scheduled duration of under 2 hours. The combined weight of the pet and its carrier must not exceed 7 kg, and the soft-sided carrier must fit under the seat in front. The charge is ₹3,500 per pet per flight. A maximum of 2 pets are carried on each flight, so pets must be booked through the contact centre at least 48 hours before departure. Pets must be at least 8 weeks old and have a vaccination certificate. Pets are not carried in the hold on any flight. Trained service dogs accompanying passengers with disabilities travel free in the cabin on all flights. Special assistance: wheelchair assistance from check-in to the aircraft seat, and from the aircraft to the arrivals hall, is free of charge. Please request it at least 48 hours before departure in Manage Booking or through the contact centre; later requests are met where staff are available. Passengers travelling with their own battery-powered wheelchair must tell us at least 72 hours before departure and give the battery type and watt-hour rating. Passengers who need medical oxygen or a stretcher, or who have had a recent illness or surgery, must submit a medical clearance form signed by a doctor at least 72 hours before departure. Visually and hearing impaired passengers can ask for a staff escort at the airport at no cost.

title: Delays, missed flights and no-show rules
text: Delays: if your flight is delayed by more than 2 hours beyond its scheduled departure time, you receive a meal voucher worth ₹300 per passenger, to be used at the airport food outlets listed on the voucher. If the delay is more than 6 hours, you may choose a free change to another Saffron Kite Air flight within 7 days or a full refund. If the delay is caused by Saffron Kite Air and pushes the departure past midnight, hotel accommodation is provided to passengers who are not residents of the departure city. Delay information is sent by SMS and WhatsApp to the mobile number on the booking. No-show: a passenger who does not check in before the counter closes, or who checks in but does not board before the gate closes, is a no-show. The base fare and fuel charge are forfeited; statutory taxes and the user development fee are refunded to the original payment method if requested within 90 days. Go-Show: a passenger who has missed their flight can report to the Saffron Kite Air transfer desk at the airport within 2 hours of the scheduled departure time and move to the next flight to the same destination on the same day for a flat ₹2,000 per passenger, subject to seats being available. If there is no later flight to that destination on the same day, Go-Show is not available and the no-show rules apply. The checked baggage allowance on the new flight stays the same.

title: Monsoon Club tiers and lounge access
text: Monsoon Club is Saffron Kite Air's frequent flyer programme and is free to join. Members earn 3 points per ₹100 of base fare on Saver bookings and 5 points per ₹100 on Flexi bookings; 100 points can be redeemed for ₹100 off a future booking. Points expire 24 months after they are earned. Tiers are based on flights taken in a calendar year: Blue on joining, Silver after 10 flights, and Gold after 25 flights. Silver members get priority check-in and 5 kg of extra checked baggage on every flight. Gold members get 10 kg of extra checked baggage, priority check-in and priority boarding, a free standard seat on every booking, and 4 free lounge visits per calendar year. Tier status lasts until the end of the following calendar year. Lounges: Saffron Kite Air does not run its own lounges, but passengers can use partner lounges at the domestic terminals in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi. A lounge pass costs ₹1,499 per visit when pre-booked on the website or app at least 6 hours before departure, and allows a stay of up to 3 hours before your flight. Lounge passes cannot be bought at the lounge door. Gold members use their free visits by showing their membership card and boarding pass at the lounge reception. Children under 2 enter free with a paying adult.

title: OPD timings and consultation fees, Baner branch (Pune)
text: This page covers the outpatient department (OPD) at the Varunika Hospitals Baner branch in Pune. OPD timings: Monday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 8:00 pm. On Sundays only the general medicine and paediatrics OPDs run, from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm. The OPD is closed on 26 January, 15 August and on Lakshmi Puja day during Diwali; the Emergency department stays open. Consultation fees at Baner: general medicine and paediatrics ₹700; specialist consultations (orthopaedics, gynaecology, ENT, dermatology, ophthalmology, general surgery, psychiatry) ₹1,000; super-specialist consultations (cardiology, neurology, nephrology, gastroenterology, medical oncology) ₹1,500. A one-time registration fee of ₹150 is charged on the first visit and creates your hospital ID card, which is valid at both branches. Senior citizens aged 65 and above get 10% off the consultation fee on showing age proof; the discount does not apply to video consultations or health check packages. Walk-ins at Baner: walk-in tokens are issued only for general medicine and paediatrics, from the OPD reception, until 6:30 pm. Specialist and super-specialist consultations at Baner are by prior appointment only, booked through the call centre, the app or WhatsApp. A walk-in patient who asks for a specialist is offered the next available appointment slot, which may be on a later day. Patients with chest pain, breathlessness, a fresh injury or heavy bleeding should go straight to the Emergency department on the ground floor, which needs no appointment. Payment at the OPD billing counter is by cash, UPI, debit card or credit card.

title: OPD timings and consultation fees, Gangapur Road branch (Nashik)
text: This page covers the outpatient department (OPD) at the Varunika Hospitals Gangapur Road branch in Nashik. OPD timings: Monday to Saturday, 9:30 am to 7:00 pm. There is no Sunday OPD at Nashik; on Sundays and on 26 January, 15 August and Lakshmi Puja day only the Emergency department is open. Consultation fees at Nashik: general medicine and paediatrics ₹600; specialist consultations (orthopaedics, gynaecology, ENT, dermatology, ophthalmology, general surgery) ₹900; super-specialist consultations (cardiology, neurology, nephrology) ₹1,300. Gastroenterology and medical oncology are not offered at Nashik; patients are referred to the Baner branch in Pune. Psychiatry at Nashik is available only as a video consultation. A one-time registration fee of ₹100 is charged on the first visit at Nashik; patients already registered at Baner do not pay it again. Senior citizens aged 65 and above get 10% off the consultation fee on showing age proof. Walk-ins at Nashik: walk-in tokens are issued for all OPD specialities until 5:00 pm, subject to the doctor's availability that day. Patients with an appointment are seen first and walk-in tokens are called in between, so the wait for walk-ins can be one to two hours on Mondays. Patients with chest pain, breathlessness, a fresh injury or heavy bleeding should go straight to the Emergency department, which is open 24 hours and needs no appointment. Payment at the OPD billing counter is by cash, UPI, debit card or credit card.

title: Appointments, cancellations and free follow-up visits
text: These rules apply to OPD appointments at both Varunika Hospitals branches (Baner, Pune and Gangapur Road, Nashik). Booking: appointments can be booked through the call centre on 020 4719 2200 (7:00 am to 10:00 pm, all days), through the Varunika app, or on WhatsApp. Appointments can be booked up to 14 days ahead. App and WhatsApp bookings are prepaid; call-centre bookings can be paid at the OPD counter on the day. Please arrive 20 minutes before your slot for registration and vitals. Late arrival: if you arrive more than 15 minutes after your slot, you are moved to the end of that doctor's queue for the day. Cancellation and refunds: you can cancel or reschedule free of charge up to 24 hours before your slot, and a prepaid fee is refunded in full to the original payment mode within 5 working days. If you cancel within 24 hours of the slot, a cancellation fee of ₹200 is deducted from the refund. If you do not turn up and do not cancel, the full consultation fee is forfeited. Each appointment can be rescheduled free of charge once, if done more than 24 hours before the slot. Free follow-up: a follow-up visit is free only within 5 days of the paid consultation, counting the day after the consultation as day 1. The free follow-up must be with the same doctor at the same branch and covers one visit only. From day 6 onwards, the full consultation fee applies. Video consultations do not carry a free follow-up. Follow-up visits still need an appointment; please mention that it is a follow-up when booking so the fee is waived.

title: Video consultations (teleconsultation)
text: Varunika Hospitals offers video consultations through the Varunika app for patients anywhere in India. Slots run every day from 8:00 am to 10:00 pm. Fees: general medicine and paediatrics ₹500; specialist video consultations (dermatology, gynaecology, ENT, psychiatry, orthopaedics follow-ups) ₹800. Super-specialist doctors (cardiology, neurology, nephrology, gastroenterology, oncology) take video consultations only for their existing patients, at ₹1,000. The fee is paid in the app at the time of booking, and the senior citizen discount does not apply. How it works: upload any previous reports and prescriptions in the app before the call. You will get a video link 10 minutes before your slot. If the doctor has not joined within 15 minutes of the slot time, you can choose a full refund, credited within 3 working days, or a free rebooking. If you miss the call yourself, the fee is not refunded. After the call, the e-prescription appears in the app within 2 hours. Doctors cannot prescribe narcotic or psychotropic medicines by video, and fitness certificates and sick-leave certificates are not issued on video consultations; these need an in-person visit. Video consultations are not for emergencies. For chest pain, breathlessness, fits, heavy bleeding or a serious injury, go to the nearest emergency department or call our 24-hour emergency line on 020 4719 2299. You will need a phone or laptop with a camera, a stable internet connection, and a quiet, well-lit place. Video consultations do not include a free follow-up.

title: Essential Health Check package
text: The Essential Health Check is the basic preventive health check at Varunika Hospitals, available at both the Baner (Pune) and Gangapur Road (Nashik) branches. Price: ₹2,499 per person. What is included: complete blood count (CBC), fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, lipid profile, liver function test, kidney function test (creatinine, urea, uric acid), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), urine routine, chest X-ray, resting ECG, and a consultation with a physician. Not included: treadmill test (TMT), 2D echo, vitamin D, vitamin B12 and ultrasound, which are part of the Executive Health Check. Timings: reporting time is 7:30 am to 10:30 am, Monday to Saturday, by prior booking only. You must come after a 12-hour fast; plain water is allowed. The visit takes about 3 hours. Reports: the full report is uploaded to the Varunika app within 48 hours of the visit, and a printed file can be collected from the health check desk after that. The physician consultation is done on a separate visit, after the reports are ready, and must be used within 15 days of the check. Booking: book through the call centre or the app at least one day in advance. Cancellation up to 24 hours before the slot is free; after that, ₹300 is deducted. Add-ons can be booked at the counter on the day: vitamin D ₹900, vitamin B12 ₹700, ultrasound abdomen ₹1,400. Women can add a Pap smear for ₹800. The senior citizen discount does not apply to health check packages.

title: Executive Health Check package
text: The Executive Health Check is the comprehensive preventive health check at Varunika Hospitals, available only at the Baner branch in Pune. Price: ₹5,999 per person, or ₹10,999 for two people booked together for the same day. What is included: everything in the Essential Health Check (CBC, fasting blood sugar, HbA1c, lipid profile, liver and kidney function tests, TSH, urine routine, chest X-ray, resting ECG) plus a treadmill test (TMT), 2D echo, vitamin D, vitamin B12, ultrasound abdomen, pulmonary function test, an eye check and a dental check. Consultations: on the same day, with a physician, a cardiologist and a dietitian. Timings: reporting time is 7:30 am to 9:30 am, Monday to Saturday, by prior booking only, at least two days in advance. You must come after a 12-hour fast; plain water is allowed. Breakfast is served after the fasting samples are taken. Wear comfortable shoes for the treadmill test. The visit takes about 5 hours. Reports: same-day reports are handed over at the final physician consultation, usually by 5:00 pm. Reports that need more time, such as any add-on culture tests, are uploaded to the app later. Cancellation up to 48 hours before the slot is free; after that, ₹500 is deducted. People with a known heart condition should tell the call centre when booking, as the cardiologist may replace the treadmill test with another test. The senior citizen discount does not apply.

title: Lab sample collection and report turnaround times
text: The Varunika Hospitals laboratory serves both branches. Sample collection hours at the collection centres in Baner and Nashik: Monday to Saturday 7:00 am to 9:00 pm, and Sunday 7:00 am to 12:00 pm. Fasting samples are collected only until 11:00 am. Report turnaround times, counted from sample collection: complete blood count and blood sugar within 4 hours; lipid profile, liver function and kidney function tests the same day by 7:00 pm if the sample is given before 11:00 am, otherwise the next day; HbA1c and thyroid tests the next day by 12:00 pm; vitamin D and vitamin B12 within 48 hours; urine and blood culture reports within 72 hours, with a final report up to 5 days if the culture grows bacteria; biopsy (histopathology) reports in 7 working days. Reports are sent as an SMS link and appear in the Varunika app. One printed copy is free at the report counter, open 8:00 am to 8:00 pm; each reprint costs ₹50. Home sample collection is available within Pune and Nashik city limits, from 6:30 am to 11:00 am, all days. The home collection charge is ₹250 per visit, waived when the test bill is ₹2,000 or more. Home collection must be booked by 8:00 pm the day before through the call centre or the app. The phlebotomist carries an ID card and collects payment by UPI or card at the time of collection. Reports for home collection samples follow the same turnaround times.

title: Test preparation and fasting instructions
text: Please read these instructions before coming for a blood test at Varunika Hospitals. Fasting tests: for fasting blood sugar, lipid profile and all health check packages, Varunika Hospitals requires a strict 12-hour fast before the sample is taken. This applies to every fasting test at our labs, even where other labs ask for 8 hours. If you have fasted for less than 12 hours, the lab will still take the sample but will report the sugar as a random sugar, not a fasting sugar, and you may be asked to come again. Do not fast for more than 14 hours. During the fast you may drink plain water. Do not have tea, coffee, milk, juice, chewing gum, tobacco or pan masala. Medicines: take your usual blood pressure and thyroid medicines with water unless your doctor has told you otherwise. Do not take diabetes tablets or insulin until after the fasting sample; bring them with you. Post-prandial (PP) sugar: the PP sample is taken exactly 2 hours after you start your meal. Tell the collection staff the time you started eating. Do not eat again or have tea during those 2 hours. Urine tests: give the first urine of the morning, midstream, in the sterile container provided by the lab. Ultrasound: ultrasound abdomen needs a 6-hour fast; a pelvic ultrasound needs a full bladder, so drink four to five glasses of water one hour before and do not pass urine. Please bring your doctor's prescription, a photo ID and your previous reports to every test visit.

title: Visiting hours, visitor passes and parking
text: Visiting hours at both Varunika Hospitals branches, all days: general wards and private rooms 11:00 am to 12:00 pm and 5:00 pm to 7:00 pm. ICU, NICU and HDU: 4:00 pm to 4:30 pm only, one visitor at a time, immediate family only. Passes: every admitted patient is given one attendant pass, which allows one person to stay with the patient round the clock, and two visitor passes, which are valid only during visiting hours. Passes must be shown at the lift lobby security desk. A lost attendant pass is replaced at the admissions desk for ₹100. Children: children under 12 are not allowed into wards, private rooms or ICUs at any time, including the maternity ward. Children under 12 can meet a patient only in the family lounge on the ground floor, between 5:00 pm and 6:00 pm, and only if the treating team allows the patient to come down. Infection control: all visitors must use the hand sanitiser at the ward entrance. Flowers and outside food are not allowed in ICUs. Visitors with fever, cough or cold are asked not to visit. Parking at Baner: basement parking for cars is ₹40 for the first 3 hours and ₹20 for every additional hour; two-wheelers pay ₹20 per day. Attendants of admitted patients can buy a car parking pass for ₹150 per day at the admissions desk. Parking at Nashik: open parking inside the campus, free for patients and visitors, subject to space; the gate closes at 11:00 pm.

title: Insurance and TPA cashless desk
text: The insurance and TPA desk handles cashless hospitalisation for patients with health insurance. It is on the ground floor next to Admissions at both Varunika Hospitals branches. Desk hours: Monday to Saturday 8:00 am to 8:00 pm, and Sunday 9:00 am to 2:00 pm. The desk is closed on Sunday afternoons and evenings; emergency admissions at those times are registered by the Admissions desk and the cashless request is sent the next morning. The hospital is empanelled with most major health insurers and TPAs; the current list is displayed at the desk and in the app. Planned admissions: the pre-authorisation request must be submitted at least 72 hours before the planned admission date. Bring the policy card or e-card, a photo ID of the patient, the treating doctor's admission advice with the cost estimate, and previous reports. Emergency admissions: the pre-authorisation request must be submitted within 24 hours of admission. Deposit on cashless: even when a cashless request has been sent, a refundable deposit of ₹10,000 is collected at admission. It is adjusted against non-payable items such as registration, consumables, attendant food and toiletries, and any co-payment or room-rent difference under your policy, which the patient pays at discharge. If the insurer rejects or partly approves the request, the balance must be paid as a self-paying patient. At discharge, the desk sends the final bill to the insurer; final approval usually arrives within 3 hours, and the patient can leave once it is received and the non-payable amount is paid. For reimbursement claims, the desk gives you the original bills and discharge summary.

title: Admission deposits and refunds
text: Self-paying patients pay an advance deposit at the time of admission at either Varunika Hospitals branch. Deposit by room category: general ward ₹20,000; twin sharing room ₹35,000; single room ₹50,000; deluxe room ₹75,000; ICU ₹1,00,000. For planned surgery the deposit is the room deposit or 50% of the surgery estimate, whichever is higher. If the running bill goes above the deposit, the billing team will ask for an interim deposit. Payment modes: UPI, debit card, credit card, NEFT or RTGS, demand draft, and cash up to ₹1,99,999 per admission. Documents: a photo ID of the patient (Aadhaar card, PAN card, passport, voter ID or driving licence) and a photo ID of the relative who signs the admission consent form. For a patient who arrives unconscious, the ID can be submitted within 24 hours. Refund of excess deposit: if the final bill is lower than the deposit, the excess is not paid back in cash at the discharge counter. It is refunded only by bank transfer to the patient's bank account, or to the original card for card payments, within 10 working days of the final bill being settled. Please fill in the refund form and attach a cancelled cheque at the billing counter on the day of discharge; delays in giving bank details will delay the refund. Cashless patients pay a separate refundable deposit, explained in the insurance and TPA desk document.

title: Discharge process
text: Discharge at Varunika Hospitals usually works as follows. The treating doctor decides on discharge during the morning round, and the ward nurse informs the family by 11:00 am. The billing team then prepares the final bill; for self-paying patients this takes about 2 to 3 hours, and for cashless patients it also depends on the insurer's final approval. Room vacating time: the room must be vacated by 2:00 pm on the day of discharge. If the patient leaves the room after 2:00 pm, half a day's room rent is added to the final bill; after 8:00 pm, a full day's room rent is added. The same rule applies to ICU beds. What you receive: two copies of the discharge summary, signed by the treating doctor, along with the final bill, the receipts, all original reports and films, and the take-home medicines from the in-house pharmacy. Please check the medicine list with the nurse before you leave. Unopened take-home medicines can be returned to the pharmacy within 7 days with the bill. Follow-up: the discharge summary gives the date for the follow-up visit, which must be booked through the call centre. Leaving against medical advice: if the family decides to take the patient home before the doctor advises discharge, a relative must sign a discharge against medical advice (DAMA) form. Wheelchairs and help to the car park are available from the ward on request. Discharges are not processed between 10:00 pm and 7:00 am except for a medical emergency transfer.

title: Medical records requests (effective 1 June 2023)
text: This page describes how patients can get copies of their medical records from Varunika Hospitals. Effective 1 June 2023. Requests are made at the Medical Records Department (MRD) at either branch, Monday to Friday, 10:00 am to 5:00 pm, using the records request form. Copies of a complete inpatient case file are ready within 7 working days of the request. The fee is ₹300 per inpatient file, whatever the number of pages. Copies of outpatient prescriptions and lab reports can be downloaded free from the Varunika app. Who can apply: the patient; or another person carrying an authorisation letter signed by the patient, with photo ID copies of both the patient and the person collecting. For a minor, a parent or legal guardian can apply. For a deceased patient, the legal heir can apply with the death certificate and proof of relationship. Courier delivery anywhere in India is available for ₹100 extra. Copies are certified by the MRD officer on each page. Original files are never handed over; they remain with the hospital and are stored for the period required by law. Requests from police, courts and insurers are handled separately by the medico-legal cell. A discharge summary copy is always given free to the patient at the time of discharge, and a duplicate discharge summary costs ₹100 at the MRD.

title: Medical records requests (effective 1 August 2026), replaces the June 2023 version
text: Effective 1 August 2026, this replaces the medical records policy of 1 June 2023. Requests are made at the Medical Records Department (MRD) at either Varunika Hospitals branch, Monday to Saturday, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, using the records request form, or by email to the MRD with a signed scanned form. Timeline: certified copies of an inpatient case file are released only after 15 working days from the date of the written request. Every file is audited and certified page by page by the MRD before release, and requests cannot be fast-tracked, including for insurance claims; for insurance, the free discharge summary and final bill are normally enough to start a claim. Fee: ₹500 per inpatient file of up to 50 pages, and ₹5 for every page beyond 50. Courier delivery anywhere in India is ₹100 extra. Outpatient prescriptions and lab reports remain free to download from the Varunika app. Who can apply: the patient; or another person carrying an authorisation letter signed by the patient, with photo ID copies of both the patient and the person collecting. The letter must name the person collecting and the admission dates of the file requested. For a minor, a parent or legal guardian can apply. For a deceased patient, the legal heir can apply with the death certificate and proof of relationship. Original files are never handed over. A discharge summary copy is given free at the time of discharge; a duplicate discharge summary costs ₹100 at the MRD.

title: Emergency department, pharmacy and vaccination clinic
text: Emergency: the Emergency departments at both Varunika Hospitals branches are open 24 hours, all days, and do not need an appointment. Patients are seen in order of medical urgency, not arrival time. The emergency consultation fee is ₹1,200 at Baner and ₹1,000 at Nashik, and tests and treatment are billed separately. For non-urgent problems such as a mild fever, a routine prescription refill or a check-up, please use the OPD instead, which is quicker and costs less. Ambulance: call 020 4719 2299. Pharmacy: the pharmacy at Baner is open 24 hours. The pharmacy at Nashik is open 8:00 am to 11:00 pm; at night, medicines for Emergency patients are issued from the emergency stock. Both pharmacies fill outside prescriptions and give a 10% discount on bills above ₹1,000, except on surgical items and baby food. Vaccination clinic: children's vaccinations at Baner are given on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, 10:00 am to 1:00 pm; at Nashik on Wednesday and Saturday, 9:30 am to 12:30 pm. No appointment is needed for children's vaccinations, but please bring the child's vaccination card. Adult vaccines (influenza, hepatitis B, HPV, typhoid, pneumococcal) are given by appointment at both branches on weekdays. Vaccines are charged at their printed price plus a ₹150 administration charge per visit. The vaccination clinic is closed on public holidays. Travel vaccines such as yellow fever are not available at either branch.

title: Private GP appointments: fees and booking
text: Wrenfield Clinics offers private GP appointments at our Leeds (Park Square) and York (Micklegate) clinics. A standard GP appointment lasts 15 minutes and costs £79. An extended GP appointment lasts 30 minutes and costs £139, and is recommended for more than one problem, complex medication questions or a full review. A practice nurse appointment lasts 20 minutes and costs £45 (dressings, injections, blood pressure checks and ear irrigation). Booking: appointments can be booked online, in the Wrenfield app, or by phone on 0113 496 0412 (Monday to Friday 7:30 am to 8:00 pm, Saturday 8:30 am to 1:00 pm). Appointments can be booked up to 4 weeks ahead, and same-day appointments are released at 7:30 am each weekday. Payment is taken by card at the time of booking; insured patients should see the payment and insurance page. Arrival: please arrive 5 minutes early so reception can check your details. If you arrive more than 10 minutes late for a 15-minute appointment, or more than 15 minutes late for a 30-minute appointment, the GP may not be able to see you; the appointment then counts as a missed appointment and the full fee is charged. Reception will offer the next available slot, which is paid separately. What is included: the consultation, any referral letter or prescription the GP decides on during the appointment, and a written summary in the app. Blood tests and other investigations are charged separately at the published price. Chaperones are available on request at no extra cost.

title: Leeds clinic (Park Square): opening hours, blood tests and access
text: The Wrenfield Clinics Leeds clinic is at Park Square in Leeds city centre, a 10-minute walk from Leeds railway station. Opening hours: Monday to Friday 7:30 am to 8:00 pm, Saturday 8:30 am to 1:00 pm, closed on Sundays and bank holidays. Walk-in blood tests: the phlebotomy room at Leeds takes walk-in patients with a blood test form, with no appointment needed, Monday to Friday 7:30 am to 11:00 am and Saturday 8:30 am to 12:00 pm. Waiting times are longest on Monday mornings. Outside these hours, blood tests at Leeds are by appointment. Services at Leeds: private GP and nurse appointments, the Core and Advanced Health Assessments, ECG, the travel clinic and our registered yellow fever vaccination centre. Parking: there is no on-site parking at Leeds. The nearest public car park is on King Street, about 4 minutes' walk away, and parking tickets are not validated. A drop-off bay outside the main door can be used for up to 10 minutes by blue badge holders. Access: step-free entrance, a lift to all three floors, an accessible toilet on the ground floor and a hearing loop at reception. Contact: 0113 496 0412, or message us in the app.

title: York clinic (Micklegate): opening hours, blood tests and access
text: The Wrenfield Clinics York clinic is on Micklegate, a 5-minute walk from York railway station. Opening hours: Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 6:30 pm. The York clinic is closed on Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays. Blood tests: the York clinic does not take walk-in blood tests. Blood tests at York are by appointment only, Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 10:30 am, booked in the app or by phone. Patients who want a walk-in blood test can use the Leeds clinic. Services at York: private GP and nurse appointments, Core Health Assessments and ECG. The Advanced Health Assessment is available at York on Tuesdays and Thursdays only. The travel clinic and yellow fever vaccination are not available at York. Parking: there are 3 on-site parking spaces at the rear of the building, which must be booked with reception at least one day ahead; they are free for patients for up to 2 hours. Access: the York clinic is in a listed building with no lift. Consulting rooms are on the first floor, but a ground-floor consulting room can be booked for patients who cannot manage stairs; please tell us when booking. Contact: 01632 960 730, or message us in the app.

title: Cancellations and missed appointments (effective 1 March 2024)
text: This policy applies to GP, nurse and health assessment appointments at Wrenfield Clinics. Effective 1 March 2024. Cancelling or rebooking: you can cancel or move an appointment free of charge up to 24 hours before the appointment time, in the app or by phone. Late cancellations: if you cancel or move an appointment within 24 hours of the appointment time, 50% of the appointment fee is charged. Missed appointments: if you do not attend and do not tell us, the full fee is charged. Health assessments: cancelling a Core or Advanced Health Assessment within 24 hours forfeits a £50 booking deposit, and the rest of the fee is refunded. Video consultations can be cancelled free of charge up to 1 hour before. Refunds for eligible cancellations are made to the card used for booking within 5 working days. We understand that emergencies happen; the clinic manager may waive a charge for a hospital admission or a bereavement if you contact us within 7 days. Patients who miss three appointments in a 12-month period may be asked to book by phone only.

title: Cancellations and missed appointments (effective 1 September 2026), replaces the March 2024 policy
text: Effective 1 September 2026. This policy replaces the cancellation policy of 1 March 2024 and applies to GP, nurse and health assessment appointments at both Wrenfield Clinics sites. Cancelling or rebooking: you can cancel or move an appointment free of charge up to 48 hours before the appointment time, in the app or by phone on 0113 496 0412. Late cancellations of GP and nurse appointments: within 48 hours the full fee is charged. There is no longer a 50% charge; a cancellation or change made less than 48 hours before the appointment is treated in the same way as a missed appointment. Missed appointments: if you do not attend, the full fee is charged. Arriving too late to be seen also counts as a missed appointment. Health assessments: cancelling a Core or Advanced Health Assessment within 48 hours forfeits a £75 booking deposit; the rest of the fee is refunded. Video consultations: these can still be cancelled free of charge until 2 hours before the appointment. Refunds for eligible cancellations are made to the card used for booking within 5 working days. Exceptions: the clinic manager may waive a charge for an unplanned hospital admission or a bereavement, if you contact us within 7 days with brief details. Patients who miss two appointments in a 12-month period must pay in full by phone before any further booking is confirmed. Why we changed the policy: short-notice cancellations left many same-week GP slots empty that other patients could have used.

title: Video GP consultations
text: Wrenfield Clinics offers video GP consultations for patients anywhere in the UK, through the Wrenfield app. A video GP appointment lasts 15 minutes and costs £59. Video appointments are available every day, including weekends and bank holidays, from 7:00 am, with the last appointment starting at 9:45 pm. Same-day slots are usually available. Video appointments can be cancelled free of charge until 2 hours before. What the GP can do on video: assess and advise, issue a private prescription sent electronically to a UK pharmacy of your choice (included in the fee; you pay the pharmacy for the medicine), write a referral letter to a specialist, and request blood tests. Fit notes: a video GP can issue fit notes for up to 14 days if clinically appropriate; longer requires a face-to-face appointment. You do not need a fit note for the first seven days of sickness, as you can self-certify. Controlled drugs, such as strong painkillers and sleeping tablets, are not prescribed on video. If the GP decides you need to be examined in person, we will book a face-to-face appointment within 7 days and the £59 is deducted from the face-to-face fee. Video consultations are not for emergencies; for chest pain, severe breathlessness or signs of a stroke, call 999. What you need: a smartphone, tablet or computer with a camera and microphone, a stable internet connection, and a quiet, private place. You can test your camera and sound in the app before your appointment.

title: Core Health Assessment
text: The Core Health Assessment is the standard Wrenfield Clinics health check for adults aged 18 and over, available at both Leeds and York. Price: £199. The appointment takes 45 minutes with a health assessment nurse. What is included: blood pressure, height, weight, BMI and waist measurement, a urine dip test, and blood tests for full blood count, cholesterol (lipid profile), HbA1c, liver function and kidney function. Preparation: you do not need to fast for this assessment. Please eat and drink normally, drink plenty of water beforehand and bring a list of any medicines you take. Results: your results, with the GP's written comments, are released in the patient portal within 5 working days, followed by a 15-minute video results appointment with a GP, which is included in the price and booked for you by our team. If anything needs urgent attention, a GP will call you sooner. Not included: ECG, thyroid tests, vitamin D, ferritin and spirometry, which are part of the Advanced Health Assessment. Extra blood tests can be added on the day at the published price. Booking: Core assessments run Monday to Friday at both clinics. Cancelling within 48 hours of the appointment forfeits the £75 booking deposit. Health assessments are self-pay and are not usually covered by private medical insurance. Corporate packages are available for employers booking five or more staff.

title: Advanced Health Assessment
text: The Advanced Health Assessment is the most detailed Wrenfield Clinics health check for adults aged 18 and over. Price: £429. It is available at Leeds Monday to Saturday and at York on Tuesdays and Thursdays only. The appointment takes 90 minutes. What is included: everything in the Core Health Assessment (blood pressure, BMI, waist, urine dip, full blood count, cholesterol, HbA1c, liver and kidney function), plus a resting ECG, thyroid function, vitamin D, ferritin (iron stores), spirometry (a breathing test), and a PSA blood test for men aged 50 and over on request. Preparation: you do not need to fast for this assessment. Please eat and drink normally, drink plenty of water, and avoid heavy exercise and caffeine for 2 hours before, because of the spirometry test. Wear a top that is easy to remove for the ECG. Results: results are ready within 3 working days and are discussed at a 30-minute face-to-face GP consultation, which is included in the price and booked at the clinic you choose. Not included: imaging such as ultrasound, which can be arranged separately. Booking: cancelling within 48 hours of the appointment forfeits the £75 booking deposit. Health assessments are self-pay and are not usually covered by private medical insurance. If you are booking for a couple on the same day, ask about the £60 joint booking saving.

title: Blood tests: fees, preparation and requests from other doctors
text: Blood tests at Wrenfield Clinics can be requested by a Wrenfield GP or nurse, or by a doctor outside Wrenfield, such as a private consultant. Tests requested by our own clinicians: the blood draw is included, and you pay the published lab price for each test. Tests requested by an external doctor: please bring the doctor's signed request form. There is a £25 sample collection fee on top of the lab price of the tests requested. Results of externally requested tests go directly to the requesting doctor, who is responsible for explaining them; our GPs do not review or interpret them. Where to have blood taken: walk-in blood tests are available at the Leeds clinic; at York, blood tests are by appointment only (see the clinic pages for times). We do not take blood from children under 12. Preparation: most blood tests, including cholesterol, do not need fasting. Fast only if the requesting doctor has specifically asked for a fasting glucose or fasting lipid test; in that case do not eat for 8 hours before, but keep drinking water. For all blood tests, drink plenty of water beforehand and take your usual medicines unless told otherwise. Turnaround times from the lab: routine tests (full blood count, kidney and liver function, cholesterol, HbA1c) in 2 working days; vitamin D and B12 in 3 working days; specialist send-away tests up to 10 working days. Results of tests requested by our clinicians are released to the patient portal after GP review, as described on the test results page.

title: Test results: how and when you receive them
text: At Wrenfield Clinics, test results requested by our GPs and nurses are released to you only after a Wrenfield GP has reviewed them. Results are released to the patient portal after GP review, usually within 1 working day of the lab report reaching us, with a short written comment from the GP explaining what they mean. Health assessment results follow their own timelines, described on the Core and Advanced Health Assessment pages. If a result needs action, a GP will phone you within 2 working days to discuss next steps; urgent results are acted on the same day. Results over the phone: reception and nursing staff are not permitted to read out or interpret results over the phone under any circumstances, including when you have passed security questions. This protects your confidentiality and makes sure results are explained by a clinician. If you cannot use the portal, you can collect a printed copy from reception with photo ID once the GP has reviewed it, or book a 10-minute results appointment with a GP by video or face to face, which costs £35. Results for children under 16 are released to the parent or guardian's portal account. Results of tests requested by external doctors are sent to that doctor and are not shown in your portal. If you have not heard anything 10 working days after a test, please message us through the portal.

title: Prescriptions and repeat medication
text: Private prescriptions: any prescription issued by a Wrenfield GP during a consultation, including a video consultation, is included in the consultation fee. A private prescription issued outside a consultation, for example for a medicine recommended in a letter from your specialist, costs £15 per prescription, and the GP must agree that it is appropriate. With any private prescription you pay the pharmacy the full price of the medicine; NHS prescription charges and exemptions do not apply. Prescriptions are sent electronically to a UK pharmacy of your choice, or a paper copy can be collected from reception with photo ID. Repeat prescriptions: request repeats in the patient portal. Allow 4 working days for a repeat prescription to be processed; requests made after 4:00 pm count from the next working day. Repeat prescriptions are only issued to patients seen by a Wrenfield GP in the last 12 months, and medicines on repeat need a medication review with a GP every 6 months (a standard GP appointment). Each repeat prescription costs £15. Controlled drugs, including strong painkillers and most sleeping tablets, are never issued on repeat. Lost prescriptions: a replacement private prescription is £15. Urgent requests: if you are about to run out, please tell us when you request; we cannot guarantee faster processing, so please order early. Wrenfield Clinics does not run its own pharmacy.

title: Referral letters, fit notes, reports and medical records
text: Referral letters: if a Wrenfield GP decides during a consultation that you need to see a specialist, the referral letter is included in the consultation fee and is usually ready the same day in the app. A standalone referral letter without a consultation costs £45. This is only possible if a Wrenfield GP has seen you about the same problem in the last 12 months; otherwise you need to book an appointment first. Standalone letters are ready within 3 working days. Most private insurers also need an authorisation code before you see the specialist. Fit notes: a GP can issue a fit note at a face-to-face or video appointment when clinically appropriate; fit notes are not issued without a consultation. You do not need a fit note for the first seven days of sickness, as employees can self-certify. Video GPs can issue fit notes for up to 14 days. Forms and reports: insurance claim form completion £60, ready within 10 working days; fitness-to-fly letter £40; private medical report for an employer or insurer £120, ready within 15 working days. These fees are payable in advance. Copies of your medical records: you can ask for a copy of your records with a subject access request, in writing or by email, with photo ID. Under UK data protection law this is free of charge, and we will respond within one month. A summary printout of your recent consultations can be given at reception on request, free.

title: Children and young people
text: Wrenfield Clinics sees children aged 12 months and over at both Leeds and York. We do not see babies under 12 months at either clinic. Our GPs do not provide baby checks or infant care; for a baby under 12 months, please contact your NHS GP or health visitor, call NHS 111 for urgent advice, or call 999 in an emergency. Accompanying adults: children under 16 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian at every appointment, including video appointments. Young people aged 16 and 17 can attend on their own and consent to their own care. A grandparent or other adult can accompany a child only with a signed consent form from a parent, given to reception before the appointment. Fees: children's GP appointments cost the same as adult appointments. Please bring your child's red book (Personal Child Health Record) for children under 5, and a list of any medicines. Vaccinations: we do not give the routine NHS childhood vaccinations, which are given free by your NHS GP practice. We offer a private chickenpox vaccine from 12 months of age, at £75 per dose, with two doses needed. Blood tests: we do not take blood from children under 12; a GP can refer your child to a children's blood test service instead. Health assessments are for adults aged 18 and over only.

title: Travel clinic and vaccinations
text: Travel clinic: the Wrenfield Clinics travel clinic runs at the Leeds clinic only, Monday to Saturday. A 20-minute travel consultation with a travel nurse costs £35 and covers your itinerary, vaccines and malaria advice; vaccines are charged separately. Please book at least 6 weeks before you travel if you can, as some courses need several doses. Yellow fever: yellow fever vaccine is only given at the Leeds clinic, which is a registered yellow fever vaccination centre. It costs £82 including the certificate (the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis). The certificate becomes valid 10 days after the vaccination, so book at least 10 days before departure. A replacement certificate for a yellow fever vaccine given at Wrenfield Clinics costs £15. Yellow fever vaccine is not given at York. Other travel vaccines: hepatitis A £65 per dose, typhoid £45, rabies £70 per dose (three doses), and a combined hepatitis A and B vaccine £95 per dose. Flu vaccine: the seasonal flu vaccine is £18, available as a walk-in at both Leeds and York from 1 October to 31 January, Monday to Friday. Malaria tablets are prescribed after the travel consultation on a private prescription. Payment is taken at the appointment.

title: Payment and private medical insurance
text: Self-pay patients: payment is taken by debit or credit card when you book, or in the app; contactless phone payments are accepted at reception. The York clinic does not accept cash; the Leeds clinic accepts cash for walk-in blood tests and flu vaccines only. Receipts and invoices are available in the app. Insured patients: Wrenfield Clinics is recognised by most major UK private medical insurers for GP appointments, specialist-referred tests and some screening. Before booking, you need an authorisation code from your insurer and your membership number; please call your insurer first, as many policies do not cover private GP appointments. We also take your card details as a guarantee at booking. Any excess, any shortfall between our fee and what your insurer pays, and anything your insurer does not cover is charged to your card within 30 days of the insurer's settlement, and you will be emailed a statement first. Health assessments and travel vaccines are self-pay and are not billed to insurers. Corporate schemes: if your employer has a Wrenfield corporate account, give your employer's scheme reference when booking; you will not be asked to pay at the appointment, except for services outside your employer's scheme. Payment queries are handled by the accounts team, Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

title: Household metered water and wastewater charges 2026/27, effective 1 April 2026
text: These charges apply to metered household customers in both the Harrowmere and Lynchford supply zones from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, and they replace the 2025/26 household charges scheme. Water supply is charged at £2.1846 per cubic metre and wastewater at £2.4130 per cubic metre. Wastewater is charged on 90 percent of the water recorded by the meter, to allow for water that does not return to the public sewer, such as water used in the garden. This is lower than the 95 percent used under the previous scheme. Customers who can show that more than 10 percent of their water does not reach the sewer, for example because of a livestock trough or a very large garden, can apply for an individual non-return assessment. Standing charges are £41.60 a year for water and £36.80 a year for wastewater, and they are charged daily even when no water is used. Surface water drainage is charged at £61.20 a year. If no rainwater from the roof or paved areas drains to the public sewer, for example because it runs to a soakaway, the customer can apply for a surface water rebate, which removes this charge and is backdated to 1 April of the year in which the application is received, but no earlier. Meters are read twice a year, and bills in between use an estimate based on the average daily use between the last two actual readings. A customer who sends in a reading within 14 days of an estimated bill will be sent a revised bill free of charge.

title: Household metered water and wastewater charges 2025/26 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 April 2026 by the 2026/27 household charges scheme. This page is kept for reference because bills for water used before 1 April 2026 were worked out on it. Water supply was charged at £2.0315 per cubic metre and wastewater at £2.2470 per cubic metre. Wastewater was charged on 95 percent of the water recorded by the meter. Standing charges were £39.20 a year for water and £34.10 a year for wastewater. Surface water drainage was charged at £57.40 a year, and the surface water rebate could be backdated for up to 2 years. Meters were read once a year, in the spring. Changeover rule: where a billing period runs across 1 April 2026, the water used is split between the old and new charges in proportion to the number of days on each side of that date, and both calculations are shown on the bill. Customers who think the split has been worked out wrongly can ask for it to be checked within 3 months of the bill date. Customers on the Fair Share social tariff or the capped charge scheme had their discount applied to these charges in the same way as they are applied now.

title: Complaints, response times and contact hours
text: Our customer contact centre is open 8 am to 8 pm Monday to Friday and 8 am to 2 pm on Saturdays, and is closed on Sundays and bank holidays. The water leak and burst line is open 24 hours on 0800 046 3311, and the gas emergency line on 0800 046 2219 is also open 24 hours. Complaints can be made by phone, in writing, online or in the app. We will reply to a written complaint within 10 working days. If we do not, household customers are paid £30 automatically, and a further £30 if we also miss the stage 2 deadline. If the customer is not happy with the first reply, they can ask for a stage 2 review by a senior manager, who will reply within 20 working days. Water complaints that are still not resolved after stage 2 can be taken to the independent consumer body for water, and after that to the water redress scheme. Gas complaints can be taken to the energy ombudsman once 8 weeks have passed since the complaint was first made, or earlier if we send a final response letter. Customers must take a complaint to the energy ombudsman within 12 months of our final response. All of these services are free to use.

title: Gas emergencies, safety checks and gas supply interruptions
text: If you smell gas, or think there is a gas leak or carbon monoxide, call the 24-hour gas emergency line on 0800 046 2219. Our emergency engineers attend uncontrolled gas escapes within 1 hour and controlled escapes within 2 hours. The engineer makes the situation safe and may turn off the supply or disconnect an unsafe appliance, but does not repair boilers, cookers or fires; pipework after the meter is the customer's responsibility and must be repaired by a registered gas engineer. We provide a free annual gas safety check for customers on the priority services register who own their home and either receive a means-tested benefit, or are over state pension age and live alone or only with others who are over pension age, disabled or under 18. Tenants are not eligible, because landlords must arrange a gas safety check every 12 months by law. If your gas supply is interrupted for more than 24 hours because of a fault on our network, household customers are paid £60, plus £60 for each further 24 hours without gas. This payment is made automatically within 20 working days. Customers on the priority services register are offered free temporary heating and cooking equipment if the interruption lasts more than 12 hours. After a gas interruption, an engineer will visit to turn the supply back on and check appliances; customers should not try to restore the supply themselves.

title: Domestic gas standard credit tariff, from 1 October 2026
text: This tariff applies to domestic gas customers with a credit meter. From 1 October 2026 it replaces the rates that applied from 1 July 2026, which were 6.34p per kWh and 31.65p per day. For customers paying by monthly direct debit, the unit rate is 6.08p per kWh and the standing charge is 30.92p per day. Customers who pay when they receive their bill pay 6.38p per kWh and 32.47p per day. All prices include VAT at 5 percent. The standing charge normally applies every day, whether or not gas is used. However, if a property records zero gas use for a full calendar month and the account holder has registered it with us as unoccupied, the standing charge for that month is waived. A property can be registered as unoccupied online or by phone, and the registration must be renewed every 6 months; the waiver is not available on prepayment meters. Gas meters are read by us at least once every 2 years, and customers are asked to send a reading every month. Readings in cubic metres are converted to kilowatt hours using a volume correction factor of 1.02264 and the average calorific value for the billing period. Customers on the 12-month fixed tariff pay 6.45p per kWh and 29.80p per day, with an exit fee of £40 if they leave more than 49 days before the end of the fix.

title: Domestic gas prepayment tariff, from 1 October 2026
text: This tariff applies to domestic gas customers with a prepayment meter, including smart meters running in prepayment mode. From 1 October 2026 the unit rate is 5.96p per kWh and the standing charge is 29.40p per day, both including VAT at 5 percent. Unlike the credit tariff, there is no standing charge waiver for unoccupied properties: the standing charge builds up every day, and any amount owed while the meter has no credit is recovered from the next top-up. Top-ups can be made in the app, by phone, or at any shop showing the payment card sign. The minimum top-up is £5.
