If credit runs out, emergency credit of £10 can be selected on the meter and is repaid from the next top-up. Friendly credit means the gas will not be cut off between 4 pm and 10 am on weekdays, or at any time at weekends or on bank holidays; any amount used during friendly credit is repaid from the next top-up. Customers who are repaying a debt through the meter will have no more than £3.50 a week deducted for the debt. Customers on the priority services register can ask for an extra £20 of discretionary credit once in any 12 months. Switching from a prepayment meter to a credit meter is free if the customer passes a credit check or pays a deposit of £120.

title: Temporary use ban (hosepipe ban), summer 2026
text: A temporary use ban has been in force since 4 August 2026 in the Lynchford supply zone only. Customers in the Harrowmere supply zone are not affected, and customers can check which zone they are in on their bill. During the ban, customers must not use a hosepipe connected to the mains to water a garden or allotment, clean a car, van or boat, fill or maintain a domestic swimming or paddling pool, clean walls, windows or paths, or fill an ornamental pond. Ponds containing fish are exempt. Watering cans and buckets filled from a tap are allowed at all times, as is using water from a water butt or grey water. Newly laid turf may be watered with a hosepipe for 14 days from the day it is laid, and new plants for 14 days from planting. Holders of a disabled parking badge, and customers on the priority services register who ask for it, are exempt. Drip irrigation systems fitted with a timer are exempt. Breaking the ban is a criminal offence with a fine of up to £1,000 on conviction. Because the ban limits how customers can use their water, household customers in the Lynchford zone receive a credit of £12 on their next bill for each full calendar month the ban is in force. The ban is reviewed every 2 weeks and will be lifted when Coldmoor Reservoir is back above 70 percent full.

title: Water supply interruptions, low pressure and guaranteed standards payments
text: For planned work that will turn off a household's water supply for more than 4 hours, we give at least 48 hours' notice in writing. If we do not give this notice, or the supply is not back on by the time we said, we pay £30 to household customers. For an unplanned interruption, such as a burst main, we aim to restore supply within 12 hours. If supply is not restored within 12 hours, household customers are entitled to £40, plus £20 for each further 24 hours without water. If the burst is on a large trunk main, the first target is 48 hours instead of 12. Payments for planned work are made automatically, but payments for unplanned interruptions are not automatic: household customers must claim them by phone or online within 3 months of the interruption, quoting their account number. Approved payments are credited to the account within 20 working days. No payment is due where the interruption was caused by a fault on the customer's own pipework. When the supply has been off for more than 12 hours, bottled water stations are opened, and customers on the priority services register have bottled water delivered within 6 hours. If water pressure falls below 7 metres head on two occasions, each lasting more than an hour, within 28 days, a payment of £25 is made. After a repair, water may look cloudy or discoloured for a short time; if it is still discoloured after running the cold kitchen tap for 20 minutes, customers should call us.

title: Leak allowance and free supply pipe repairs for household customers
text: If a metered household customer's bill is high because of a leak on their underground supply pipe, a leak allowance can be applied. The supply pipe is the pipe between the boundary stop tap and the point where it enters the building. Leaks inside the property are not covered, including dripping taps, overflowing cisterns, leaking toilets, faulty appliances and burst pipes in the loft. The leak must be repaired within 21 days of the customer finding it or of us telling them about it, and evidence of the repair, such as a plumber's invoice, must reach us within 60 days. The allowance removes the wastewater charge on the leaked water in full, because the leaked water did not reach the sewer. The water charge is not removed: the leaked water is still billed at the normal water rate, because it had already been treated and supplied. The volume of leaked water is worked out by comparing the bill with the average daily use for the same period in the previous year. Only one leak allowance is given per customer at each property in any period of 5 years. We also offer one free repair of a leak on a household supply pipe, covering up to 25 metres of pipe under a garden, drive or path; the repair is booked within 10 working days of the customer asking. If the repair finds that the supply pipe is made of lead, we replace it up to the building at no charge.

title: Leak allowance for business customers
text: This page applies to non-household premises such as shops, offices, farms and community buildings. Household customers should read the household leak allowance page instead, because the rules are different. If a business customer's metered bill is high because of an underground leak on their supply pipe, a leak allowance can be applied once the leak is repaired. The repair must be made within 14 days of the leak being found or reported to the customer, and evidence of the repair must reach us within 30 days. The allowance removes the wastewater charge on the leaked water in full and reduces the water charge on the leaked water by 50 percent. A leak allowance is only considered where the leaked volume is at least 50 cubic metres. Only one leak allowance is given per premises in any period of 3 years. Leaks inside buildings, on irrigation systems, in swimming pools or on troughs and fittings are not covered. There is no free repair service for business supply pipes; the customer must use their own contractor. Where a business occupies part of a building with a shared supply, the allowance is split according to the floor area each occupier uses.

title: Switching to a water meter, switching back, and assessed charges
text: Any household customer who pays unmetered charges can ask for a water meter to be fitted free of charge. We will carry out a survey within 21 days of the request and, where a meter can be fitted, fit it within 60 days of the request. Most meters are fitted in a boundary box under the pavement, so nobody needs to be at home. Metered charges start from the date the meter is fitted. If the metered bills turn out to be higher, the customer can switch back to unmetered charges at any time within 24 months of the meter being fitted, or within 30 days of receiving the second bill based on actual readings, whichever is later. A switch back takes effect from the date of the request, and the difference for the period already metered is not refunded. Customers who move into a property that already has a meter cannot switch back. Where a meter cannot be fitted, for example because the supply pipe is shared or cannot be reached, the customer is offered an assessed charge instead: £318 a year for a single occupier, or a charge based on the number of bedrooms, which is £402 a year for one or two bedrooms, £529 for three bedrooms and £648 for four or more. The customer pays the assessed charge or their unmetered charge, whichever is lower. Unmetered charges for 2026/27 are £1.4210 for water and £1.6380 for wastewater per pound of rateable value, plus the same standing charges as metered customers.

title: Moving home
text: Customers moving out should tell us at least 2 working days before the moving date, and give closing readings for the water meter and the gas meter on the day they leave. Readings can be given online, in the app or by phone, and a dated photo of each meter is accepted as proof. If we are told within 14 days after the moving date, charges stop on the moving date. If we are told more than 14 days after the moving date, charges continue until the date we are told, and they cannot be backdated to the moving date, even with a completion statement or a tenancy agreement. A final bill is sent within 10 working days of the closing readings, and any credit is refunded within 10 working days of the final bill. Customers moving into a property must tell us within 14 days and give opening readings. Where a property in the Lynchford supply zone changes occupier and has no water meter, a meter is fitted and the new occupier is billed on metered charges from the date the meter is fitted. In the Harrowmere supply zone new occupiers can choose to stay on unmetered charges. Direct debits are moved to the new address automatically if both properties are in our area.

title: Paying your bill: instalments, direct debit and missed payments
text: Unmetered water customers receive one bill a year in March covering April to March, and metered customers are billed every 6 months. By default, the annual water bill is split into 10 monthly direct debit payments from April to January. Customers can ask for 12 monthly payments instead, or for weekly or fortnightly payments using a payment card. Direct debit payment dates can be the 1st, 8th, 15th or 22nd of the month. There is no discount for paying by direct debit. Customers who pay the full year's water bill by 30 April receive a discount of 1.5 percent. Gas customers on a credit meter pay a fixed monthly direct debit worked out from their expected use for the year, and the amount is reviewed every 6 months. If a direct debit payment is returned unpaid, we will try to collect it again 10 days later, and there is no charge for a returned payment. If two water instalments in a year are returned unpaid, the instalment arrangement is cancelled and the rest of the year's bill becomes due within 14 days. Payments can also be made by debit or credit card online or by phone, by bank transfer, or with cash at any shop showing the payment card sign; card payments are free. Customers who are worried about paying should call us before missing a payment so that a payment plan can be agreed.

title: Priority services register
text: The priority services register is a free service for customers who need extra help. Customers can register if they are of state pension age, have a disability or long-term health condition, have a hearing, sight or speech difficulty, depend on water or gas for medical equipment such as home dialysis, have children under 5 living at home, or are temporarily in need, for example after an operation or a bereavement. Temporary registrations last 12 months and all other registrations are reviewed every 2 years. Registered customers receive advance notice of planned water and gas interruptions, bottled water delivered to their door within 6 hours during a water interruption of more than 12 hours, temporary heating and cooking equipment during gas interruptions, and bills in large print, braille or audio. A password scheme lets customers check that a caller at the door is genuine. A nominee, such as a relative or carer, can be set up to receive bills and letters. Customers who cannot read their gas meter safely can ask for it to be moved free of charge, and those who cannot reach their stop tap can have a free visit to fit an easy-turn stop tap. With the customer's consent, registration details are shared with the regional electricity network so the customer does not need to register twice.

title: Help if you are struggling to pay: social tariff, capped charges and payment matching
text: Our Fair Share social tariff gives a 50 percent discount on water and wastewater charges to households with a total gross income below £21,500 a year. Once awarded, the discount lasts for 2 years, after which customers need to reapply. Metered customers who receive a means-tested benefit and either have three or more children under 19 living at home or have a medical condition that needs extra water can join the capped charge scheme, which limits the bill to the average household water bill, set at £512 for 2026/27. Our payment matching scheme helps customers with water arrears: for each payment made under an agreed 12-month plan, we clear the same amount of arrears, up to a maximum of £1,000. A customer can miss up to 2 payments in the plan before it is cancelled. Gas customers in hardship can apply to our hardship fund for a grant of up to £750 towards gas arrears, once in any 2 years. If a customer tells us they are getting debt advice, we pause recovery action for 60 days. We never disconnect a household water supply for non-payment, as this is not allowed by law. For gas debts we will always offer a payment plan before considering a prepayment meter, and a prepayment meter will never be fitted under warrant for a customer on the priority services register.

title: Bill dates, due dates and delayed payment surcharge
text: Domestic consumers are billed every two months; commercial (LT-II) and industrial consumers are billed monthly. The due date is printed on the bill and is 15 days from the bill date for domestic connections and 10 days for commercial connections. A delayed payment surcharge (DPS) of 1.5 percent per month on the unpaid amount is added from the day after the due date, worked out per day of delay, with a minimum surcharge of ₹20. The DPS appears on the following bill. Holiday rule: if the printed due date falls on a Sunday or a public holiday, a payment on the next working day is treated as on time only at cash counters. Online payments must be completed by 11:59 pm on the printed due date, because the online channels are open every day. A prompt payment rebate of 1 percent of energy charges, capped at ₹100, is given when a domestic bill is paid in full within 5 days of the bill date through any digital channel. Bills that are not received can be downloaded from the app or website using the 12-digit consumer number; non-receipt of a bill is not accepted as a reason to waive the DPS.

title: Customer care centres, hours and helplines
text: Customer care centres are at Station Road in Nalgarh, the Collectorate Complex in Sirupur, and the Kanhai and Ralegaon sub-division offices. They are open 9:30 am to 5:30 pm, Monday to Saturday, and are closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Cash counters close at 4:30 pm. The Nalgarh centre stays open until 7 pm on the last two working days of each month, for bill payments only. The 24-hour helpline 1800 425 7766 is for outages and safety emergencies only; billing queries on the helpline are handled from 8 am to 8 pm, and calls about bills outside those hours are asked to call back. Complaints not resolved within 15 days can be taken to the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum at Sirupur. After a decision by the forum, a consumer who is still not satisfied may approach the state Electricity Ombudsman within 30 days of the forum's order. There is no fee for filing a complaint with either the forum or the ombudsman.

title: Disconnection for non-payment and reconnection
text: If a bill remains unpaid 15 days after the due date, a disconnection notice is sent by SMS and as a printed notice, and supply may be disconnected after a further 7 days. Disconnections are not carried out after 4 pm, on Sundays or on public holidays. To reconnect, all dues including the delayed payment surcharge must be paid. The reconnection fee is ₹125 for single-phase connections and ₹350 for three-phase connections, and it is added to the next bill rather than collected upfront. Supply is restored within 6 hours of payment in Nalgarh city and within 24 hours elsewhere. If a connection stays disconnected for more than 6 months, the supply agreement is terminated, the security deposit is adjusted against the dues, and a fresh connection application with full charges is needed. A part payment does not stop a disconnection unless an instalment plan has been approved by the section officer. Instalment plans allow arrears above ₹5,000 to be paid in up to 3 monthly instalments, and are allowed once in any 24-month period.

title: Meter accuracy testing on request
text: Consumers who suspect a faulty meter can ask for it to be tested by paying a testing fee of ₹200 for single-phase meters and ₹500 for three-phase meters. Testing is done at the premises with a reference meter within 10 working days, and the consumer or a representative may be present. If the consumer disputes the site result, the meter can be sent to the accredited laboratory at Sirupur for an extra ₹300. A meter is treated as accurate if its error is within plus or minus 1 percent for smart meters, or plus or minus 2 percent for older electromechanical meters. If the meter is found running fast beyond the limit, the testing fee is refunded and bills for up to the previous 6 months are revised. If it is found running slow beyond the limit, Vellora may recover the shortfall for up to 3 months only. While a test is pending, the consumer must keep paying the average of the last 3 undisputed bills to avoid disconnection.

title: Prepaid smart meters
text: Prepaid smart meters are being installed across Nalgarh city since 2025 and are optional elsewhere. Prepaid consumers get a rebate of 2 percent on energy charges. The minimum recharge is ₹200, and recharges can be made in the app, through UPI or at any cash counter. Low balance alerts are sent by SMS at ₹300 and at ₹100. When the balance goes below zero, supply is not cut immediately: an emergency credit of ₹150 or 3 days, whichever runs out first, is allowed automatically. Supply is never cut between 6 pm and 9 am, on Sundays or on public holidays; disconnection for a negative balance happens only between 10 am and 1 pm on working days, and supply returns within 15 minutes of a recharge. Daily fixed charges are deducted from the balance at midnight. Any unused balance is refunded within 30 days if the connection is closed. Switching back to a postpaid meter is allowed after 12 months on prepaid, with a meter change fee of ₹500.

title: New domestic connection: documents, charges and timelines
text: Applications for a new domestic connection can be made online or at the section office. Documents needed: proof of ownership or occupancy, which can be a sale deed, a property tax receipt, or a registered rent agreement with owner's NOC; a photo ID; and a wiring completion certificate from a licensed electrical contractor. Charges for a single-phase domestic connection up to 5 kW are an application fee of ₹50, a service connection charge of ₹1,500, and a refundable security deposit of ₹800 per kW of sanctioned load. Three-phase domestic connections above 5 kW and up to 20 kW have a service connection charge of ₹4,000 and the same deposit rate. The connection is released within 7 working days in Nalgarh and Sirupur towns and within 15 working days in rural areas, where no network extension is needed. Where a new pole or line extension is required, the cost is estimated separately and the connection is released within 30 days of payment of the estimate. The security deposit earns interest at the bank rate, credited every year on the April bill.

title: New commercial (LT-II) connection: documents, charges and timelines
text: This page covers shops, offices, clinics and other non-domestic premises up to 50 kW. Documents needed: proof of ownership or a registered lease, a photo ID of the proprietor or authorised signatory, a trade licence or shop and establishment registration, and a wiring completion certificate from a licensed electrical contractor. Charges for a single-phase commercial connection are an application fee of ₹100, a service connection charge of ₹3,000, and a refundable security deposit of ₹2,000 per kW of sanctioned load. Three-phase commercial connections have a service connection charge of ₹6,500 and the same deposit rate. Commercial connections are released within 10 working days in towns and 20 working days in rural areas where no network extension is needed. A commercial connection cannot be released at a residential address unless the owner has a mixed-use approval from the municipality. Commercial consumers are billed monthly, and the security deposit is reviewed every April against the average of the last 12 bills; any shortfall is billed as an additional deposit.

title: Planned and unplanned outages, and compensation
text: Planned maintenance shutdowns are announced at least 48 hours in advance by SMS and in local newspapers, and each shutdown is limited to 6 hours between 9 am and 5 pm. Unplanned outages can be reported on the 24-hour helpline 1800 425 7766, by SMS to 56070, or in the app; every report gets a complaint number. Under Vellora's standards of performance, if supply to an individual consumer is not restored within 4 hours in towns or 12 hours in rural areas after the fault is reported, the consumer is entitled to ₹50 for each additional 6 hours or part of it, up to ₹500 per incident. Compensation is not automatic: it must be claimed in writing or through the app within 30 days of the outage, quoting the complaint number. Compensation is not payable for outages caused by storms declared a natural calamity, by faults in the consumer's own wiring, or during load shedding ordered by the state grid. Approved compensation is credited on the next bill.

title: Payment channels and limits, effective 1 January 2026
text: Bills can be paid through the Vellora Energy app, the website, any UPI app using the 12-digit consumer number, net banking, debit and credit cards, and at 46 cash collection counters across the two circles. Credit card payments carry a convenience fee of 0.9 percent of the amount plus GST, charged by the payment gateway; UPI, net banking and debit card payments are free. Cash is accepted only for bills up to ₹10,000; anything above that must be paid digitally or by demand draft drawn in favour of Vellora Energy Distribution Ltd. This limit replaces the earlier ₹50,000 cash limit set by the 2023 collection circular. Cheques are accepted at counters for domestic bills only. A dishonoured cheque attracts a penalty of ₹500 plus the delayed payment surcharge, and after two dishonoured cheques in 12 months the account is barred from paying by cheque for one year. Payments made through third-party apps can take up to 2 working days to show on the account, but the time stamp on the payment receipt is treated as the payment date when the surcharge is worked out.

title: Cash collection circular VED/COM/2023/14 (superseded)
text: Circular VED/COM/2023/14, dated 3 March 2023, is superseded by the payment channel rules that took effect on 1 January 2026, and is kept here only for reference. Under this circular, cash payments were accepted up to ₹50,000 per bill at all collection counters, and cheques were accepted at counters for both domestic and commercial bills. A dishonoured cheque attracted a penalty of ₹250, and there was no bar on future cheque payments after a dishonour. Counter hours under the circular were 9 am to 4 pm on working days and 9 am to 1 pm on the first and third Saturdays. Credit card payments at that time were accepted only on the website, with a convenience fee of 1.1 percent. Collection agents were required to issue a printed receipt for every cash payment and to deposit collections at the sub-division office by 5 pm the same day. Consumers paying arrears of more than ₹25,000 needed the approval of the assistant engineer before the counter could accept the payment.

title: Rooftop solar for domestic consumers: net billing, effective 1 October 2025
text: From 1 October 2025, new domestic rooftop solar systems are connected under net billing, not net metering. Under net billing, every unit you import from the grid is charged at the normal domestic tariff, and every unit you export is credited at a fixed rate of ₹2.85 per unit. Exports therefore do not cancel imports one for one. This replaces net metering, under which exports offset imports unit for unit; systems commissioned before 1 October 2025 stay on net metering until 30 September 2032. The maximum system size is 10 kW or the sanctioned load, whichever is lower. The application fee is ₹1,000, and the bidirectional meter costs ₹3,600, paid by the consumer. Export credits are adjusted against later bills. Any credit still unused on 31 March each year will lapse, with no payout and no carry-forward into the next financial year. A system can be commissioned only after inspection by the section engineer, which is done within 15 working days of the installer's completion report.

title: Domestic (LT-I) tariff schedule, effective 1 April 2026
text: This schedule applies to all domestic (LT-I) connections in the Nalgarh and Sirupur circles with effect from 1 April 2026 and replaces the schedule dated 1 April 2024. Energy charges are telescopic and are set per billing month: 0 to 100 units at ₹3.40 per unit, 101 to 250 units at ₹5.15 per unit, 251 to 400 units at ₹6.90 per unit, and above 400 units at ₹8.25 per unit. Because domestic meters are read every two months, the slab limits are doubled for a bimonthly bill, so the first 200 units of a two-month bill are charged at ₹3.40 per unit, the next 300 units at ₹5.15, and so on. The fixed charge is ₹45 per kW of sanctioned load per month, with a minimum of ₹45 per month for any connection, including a locked house with zero consumption. Electricity duty of 6 percent is levied on energy charges only, not on fixed charges. A fuel and power purchase cost adjustment (FPPCA) is applied quarterly and shown as a separate line on the bill; for July to September 2026 it is 18 paise per unit. Lifeline consumers whose consumption stays at or below 50 units per month are billed at a flat ₹1.75 per unit with no fixed charge, but if consumption crosses 50 units in any month the entire bill for that period is charged at the normal slab rates.

title: Domestic (LT-I) tariff schedule, effective 1 April 2024 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 April 2026 by the current domestic tariff schedule. This page is kept for reference because bills for consumption before 1 April 2026 were calculated on it. Energy charges were telescopic per billing month: 0 to 100 units at ₹3.10 per unit, 101 to 200 units at ₹4.80 per unit, 201 to 400 units at ₹6.40 per unit, and above 400 units at ₹7.90 per unit. The fixed charge was ₹40 per kW of sanctioned load per month. Electricity duty was 5 percent of energy charges. Lifeline consumers using up to 50 units per month were billed at ₹1.50 per unit. For bimonthly bills the slab limits were doubled in the same way as today. Changeover rule: where a two-month billing period includes days both before and after 1 April 2026, total consumption is split between the old and new schedules in proportion to the number of days in each, and both calculations are shown on the bill. Consumers who believe the split was calculated wrongly can ask for a recalculation at their section office within 60 days of the bill date.

title: Name change and ownership transfer
text: To change the name on a connection after a purchase or an inheritance, submit the transfer form with the sale deed or a legal heir certificate, a photo ID, and a no-dues certificate for the connection. The fee is ₹100 for domestic and ₹500 for commercial connections. Tenants cannot have an existing connection transferred into their own name; a tenant can only be added as an alternate contact for SMS alerts and bill reminders, and the connection stays in the owner's name. Transfers are processed within 7 working days. The existing security deposit moves to the new owner only if the previous owner signs a consent letter; otherwise the new owner pays a fresh deposit and the old deposit is refunded to the previous owner. When the transfer follows the death of the registered consumer, the fee is waived if the application is made within 6 months of the date of death; after 6 months the normal fee applies. Name corrections for spelling mistakes are free and are handled at the section office.

title: Bank feeds: sync and troubleshooting
text: Bank feeds connect a current or savings account so that transactions are pulled in automatically for reconciliation. Bank feeds are available on Growth and Pro only; Starter users can import statements as CSV or XLSX files. On Growth, feeds refresh once a day at about 6 am. On Pro, they refresh every 4 hours and can also be refreshed manually up to 5 times a day. Up to 2 bank accounts can be connected on Growth and up to 10 on Pro. A feed is set up through a consent you give on your bank's own login page, and this consent expires every 180 days. When it expires the feed stops quietly, with only an alert on the dashboard, and the Owner must reconnect it from Banking, Reconnect. This is the most common reason a feed stops working. Other causes are an account that was closed or renamed at the bank, a bank server outage, after which the feed recovers on its own within 48 hours, or a joint account that needs the other holder's approval. Transactions older than 90 days cannot be pulled through a feed and must be imported from a statement. Duplicate transactions after a reconnect can be removed with the Remove duplicates option on the reconciliation screen.

title: Renewal, auto-debit and subscription invoices
text: Subscriptions renew automatically at the end of each monthly or annual term. For customers paying by card or UPI autopay, the renewal payment is attempted 3 days before the renewal date, not on the renewal date itself, so that a failed payment can be fixed before service is affected. If the first attempt fails, it is retried 2 days before and again on the renewal date. Autopay can be set up with a credit card, a debit card or a UPI mandate. Customers paying by net banking or bank transfer get a payment link 7 days before renewal and must pay it manually. Renewal reminders are sent by email and SMS 15 days and 3 days before renewal. Renewals are charged at the price list in force on the renewal date. To get a GST invoice with your GSTIN, so that you can claim input tax credit, add the GSTIN under Settings, Subscription before the payment is made; a subscription invoice cannot be re-issued with a GSTIN after the end of the month in which it was raised. Switching from monthly to annual billing can be done at any time, and the unused days of the current month are adjusted against the annual price. Switching from annual to monthly billing takes effect only at the end of the annual term.

title: Backups and data export
text: Every company is backed up automatically every night, and nightly backups are kept for 30 days. Customers cannot restore a backup themselves; restore requests go through support, and a restore overwrites all entries made after the backup date. One restore per quarter is free, and further restores cost ₹499 plus GST each. You can export data at any time while the subscription is active. Reports and registers export as XLSX, CSV or PDF. A full company backup downloads as a single encrypted .lwbk file, which can only be opened by importing it into an account on our service; it cannot be read in spreadsheet software. For use outside our service, choose Full Export, which produces a ZIP of CSV files for all masters and transactions plus PDF copies of every invoice. A Full Export of a large company can take up to 6 hours, and a download link valid for 7 days is emailed to the Owner. Attachments such as scanned bills are included in Full Export up to 5 GB per company. All data is stored in data centres in India and is not moved abroad. The mobile app keeps an offline copy of the last 90 days of invoices only; it is not a backup.

title: GST returns, e-invoicing and e-way bills
text: The app prepares GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B from the sales and purchase data in your books. On Growth and Pro, GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B can be filed directly from the app through our GST Suvidha Provider partner, by verifying with an EVC OTP sent to the authorised signatory; filing with a digital signature certificate is supported on Pro only. On Starter, the app prepares the return as a JSON file that you upload on the GST portal yourself. GSTR-9 annual returns and GSTR-4 composition returns cannot be filed from the app; a summary report is provided to help you prepare them. Purchase invoices can be matched with GSTR-2B, which is imported automatically on the 14th of each month on Pro and imported manually on Growth. E-invoices (IRNs) and e-way bills are generated from the invoice screen and count against the monthly quota of your plan: 100 each on Growth and 1,000 each on Pro. Cancelled IRNs still count toward the quota. Top-up packs of 100 e-invoices cost ₹199 plus GST and are valid until the end of the month in which they are bought. GSTIN validation checks the format and the live status of the number; a GSTIN that shows as cancelled or suspended cannot be saved on a customer.

title: Invoice numbering and financial-year closing
text: Each company can have up to 10 invoice series, each with its own prefix, for example by branch or by document type. Invoice numbers are limited to 16 characters including the prefix, and may use letters, digits, hyphen and slash. Numbering does not restart automatically at the start of a financial year: an existing series simply continues on 1 April. To start from 1 for the new year, create a new series for that financial year under Settings, Invoice Series before raising the first invoice of the year. If two invoices end up with the same number, which can happen when a series was edited manually, the second one is flagged and e-invoice generation for it is blocked until it is renumbered. To close a financial year, the Owner or an Admin runs Year-End Closing, which carries forward ledger balances, stock values and outstanding invoices as opening balances. A closed year is locked for editing. Only the Owner can reopen a closed year, and only until 30 November of the following financial year; after that date the year is permanently locked and any corrections must be posted as adjustment entries in the current year. Year-End Closing can be run from 1 April onwards, and you can keep billing in the new year before the old year is closed.

title: Assisted migration for Growth plan customers
text: Customers on Growth can move their books from another accounting software or from spreadsheets either on their own, using the free import templates, or with assisted migration for a one-time fee of ₹2,999 plus GST per company. Assisted migration on Growth covers masters, meaning customers, vendors, items and ledgers, and opening balances as on the cut-over date only. Past transactions are not migrated on Growth. You send us a trial balance, outstanding receivables and payables, and a stock summary as on the cut-over date, in XLSX or CSV format. The migration is completed within 7 working days of receiving complete data, and you get a reconciliation sheet comparing the old and new trial balances. Opening GST input credit is not migrated as a balance and must be entered as a journal by your accountant. The cut-over date must be the first day of a month. The migration fee is not refundable once work has started. If you upgrade from Growth to Pro within 30 days of paying for assisted migration, the fee is credited against your Pro subscription.

title: Assisted migration for Pro plan customers
text: Customers on Pro get assisted migration free of charge for up to 5 companies. Assisted migration on Pro covers masters, meaning customers, vendors, items and ledgers, opening balances as on the cut-over date, and up to 3 years of past transactions, including invoices, bills, receipts and payments, so that prior-year reports can be run inside the app. You send us a trial balance, outstanding receivables and payables, a stock summary and day books for the years to be migrated, in XLSX or CSV format. The migration is completed within 5 working days of receiving complete data. A migration specialist then books a 30-minute verification call to walk through the reconciliation sheet with you or your accountant. Migrations of more than 3 years of history, or of more than 5 companies, are quoted separately at ₹1,500 per extra company and ₹1,000 per extra year. Opening GST input credit is migrated as an opening balance in the electronic credit ledger. The cut-over date can be any date, but the first day of a quarter is recommended.

title: Multi-currency invoicing
text: Multi-currency invoicing is available on Pro only. You can raise invoices in 24 foreign currencies, including US dollars, euros, pounds sterling and UAE dirhams. Exchange rates are not fetched automatically: you must enter the exchange rate on each foreign-currency invoice and on each payment received, and the app does not suggest a rate. The base currency of every company is Indian rupees and cannot be changed. When a payment is received at a different rate from the invoice, the difference is posted automatically to the Exchange Gain or Loss ledger. Export invoices can be marked either as supply under LUT without payment of IGST, or as supply with payment of IGST. The LUT reference number and its validity must be entered under Settings, GST before the first export invoice of each financial year, or export invoices under LUT cannot be saved. Foreign-currency invoices show amounts in both the foreign currency and rupees on the PDF. A company that downgrades from Pro to Growth keeps its existing foreign-currency invoices for viewing and reports, but cannot raise new ones or record receipts against them except as a rupee amount.

title: Payroll add-on
text: Payroll is an add-on available on Growth and Pro at ₹40 per employee per month plus GST, with a minimum charge of ₹400 per month; on Pro the first 10 employees are included free. Billing is based on the number of employees for whom a payslip is generated in the month, not the number of employees on record. Payroll calculates salary, PF and ESI contributions, professional tax for 12 states, and TDS on salary under both the old and new tax regimes. It generates the PF return file and the ESI contribution file for upload on the respective portals, but it does not pay the challans for you. Payslips are emailed to employees on the 1st of each month, or on the date you set, and employees can download them through a self-service link. Salaries are not paid out by our service; a bank upload file in a standard CSV format is generated for you to upload in your net banking. Form 16 Part B is generated on Pro only. Payroll cannot be run from the mobile app. The payroll add-on can be switched off at any time and stops billing from the next month.

title: Plans and pricing, effective 1 July 2026
text: This price list applies to all new subscriptions and to all renewals from 1 July 2026, and replaces the price list dated 1 April 2025. All prices are in rupees and exclude GST, which is charged at 18 percent on every subscription invoice. Starter costs ₹449 per month and includes 1 user, 1 company and up to 50 sales invoices per month; e-invoicing and e-way bills are not available on Starter. Growth costs ₹1,199 per month and includes 3 users, 2 companies, up to 500 sales invoices per month, 100 e-invoices per month and 100 e-way bills per month. Pro costs ₹2,499 per month and includes 8 users, 5 companies, unlimited sales invoices, 1,000 e-invoices per month, 1,000 e-way bills per month and multi-currency invoicing. Annual billing is charged at the price of 10 months, so a year of Starter costs ₹4,490, a year of Growth costs ₹11,990 and a year of Pro costs ₹24,990, all plus GST. The invoice limit counts sales invoices only; quotations, purchase bills, credit notes and delivery challans do not count. Unused invoices do not carry forward to the next month. When a company reaches its monthly invoice limit, new sales invoices are blocked until the 1st of the next month or until the plan is upgraded, but existing invoices can still be viewed, edited and shared. Customers who were on the April 2025 prices keep them until their first renewal after 30 September 2026.

title: Plans and pricing, effective 1 April 2025 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 July 2026 by the current price list. This page is kept for reference because some customers are still billed at these prices until their first renewal after 30 September 2026. All prices were in rupees and excluded GST at 18 percent. Starter cost ₹399 per month with 1 user, 1 company and up to 30 sales invoices per month. Growth cost ₹999 per month with 3 users, 2 companies, up to 300 sales invoices per month and 50 e-invoices per month; e-way bills were sold separately at ₹99 for a pack of 50. Pro cost ₹1,999 per month with 10 users, 5 companies, unlimited sales invoices, 500 e-invoices per month and 500 e-way bills per month. Annual billing was offered at the monthly price times 12, less a discount of 15 percent. Under this price list, add-on users cost ₹199 per user per month and were available on Pro only. Multi-currency invoicing was a separate add-on at ₹300 per month on Growth and Pro. Credit notes counted toward the monthly invoice limit under this price list, which was one of the main changes in the July 2026 revision. Customers moving from this price list to the current one at renewal are told by email 30 days in advance.

title: Cancellation and refund policy
text: Monthly plans can be cancelled at any time from Settings, Subscription. When a monthly plan is cancelled, the unused whole days of the current month are refunded pro-rata to the original payment method within 7 working days, and the GST on the refunded amount is reversed through a credit note. Annual plans get a full refund only if they are cancelled within 14 days of the first annual payment. After 14 days, annual plans are not refundable, and the plan stays active until the end of the term. The 14-day window applies once per customer and does not apply to renewals. Add-on users, e-invoice top-up packs, payroll add-on charges and assisted migration fees are never refunded, and no refund is given for unused invoice limits. Refunds to UPI and debit cards usually show within 5 working days of being processed; credit card refunds can take up to one billing cycle. Accounts suspended for non-payment, or terminated for misuse of the service, are not eligible for any refund. Refund requests can also be raised with support by quoting the subscription ID, which starts with the letters LW and is printed on every subscription invoice.

title: Support hours and channels
text: Support channels depend on your plan. Starter has email and in-app chat only, from 10 am to 6 pm, Monday to Saturday; there is no phone support on Starter. Growth has email, chat and phone support from 9 am to 7 pm, Monday to Saturday. Pro has priority phone and chat support from 8 am to 10 pm every day, including Sundays, and accounts with 5 companies get a named account manager. On all plans, chat stays open until 11 pm from the 9th to the 11th and from the 18th to the 20th of each month to cover GST filing dates. Support is closed on Republic Day, Independence Day and Diwali. The support phone number is 1800 309 4521. First response targets are 15 minutes on chat and 1 working day on email; Pro email gets a reply within 4 working hours. Callbacks can be booked in the app for a 30-minute slot. Support is available in English, Hindi, Tamil and Marathi. Our staff will never ask for your password or for an OTP, and you never need to share an OTP to get help; report any such request through the in-app chat.

title: Non-payment, suspension and data retention, effective 1 January 2026
text: This rule took effect on 1 January 2026 and replaces the earlier rule under which lapsed accounts stayed in read-only mode for 60 days. If a renewal is not paid, the account enters a grace period of 7 days, during which everything works normally and a banner shows the amount due. After the grace period the account is suspended. No user, including the Owner and the Accountant login, can sign in, and data cannot be viewed or exported until the dues are cleared. There is no read-only mode. E-invoices and e-way bills cannot be generated during suspension. Paying the dues in full restores access within 30 minutes, with all data intact. Data of a suspended account is retained for 120 days from the date of suspension, and a final notice is sent by email and SMS on day 90. After 120 days, all companies in the account are permanently deleted, including backups, and cannot be recovered. Customers who plan to stop using the service should export their data before the term ends. Within the 120 days, a customer can ask support for a one-time data export of a suspended account without renewing, on payment of a retrieval fee of ₹999 plus GST; the export is delivered as a Full Export within 3 working days.

title: Users, add-on users and accountant access
text: Each plan includes a set number of users, as listed on the current price list. Additional users can be added on Growth and Pro at ₹249 per user per month plus GST; Starter cannot have add-on users and must upgrade. Add-on users are billed for the full calendar month in which they are added, whatever the date, with no proration, and from the next renewal they are billed together with the plan. Removing an add-on user takes effect from the next month, and there is no refund for the current month. Every company on any plan, including Starter, can invite one Accountant login free of charge. The Accountant login does not count toward the user limit. It can view all books, post journal entries, and prepare and file GST returns, but it cannot change billing, delete the company or invite other users. A second accountant from the same firm needs a regular paid user seat. The roles available are Owner, Admin, Staff, Viewer and Accountant. Staff users can create invoices and record payments but cannot see bank balances or payroll. Only the Owner can transfer ownership of an account, which needs an OTP sent to both the old and the new owner's registered mobile numbers. Two-factor login with OTP is mandatory for the Owner and Admin roles and optional for the others.

title: Public API: access, rate limits and tokens
text: The REST API is available on Team, Business and Enterprise; Free workspaces have no API access. Rate limits are 100 requests per minute on Team, 300 requests per minute on Business and 1,000 requests per minute on Enterprise. Limits apply per workspace, not per token: every personal token, service token and connected integration in the workspace shares the same allowance, so creating another token does not add capacity. Requests over the limit receive an HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header. If a token keeps sending requests over the limit for more than 10 minutes, it is suspended for 1 hour. Personal tokens expire after 90 days unless renewed; service tokens, available on Business and Enterprise, do not expire but must be tied to an admin. Each user can hold up to 25 active tokens. Webhooks are retried 5 times over 24 hours if the receiving endpoint does not return a success status, and are disabled after 3 consecutive days of failures. Bulk endpoints accept up to 100 items per request and count as a single request against the limit.

title: Seat billing, proration and invoices
text: Each member in a paid workspace uses one seat. Seats added during a billing period are charged immediately, prorated by the day for the time left in the current monthly or annual period. On monthly billing, seats can be removed at any time, but the lower seat count takes effect at the next monthly renewal and no credit is given for the current month. On annual billing, the number of paid seats can only be reduced at the annual renewal date; removing a member before then frees the seat for someone else to use but does not reduce the charge or produce a refund. Invoices are issued on the renewal date and are paid by credit or debit card. Business workspaces on annual billing and all Enterprise workspaces can pay by bank transfer on 30-day terms. If a card payment fails, the charge is retried 1, 3 and 7 days later, and owners are emailed each time. If an invoice is still unpaid 14 days after the first failed attempt, the workspace becomes read-only until payment is made; nothing is deleted. Tax IDs such as a VAT or GST number can be added in billing settings and appear on future invoices only; past invoices are not reissued.

title: Changing plans: upgrades and downgrades
text: Upgrades take effect immediately, and the price difference for the rest of the billing period is charged straight away, prorated by the day. Downgrades also take effect immediately at the moment they are confirmed, not at the end of the current billing period, so the workspace loses the higher plan's features right away. The unused value of the higher plan for the rest of the period is not refunded to the card; it is added to the workspace as account credit, which is applied automatically to future invoices and expires 12 months after it is issued. If the workspace is over the limits of the new plan, nothing is deleted: boards, files and automations beyond the new limits become read-only or paused until usage is brought under the limit or the workspace upgrades again. Downgrading from Business to Team removes single sign-on, so members who signed in only through SSO must set a password; they are emailed a link that is valid for 72 hours. Owners can downgrade only once in any 30-day period. A downgrade to Free is treated as a cancellation of the paid subscription and follows the cancellation and retention rules.

title: Workspace deletion, data export and retention
text: Only the primary owner can delete a workspace. On Team, Business and Enterprise, a deleted workspace can be restored within 14 days by the owner through a support ticket; after 14 days it is purged. On the Free plan there is no recovery window: a deleted Free workspace is permanently deleted immediately and cannot be restored by support. Items deleted from boards go to the trash and stay there for 30 days on Free and 90 days on paid plans. When a paid subscription is cancelled, the workspace moves to Free at the end of the paid term; content over the Free limits is kept read-only for 180 days, after which the oldest files over the 2 GB storage limit are deleted first. Closed user accounts are deactivated for 30 days, during which the person can sign back in to reopen them, and are then erased. Backups containing deleted data are overwritten within 35 days. Data export: owners and admins on paid plans can export the whole workspace, including boards, tasks, docs, comments and attachments, as a JSON archive from the admin console. On Free, export is only available one board at a time as a CSV file, without attachments. Export links are emailed and expire after 72 hours, and exports over 10 GB are split into parts.

title: Education discount
text: Accredited schools, colleges and universities get 50 percent off the Business plan. The education discount applies to annual billing only and cannot be combined with other offers. Verification needs an institutional email domain and proof of accreditation, and takes up to 5 business days. Teachers and students using a personal workspace for coursework can use the Team plan free for up to 10 seats, renewed every 12 months by verifying again. If the discount is granted after purchase, it applies from the next renewal and is not backdated. Commercial arms of universities, private tutoring businesses and training companies are not eligible. The discount covers up to 500 seats in one workspace; seats beyond that are charged at the standard annual price. The education discount does not apply to Enterprise or to automation top-up packs. Separate rules, with a different discount rate and billing options, apply to registered nonprofits.

title: Nonprofit discount
text: Registered nonprofits and charities get 30 percent off the Team and Business plans, on either monthly or annual billing. Verification needs a registration certificate from the country's charity or nonprofit regulator and takes up to 10 business days. The nonprofit discount does not apply to Enterprise or to automation top-up packs, and political parties, government bodies and organisations whose main activity is religious worship are not eligible. The discount covers up to 200 seats in one workspace; seats beyond that are charged at the standard price. It is applied from the date of approval, and charges made before approval are not refunded. Eligibility must be verified again every 24 months, and the discount ends at the next renewal if it is not. The nonprofit discount cannot be combined with the education discount; an organisation that qualifies for both gets the education discount if it bills annually.

title: Roles, guests and guest billing
text: Every workspace has one primary owner, plus admins, members and guests. Team workspaces are limited to 3 admins; Business and Enterprise have no admin limit. Members are billed seats. Guests are people outside your organisation who are invited to specific projects only; they cannot see the member directory, create projects or join the workspace as a whole. Guest allowances are 2 guests on Free, 1 guest per paid seat on Team, and 5 guests per paid seat on Business; Enterprise has no guest cap. Guest access is free only at viewer or commenter level. A guest who is given editor permission on any project is billed as a full member seat from the next billing cycle, at the same per seat price as other members, and appears on the invoice as a guest editor. Changing the guest back to viewer before the cycle ends avoids the charge. Guest invitations expire after 7 days if they are not accepted, and guests who have not signed in for 90 days are removed from the workspace automatically, although their comments and uploads stay. On Business, only owners and admins can invite guests; on Team, any member can invite guests unless an admin turns this off.

title: Plan limits: storage, file size, automations and boards
text: Storage is pooled across the workspace. Free workspaces get 2 GB in total, Team gets 10 GB per paid seat, Business gets 50 GB per paid seat, and Enterprise storage is unlimited subject to fair use. The maximum size of a single uploaded file is 25 MB on Free, 250 MB on Team, 1 GB on Business and 5 GB on Enterprise; larger files are rejected at upload and should be shared as a link instead. An automation run is counted each time an automation rule completes its actions, so a rule with three actions still counts as one run. Monthly allowances are 100 runs on Free, 2,000 runs on Team, 25,000 runs on Business and 250,000 runs on Enterprise, shared by the whole workspace. Allowances reset at 00:00 UTC on the first day of each calendar month, not on the billing date, and unused runs do not roll over. When the allowance is used up, automations pause until the reset; there is no overage charge. Team and Business workspaces can buy a top-up pack of 5,000 extra runs for $15, valid until the end of the calendar month. Free workspaces are limited to 3 active boards; paid plans have no board limit. Version history for docs is kept for 7 days on Free, 90 days on Team, and indefinitely on Business and Enterprise.

title: Plans and pricing, effective 1 March 2026
text: This price list applies to all new and renewing subscriptions from 1 March 2026 and replaces the price list dated 1 February 2024. All prices are in US dollars per seat and exclude sales tax, VAT or GST, which is added based on the billing country. Free costs $0 and allows up to 5 members in one workspace. Team costs $10 per seat per month on monthly billing, or $8 per seat per month billed annually, which is $96 per seat per year. Team requires a minimum of 3 seats. Business costs $19 per seat per month on monthly billing, or $16 per seat per month billed annually, which is $192 per seat per year, with a minimum of 5 seats. Enterprise is priced by quote, is billed annually only, and requires at least 50 seats. Customers who were on 2024 prices keep them until their first renewal on or after 1 June 2026, after which the new prices apply. Switching from monthly to annual billing can be done at any time and takes effect immediately, with the unused part of the current month credited. Switching from annual to monthly billing is only possible at the annual renewal date. Charges are made in US dollars only; card issuers may add their own foreign transaction fees, which are not refunded.

title: Plans and pricing, effective 1 February 2024 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 March 2026 by the current price list. This page is kept for reference because workspaces that subscribed before 1 March 2026 keep these prices until their first renewal on or after 1 June 2026. Under this price list, Free allowed up to 10 members in one workspace and 5 GB of total storage. Team cost $9 per seat per month on monthly billing, or $7 per seat per month billed annually, with a minimum of 2 seats. Business cost $17 per seat per month on monthly billing, or $14 per seat per month billed annually, with a minimum of 3 seats. Enterprise was priced by quote with a minimum of 25 seats and could be billed monthly or annually. Sales tax, VAT or GST was added on top based on the billing country, as it is today. Annual billing could be switched to monthly billing at any time, with the difference credited to the account. The 2024 price list also included a Starter add-on for single users at $4 per month, which was withdrawn when this list was superseded; existing Starter users were moved to Free with their data kept.

title: Refund policy
text: Monthly subscriptions are not refunded for partial months, whether the workspace is cancelled, downgraded or has members removed. Annual subscriptions can be refunded in full if the owner asks within 14 days of the annual charge; this applies to the first annual purchase and to each automatic annual renewal. After 14 days, annual subscriptions are not refunded, but cancelling stops the next renewal and the workspace keeps its plan until the end of the paid term. Duplicate charges caused by a payment error are refunded in full, whatever the timing, within 5 business days of being reported. Refunds always go back to the original payment method and are issued within 10 business days; how long they take to appear on a statement depends on the card issuer. Automation top-up packs, unused account credit and charges for guest editors are not refundable. Refund requests must come from the workspace owner or a billing admin, through the billing page or a support ticket. If an owner files a card chargeback instead of a refund request, the workspace is set to read-only while the dispute is open. Reminder emails are sent 7 days before every annual renewal.

title: Two-factor authentication, SSO and sign-in security
text: Two-factor authentication (2FA) can use an authenticator app or a hardware security key; codes by SMS are not supported. When 2FA is turned on, the user receives 10 single-use backup codes. Admins on Business and Enterprise can require 2FA for every member. Support staff cannot remove, disable or bypass 2FA on any account, even after identity checks. A member who loses their 2FA device must sign in with a backup code or ask a workspace owner or admin to reset their 2FA from the admin console. If the primary owner loses both their device and their backup codes and there is no other admin, recovery requires proving control of the company email domain by adding a DNS TXT record, and takes up to 5 business days. After 5 failed password attempts in a row, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes; a further 5 failures lock the account until the password is reset by email. SAML single sign-on is available on Business and Enterprise, and SCIM user provisioning is on Enterprise only. Enterprise admins can set session timeouts between 1 hour and 30 days; on other plans, sessions last 14 days.

title: Uptime SLA, service credits and maintenance windows
text: Business and Enterprise subscriptions include an uptime commitment of 99.9 percent per calendar month; Free and Team have no SLA and no service credits. If monthly uptime falls below 99.9 percent, the credit is 10 percent of that month's subscription fee; below 99.0 percent it is 25 percent; below 95.0 percent it is 50 percent, which is the maximum. Credits are not applied automatically: the owner or a billing admin must request them through a support ticket within 30 days after the end of the affected month. Credits are applied to the next invoice and are never paid out as cash or refunded to a card. Downtime does not count if it is caused by scheduled maintenance, by a third-party integration, or by the customer's own network. Scheduled maintenance takes place on Sundays between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC, is announced at least 72 hours ahead on the status page, and is limited to 4 hours a month. During maintenance, boards stay readable but edits and notifications may be delayed by up to 15 minutes. Uptime is measured by external checks every minute from three regions.

title: Support channels and hours by plan
text: Free workspaces get the help centre and community forum only; email tickets from Free workspaces are answered only for billing and account access issues. Team workspaces get email support Monday to Friday, 8 am to 8 pm UTC, with a first response within 24 business hours; there is no weekend support on Team. Business workspaces get email and live chat 24 hours a day, Monday to Friday, with a first response within 8 business hours. Enterprise workspaces get round-the-clock phone, chat and email for Severity 1 issues, meaning the service is down or data is at risk, with a first response within 1 hour, and a first response within 4 business hours for everything else; each Enterprise workspace also has a named customer success manager. Support is in English on all plans, with Spanish, German and Japanese available on Business and Enterprise during local business hours. Support does not cover building custom API integrations or writing automations for customers. Public holidays do not change these hours, except 25 December and 1 January, when only Severity 1 Enterprise support is available.

title: Business plan free trial
text: Any workspace on Free or Team can start one 14-day trial of the Business plan. No credit card is needed to start the trial. Each workspace can trial Business only once, and one extension of 7 days can be granted by the sales team on request. During the trial all Business features are available, except that the automation allowance is limited to 2,500 runs and storage is limited to 20 GB in total. When a trial started from Free ends, the workspace does not drop back to the Free plan automatically. Instead it becomes read-only for 30 days: everyone can view and export content, but nobody can create or edit anything until an owner chooses a paid plan or switches to Free by hand. Switching to Free is only possible once the workspace meets the Free limits, so members beyond 5 and boards beyond 3 must be removed or archived first. If nothing is chosen within the 30 days, the workspace stays read-only; nothing is deleted. A Team workspace that trials Business returns to Team automatically at the end of the trial and keeps its Team billing. Owners are emailed 3 days and 1 day before the trial ends.

title: Refund abuse, account suspension and complaints
text: Accounts are reviewed automatically when they make more than 4 refund claims in 60 days, or when refunds add up to more than 30 percent of the value of their orders over 90 days. While an account is under review, every claim needs a photo and refunds are paid as Brambleway credit only. If a review finds claims that cannot be supported, the first step is a written warning; a second finding within 12 months leads to a 30-day suspension, and a third leads to permanent closure. When an account is closed, promotional credit is forfeited but credit bought as a gift card is refunded. You can appeal a suspension within 14 days by replying to the suspension email. Complaints: raise the problem in chat first; if it is not sorted, ask for it to go to Customer Relations, or call 0161 496 0731 between 9 am and 6 pm, Monday to Friday. Customer Relations acknowledges complaints within 2 working days and sends a final response within 10 working days, or 20 working days for complex cases. If you are still unhappy after the final response, you can refer the complaint free of charge to the independent dispute resolution service named in that response within 8 weeks.

title: Alcohol and other age-restricted items
text: Brambleway Eats operates Challenge 25. Riders must check photo ID at the door for every order containing alcohol, tobacco alternatives, lighter refills or solvents, if the person receiving it looks under 25. Accepted ID is a passport, a photocard driving licence, a proof of age card with the PASS hologram, or a military ID card. The person receiving the order must be 18 or over and must not appear drunk, and the contactless drop option is not available for orders with age-restricted items. If the ID check fails or nobody can show valid ID, the result depends on the order type. For restaurant orders, the rider keeps back only the alcoholic items, which are refunded as Brambleway credit, and hands over the rest of the food. For quick grocery and scheduled grocery orders, the whole order is returned to the hub, because sealed bags cannot be split at the door, and the order is refunded minus a £5 failed ID check fee. Alcohol ordering hours: in England and Wales alcohol can be ordered between 8 am and 11 pm. In Scotland, including Glasgow and Edinburgh, alcohol orders are accepted only between 10 am and 9:30 pm, so that every alcohol delivery is completed by 10 pm.

title: Allergen information and who is responsible
text: Restaurants and grocery suppliers are responsible for the allergen information shown on menus and product pages. Restaurants must be able to tell you which of the 14 major allergens are in a dish, and the allergen details on each menu item are supplied by the restaurant, not checked by Brambleway Eats. Our support team cannot confirm whether a dish is safe for a particular allergy. If you have an allergy, use the Contact restaurant button on the menu page or the order page, which works until the rider collects the order, and ask the restaurant directly. Allergy notes added at checkout are passed to the restaurant but are not a guarantee. Grocery product photos may not show the latest packaging, so always check the label on the item you receive before eating it. If a restaurant gave wrong allergen information, report it under Order help within 24 hours; you will get a full refund to your card and the restaurant will be reviewed. If you have a reaction, get medical help first.

title: Minimum basket rules and small order fee
text: Restaurant orders have no platform minimum, but when the food subtotal is under £12 a small order fee is added to make up the difference to £12, up to a maximum small order fee of £3.00. A restaurant can set its own higher minimum, which is shown at the top of its menu page, and in that case the order cannot be placed below it. Quick grocery orders, which are packed at our neighbourhood hubs and delivered in about 20 to 30 minutes, need a minimum basket of £15, and there is no small order fee option: the checkout will not go through below £15. Scheduled grocery orders, booked in one-hour slots up to 7 days ahead, need a minimum basket of £40, and a basket charge of £1.50 applies to scheduled orders under £60. Alcohol, tobacco alternatives, gift cards and bottle deposit charges do not count towards either grocery minimum. If items are later removed because they are out of stock or rejected substitutes take the basket below the minimum, no extra charge is added after the order has been placed. Click-and-collect orders have a minimum of £5 for both restaurants and hubs, and no small order fee.

title: Click-and-collect
text: Click-and-collect is available from participating restaurants and from every quick grocery hub. There is no delivery fee and a flat service fee of £0.49, and the minimum order is £5. After you order, the app shows a ready time. Restaurant click-and-collect orders are held for 15 minutes after the ready time, and grocery hub orders for 30 minutes. If an order is not picked up in that time it is cancelled and charged in full with no refund, because the food cannot be resold. You can tap I'm running late once per order to add another 10 minutes to the holding time. Someone else can collect for you if you share the 4-digit collection code shown in the app, but orders with age-restricted items can only be collected by the account holder with photo ID. Hubs have a marked collection counter at the front; for restaurants, ask staff for Brambleway collection orders. Collected orders can't be swapped for delivery after the ready time.

title: Delivery and service fees, effective 3 August 2026
text: This fee schedule applies to restaurant and quick grocery delivery orders in every Brambleway Eats city from 3 August 2026 and replaces the fee schedule dated 1 March 2025. The delivery fee depends on the distance between the restaurant or grocery hub and the delivery address: £0.99 for up to 1 mile, £1.99 for 1 to 2.5 miles, £2.99 for 2.5 to 4 miles, and £3.79 for 4 to 6 miles. Orders to addresses more than 6 miles away are not accepted. A busy-period surcharge of £1.00 may be added on Friday and Saturday evenings between 6 pm and 9 pm and whenever a severe weather alert is active; it is always shown before checkout. The service fee is charged on top of the delivery fee and is 9 percent of the basket subtotal, with a minimum of £0.59 and capped at £3.49 per order. Brambleway Plus members pay a reduced service fee of 5 percent on restaurant orders over £15; the service fee is otherwise not waived by membership. Click-and-collect orders have no delivery fee and a flat service fee of £0.49. All fees are refunded in full if an order is cancelled by the restaurant or by Brambleway Eats. If an order arrives more than 30 minutes after the latest time in the delivery estimate, the delivery fee is refunded automatically as Brambleway credit within 24 hours.

title: Delivery and service fees, effective 1 March 2025 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 3 August 2026 by the current delivery and service fee schedule. This page is kept for reference because orders placed before 3 August 2026 were charged on it. Under this schedule the delivery fee was £1.49 for up to 1.5 miles, £2.49 for 1.5 to 3 miles, and £3.49 for 3 to 5 miles, and orders to addresses more than 5 miles away were not accepted. There was no busy-period surcharge. The service fee was 7 percent of the basket subtotal, with a minimum of £0.49 and a cap of £2.99 per order, and it applied in the same way to members and non-members. Click-and-collect orders had no delivery fee and no service fee. Late delivery refunds were not automatic: a customer whose order arrived more than 45 minutes after the latest estimated time could ask for the delivery fee back through chat within 24 hours, and it was refunded as credit. Customers who believe an order placed before the changeover was charged under the wrong schedule can ask for a review through Order help within 30 days of the order date.

title: Substitutions on grocery orders
text: Each item in a quick grocery or scheduled grocery order has a substitution setting: Best match, which is the default, Choose a specific swap, or No substitute. Pickers substitute with a similar item of the same or larger size. If the substitute costs more, you pay the price of the item you ordered; if it costs less, you pay the lower price. Substitutes are listed in the app before the rider leaves the hub and on the receipt. Substitutes can't be handed back to the rider at the door, because riders are not allowed to take returned goods back into the hub. Instead, reject a substitute in the app within 2 hours of delivery and you will get Brambleway credit for the full substitute price; you can keep or dispose of the item. Fresh meat, fish and baby formula are never swapped for a different brand unless you picked Choose a specific swap. Items with a free-from claim, such as gluten free or nut free, are only replaced with items carrying the same claim. If no suitable substitute is in stock, the item is removed and its price is not charged.

title: Restaurant delivery hours by city
text: Restaurant delivery runs from 11 am to 11 pm, Sunday to Thursday, in every city we serve. Late-night restaurant delivery on Friday and Saturday nights runs as follows: Manchester city centre and Leeds until 2 am; Birmingham until 1:30 am; Glasgow and Newcastle until 1 am; Bristol, Cardiff, Nottingham and Edinburgh until midnight. After 11 pm the delivery radius is reduced to 3 miles in every city. Breakfast delivery starts at 7:30 am in Manchester, Leeds and Bristol only. Individual restaurants may keep shorter hours than these, and the app only shows restaurants that are open and within range. On bank holidays restaurant delivery follows Sunday hours. There is no delivery on Christmas Day, and on Boxing Day restaurant delivery starts at 12 noon. These hours are for restaurant orders only; quick grocery hours are set separately for each city.

title: Quick grocery delivery hours by city
text: Quick grocery orders are packed at our neighbourhood hubs and delivered in about 20 to 30 minutes. In Manchester and Leeds, quick grocery delivery runs from 7 am to midnight every day. In Glasgow and Birmingham it runs from 8 am to 11 pm every day. In Bristol, Cardiff, Newcastle, Nottingham and Edinburgh it runs from 8 am to 10 pm, Sunday to Thursday, and until 11 pm on Friday and Saturday. Alcohol can only be ordered within the alcohol ordering hours, which are shorter in Scotland. Scheduled grocery slots, booked up to 7 days ahead, run in one-hour slots from 8 am to 10 pm in every city. Hubs are closed on Christmas Day and open from 10 am to 6 pm on Boxing Day and New Year's Day. When a hub is very busy the app may pause quick grocery ordering for up to 30 minutes and offer the next scheduled slot instead. These hours are for grocery orders only; restaurant delivery hours are listed separately.

title: Brambleway Plus membership: price, benefits and cancellation
text: Brambleway Plus costs £7.99 a month or £69 a year, billed in advance on the day you join and on the same date each period. Members get free delivery on restaurant orders over £15 and on quick grocery orders over £25, a reduced restaurant service fee of 5 percent on orders over £15, and priority chat support. The busy-period surcharge still applies to members. Free delivery does not apply to restaurants marked as own delivery or to scheduled grocery slots on Saturdays. You can cancel at any time under Account, then Plus. Cancellation takes effect immediately: member benefits stop at the moment you cancel, not at the end of the period you have already paid for, so orders placed after cancelling are charged standard fees. Monthly members get no refund for the unused part of the month. Annual members who cancel within 14 days of a renewal payment, and have not used any member benefit since that renewal, get a full refund to their card; after that, annual members get a pro-rata refund as Brambleway credit, minus a £10 admin charge. Monthly members can pause instead of cancelling, for 1 or 2 months, once in any 12-month period; no fee is taken and no benefits apply while paused.

title: Changing or cancelling an order after it is placed
text: Restaurant orders can be cancelled free of charge until the restaurant accepts the order, which usually happens within 2 to 4 minutes. Once the restaurant has accepted, cancelling is charged at 50 percent of the food subtotal, and once the rider has collected the order it cannot be cancelled and is charged in full. Items cannot be added to a restaurant order after it is placed; place a separate order instead. The delivery address can be changed in the app only before the rider collects the order, and only to an address within 1 mile of the original; if the new address falls in a higher distance band, the difference in delivery fee is charged. Any other address change has to be cancelled and re-ordered under the rules above. Quick grocery orders can be cancelled free until picking starts, usually within 2 minutes, and cost £2.50 to cancel after that; they cannot be edited once placed. Scheduled grocery orders can be edited, with items added or removed, until 11 pm the night before for slots starting before noon, or until 3 hours before the slot start for later slots, and can be cancelled free up to the same cut-off.

title: Promo codes, referral credit and the Plus free trial
text: New customers get a welcome code worth £8 off their first restaurant order, with a minimum spend of £20 on food, not counting fees or tips. The code must be used within 14 days of creating the account. Only one promo code can be used per order, and codes can't be combined, but a code can be used together with Plus free delivery. Discounts apply to the food or grocery subtotal only, never to fees or tips, and codes cannot be used on alcohol in Scotland. If you cancel an order that used a code, the code is not reinstated; if the restaurant or Brambleway Eats cancels it, the code is reinstated within 24 hours. Referral credit: when a friend joins with your link and completes a first order over £15, you both get £5 credit, up to 10 referrals a year. Plus free trial: new members can try Brambleway Plus free for 30 days. The trial does not roll into a paid membership automatically; when the 30 days end the benefits stop, and you are only charged if you choose to continue by tapping Keep Plus. One free trial is allowed per person, payment card and delivery address.

title: Missing, damaged or incorrect items: reporting and refunds
text: Report missing, damaged, spilled or incorrect items in the app under Order help. Restaurant order problems must be reported within 24 hours of delivery; quick grocery and scheduled grocery problems must be reported within 72 hours. For damaged or spilled items a photo of the item and its packaging is required. By default, approved refunds are paid as Brambleway credit, which appears in your account straight away and can be used on any order within 12 months. A refund goes back to the original card only if you choose Refund to card when reporting the problem, or if you ask within 7 days of the credit being issued and the credit is still unused; card refunds take 3 to 5 working days to appear. Brambleway credit cannot be withdrawn as cash. If a whole order never arrives, the full amount, including fees and tip, is refunded to the original payment method automatically. For food that arrives cold or late but is otherwise correct, the refund is limited to the delivery fee unless the food is unsafe to eat. Claims for more than £40 on a single order are checked by a specialist within 2 working days before any refund is made.

title: Rider tips, contactless drop and waiting time
text: Tips are optional. You can add a tip at checkout, or afterwards from the order page for up to 48 hours after the order is delivered.
