A tip added at checkout can be changed or removed until 1 hour after delivery. The maximum in-app tip is £20 per order. 100 percent of every tip goes to the rider and is paid with their weekly earnings; Brambleway Eats takes no fee from tips. Tips are not refunded when part of an order is refunded, only when the whole order never arrives. Cash tips are also fine. Contactless drop: choose Leave at door at checkout, and the rider will leave the order at your door, knock or ring, take a photo and step back at least 2 metres. Contactless drop is not available for orders with age-restricted items. In blocks of flats, riders deliver to the flat door only if they are let into the building; orders are never left in shared lobbies. If you don't answer, the rider waits 8 minutes at the address and tries to call you twice. After 8 minutes the order is returned, marked as delivered, and is not refunded, unless you chose Leave at door, in which case it is left at the door.

title: Order cancellation and the late delivery guarantee
text: You can cancel any restaurant order free of charge within 60 seconds of placing it. After 60 seconds, once the restaurant has accepted the order, a cancellation fee of 50 percent of the item value is charged, and once the delivery partner has picked up the order it cannot normally be cancelled and no refund is given. Late delivery guarantee: if your order has not been delivered within 20 minutes after the latest arrival time shown at checkout, you can cancel it from the order screen for a full refund, including delivery fees and taxes, even if the food has already been picked up. The guarantee does not apply when heavy rain mode is on, to scheduled orders, or when the delay is caused by a wrong address, a changed address or a customer who could not be reached. If you choose to wait instead of cancelling, you receive ₹50 in promotional wallet credit once the late order is delivered. For prepaid orders, refunds from a cancellation follow the refund rules, which credit the wallet by default. For cash on delivery orders, a cancellation fee is added to your next order, and two cancelled or refused cash orders within 90 days switch off cash on delivery for the account.

title: Missing, wrong or spilled items: how to claim
text: Report a missing item or a wrong item through Help within 2 hours of delivery. Report a spill, leak or damaged packaging within 30 minutes of delivery, with at least one photo that shows the packaging as it arrived and the affected food. Claims for spills without a photo, or reported after 30 minutes, are not accepted. Approved claims are refunded as follows: a missing or wrong item is refunded at the item price plus its share of taxes and packaging; a spill is refunded for the affected items only, unless the tamper-proof seal on the bag was broken, in which case the whole order is refunded. Claims above ₹500 are checked by a person and decided within 24 hours; smaller claims are usually decided automatically. All claim refunds follow the refund rules and are credited to the wallet by default. Complaints about taste, spice level or portion size are not refundable, but they are passed to the restaurant and a goodwill credit of up to ₹75 may be given. Accounts that make more than 4 claims within 30 days are reviewed manually before further claims are approved.

title: Allergen and dietary labels on menus
text: Every dish on a restaurant menu carries a vegetarian, non-vegetarian or contains-egg marker. In addition, restaurants must tag eight allergens where present: peanuts, tree nuts, milk, gluten, egg, soy, fish or shellfish, and sesame. Allergen tags are shown in red under the dish name and in the dish details. A "may contain traces" note is added when a restaurant prepares the dish in a kitchen that also handles peanuts or tree nuts. A Jain tag means the dish is made without onion, garlic, potatoes or other root vegetables. All labels are declared by the restaurant itself and are checked by our team in a quarterly audit, not for each order. Allergy requests written in the cooking instructions box are passed to the restaurant but are not guaranteed, and a claim cannot be made because a cooking instruction was not followed. If a dish contained one of the eight tagged allergens that was not declared on the menu, you receive a full refund of the order and the dish is removed until the restaurant corrects its label. Customers with severe allergies are advised to contact the restaurant before ordering.

title: Restaurant delivery fees by distance, effective 1 July 2026
text: This delivery fee schedule applies to all restaurant orders in every city we serve with effect from 1 July 2026, and replaces the schedule dated 1 March 2025. The delivery fee depends on the road distance from the restaurant to your delivery address, as calculated by the app at checkout, not on the route the delivery partner actually takes. Up to 3 km the delivery fee is ₹25; from 3 to 6 km it is ₹39; from 6 to 8 km it is ₹55. In Bengaluru and Hyderabad, where the delivery radius goes up to 10 km, orders beyond 8 km pay ₹55 plus ₹8 for each additional km. The fee shown at checkout is locked once the order is placed and is never increased afterwards, even if the partner is rerouted. Orders placed between 11 pm and 6 am carry a separate late-night fee of ₹30, on top of the distance fee. Thali Club members pay no distance fee on restaurant orders above ₹199 within 7 km, but the late-night fee still applies to members. Delivery fees for tiffin plans are included in the plan price and are not charged per meal. GST at 18 percent is charged on the delivery fee and is shown as a separate line on the bill.

title: Restaurant delivery fees by distance, effective 1 March 2025 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 July 2026 by the current delivery fee schedule. This page is kept for reference so that support agents can explain older bills. Under this schedule the delivery fee was based on road distance from the restaurant: up to 2 km the fee was ₹20; from 2 to 5 km it was ₹35; from 5 to 8 km it was ₹49. Orders beyond 8 km were not accepted in any city. The late-night fee for orders placed between 11 pm and 6 am was ₹25. Thali Club members paid no distance fee on restaurant orders above ₹149 within 5 km. Delivery fees for orders placed before 1 July 2026 but scheduled for delivery on or after that date were charged under this old schedule, because the fee is fixed at the moment of booking. Customers who believe they were charged the new fee on such an order can raise it through Help within 30 days and the difference is refunded to the wallet. The rain surcharge and small-order fee were not part of this schedule and were set by separate notices at the time.

title: Small-order fee, platform fee and surcharges
text: A small-order fee of ₹30 is added when the item subtotal of a restaurant order is below ₹149. The subtotal is counted after restaurant discounts but before coupon codes and wallet credits. The small-order fee is charged to Thali Club members too; membership does not waive it. A platform fee of ₹6 is charged on every restaurant order and is not charged on tiffin plan meals. When heavy rain mode is switched on for a delivery zone, a rain surcharge is added: ₹20 for orders up to 4 km and ₹35 for orders above 4 km. The rain surcharge is shown with an umbrella icon before you pay and applies to members as well, because it is paid in full to the delivery partner. In Bengaluru and Pune only, a peak-hour surcharge of up to ₹15 may apply between 8 pm and 10:30 pm on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays; members do not pay the peak-hour surcharge. Packaging charges are set by each restaurant and passed on unchanged. GST on food is 5 percent and is collected by us on behalf of the restaurant; the platform fee, the small-order fee and all surcharges attract GST at 18 percent.

title: Service cities, delivery radius and late-night hours
text: Restaurant delivery is available in Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kochi and Indore. The maximum distance between the restaurant and your address depends on the city: 7 km in Pune, 10 km in Bengaluru, 10 km in Hyderabad, 6 km in Kochi and 6 km in Indore. Restaurants further away than this are hidden from your search results. Ordering hours also vary by city. In Pune, orders are accepted from 6 am to 1 am. In Hyderabad and Bengaluru, orders are accepted from 6 am to 2 am, and in the Koramangala, Indiranagar and HSR Layout zones of Bengaluru delivery runs 24 hours. In Kochi, orders are accepted from 7 am to 12:30 am, and in Indore from 7 am to midnight. Orders placed between 11 pm and 6 am carry the late-night fee in every city. During heavy rain mode the radius in any city may be reduced to 4 km for safety. Tiffin plans are only available in Pune, Bengaluru and Indore. Pick-up orders, where you collect the food from the restaurant yourself, are available in all five cities at no delivery fee.

title: Thali Club membership: price, benefits and cancellation
text: Thali Club is our paid membership. It costs ₹149 per month or ₹1,199 for a 12-month plan, paid upfront. Benefits: no distance delivery fee on restaurant orders above ₹199 within 7 km, an extra 10 percent off up to ₹60 per order at restaurants marked with the Club badge, no peak-hour surcharge, and priority chat support. Members still pay the small-order fee, the rain surcharge, the late-night fee and the platform fee. Benefits do not apply to tiffin plans or to pick-up orders. The membership renews automatically and a reminder is sent 3 days before each renewal. Cancelling a monthly plan stops the next renewal; benefits continue to the end of the current month and the current month is not refunded. Cancelling a 12-month plan works differently: the membership ends on the day you cancel, and you receive a pro-rata refund of ₹99 for each unused full month, paid to the original payment method within 7 working days. Part months are not refunded. A 12-month plan bought with a promotional discount is refunded at the discounted monthly value. One account can hold only one membership, and it cannot be transferred or shared with another phone number.

title: Scheduled orders and tipping
text: Scheduled orders can be placed up to 2 days in advance, in 30-minute delivery slots between 8 am and 10 pm. Scheduled orders must be prepaid, and the price and fees at the time of booking are locked. A scheduled order can be cancelled free of charge until 45 minutes before the start of its slot; after that it cannot be cancelled and no refund is given. Scheduled orders are not covered by the late delivery guarantee, but if one arrives more than 30 minutes after the end of its slot you receive ₹75 in promotional wallet credit. Tipping: you can add a tip of ₹10, ₹20 or ₹30, or a custom amount up to ₹200, at checkout or from the order screen until the delivery partner has picked up the order. Once the order is picked up a tip cannot be added or changed, and there is no option to tip after delivery; you can rate and compliment the partner instead. The full tip goes to the delivery partner. If an order is cancelled before pickup, the tip is refunded along with the rest of the order.

title: Payment methods and cash on delivery rules, effective 1 August 2026
text: Orders can be paid by UPI, debit or credit card, net banking or wallet credits, or by cash on delivery. These rules replace the cash on delivery rules of 2024, which allowed cash orders up to ₹3,000. Cash on delivery is available for restaurant orders with a total bill of up to ₹2,000. It is not available for tiffin plans, for scheduled orders, or for orders placed between 11 pm and 6 am. Cash on delivery means cash only: delivery partners are not allowed to accept UPI, cards or any personal payment link at the door. If you would like to pay digitally after choosing cash, use the Pay now button on the order screen before the partner arrives, which converts the order to prepaid. Partners carry change for up to ₹200, so please keep smaller notes ready for larger bills. Cash on delivery is switched off for 90 days on any account with two cancelled or refused cash orders within 90 days, and it is not offered to new accounts until the first prepaid order has been delivered. Card payments made through the app carry no extra fee, and international cards are accepted only in Bengaluru and Kochi.

title: Refund methods and timelines
text: All refunds on prepaid orders, whether from a cancellation, a missing item or an approved claim, are credited to your in-app wallet by default within 2 hours. This is the default even if you paid by credit card or UPI. If you would rather have the money back on the original payment method, choose refund to source in Help within 48 hours of the wallet credit; after 48 hours the amount stays in the wallet. Refund to source timelines are: UPI within 2 working days, net banking 5 to 7 working days, and debit and credit cards 7 to 10 working days. Once a refund to source is processed we share a reference number in the app that you can give to your bank. Refunds under ₹20 are always credited to the wallet and cannot be sent to source. For cash on delivery orders the refund goes to the wallet, or to a UPI ID you give us, which takes up to 3 working days. Membership refunds are the only exception to the wallet default and always go to the original payment method. Refunds are never paid in cash by delivery partners.

title: Contacting your delivery partner and escalating complaints
text: You can call your delivery partner from the order screen once the partner has picked up the order, and until 10 minutes after delivery. Calls go through a masked number, so neither side sees the other's real phone number, and calls are recorded for safety and quality. You can also send preset chat messages to the partner, such as gate codes. Chat support is available 24 hours a day in the app, and phone support on 1800 309 4455 is open from 8 am to 11 pm. If a complaint is not resolved by chat or phone within 72 hours, you can escalate it to the Grievance Officer from the Help section, quoting your ticket number. The Grievance Officer acknowledges every escalation within 48 hours and gives a final decision within 15 days. Escalations about safety, harassment or a partner's behaviour skip the 72-hour wait and are passed to the Grievance Officer at once. Our Grievance Officer is based at the Pune head office, and written complaints can also be posted there. Customers who are not satisfied with the final decision may approach the consumer commission for their district.

title: Home tiffin plans for residential addresses
text: Home tiffin plans deliver home-style meals to residential addresses in Pune, Bengaluru and Indore. Meals are delivered Monday to Saturday; there is no delivery on Sundays. A weekly plan of 6 lunches costs ₹720 for vegetarian and ₹900 for non-vegetarian meals, and a monthly plan of 24 meals costs ₹2,640 for vegetarian and ₹3,360 for non-vegetarian. Plans can be lunch only, dinner only or both. Lunch is delivered between 12 noon and 1:30 pm and dinner between 7:30 pm and 9 pm. To skip a lunch, skip it in the app by 9 pm on the previous day; to skip a dinner, skip it by 11 am on the same day. Meals skipped before the cutoff are not charged and extend the plan end date by one meal; meals skipped after the cutoff are charged in full. A monthly plan allows up to 6 skips. You can also pause a plan for up to 10 consecutive days once per plan. If you cancel a home plan, unused meals are refunded to the wallet minus a ₹99 cancellation charge.

title: Office tiffin plans for workplace addresses
text: Office tiffin plans deliver lunch to workplace addresses in Pune, Bengaluru and Indore, Monday to Friday only, and meals are left at the reception or the pantry desk. A plan of 20 lunches costs ₹2,300 for vegetarian and ₹2,900 for non-vegetarian meals. Lunch is delivered between 12:30 pm and 1:30 pm. To skip a lunch on an office plan, skip it in the app by 8 am on the same day. Meals skipped before the cutoff are not charged and extend the plan end date; meals skipped after the cutoff are charged in full. An office plan allows up to 8 skips, and public holidays declared by the state are skipped automatically without counting towards that limit. Office plans cannot be paused; instead, use skips. Dinner is not offered on office plans. If you cancel an office plan, unused meals are refunded to the wallet minus a ₹149 cancellation charge. A home plan and an office plan can run on the same account at the same time, but each needs its own delivery address and is billed separately.

title: Wallet credits: types, use and expiry
text: The wallet holds two kinds of credit. Refund credits come from cancellations, missing items and approved claims. Promotional credits come from cashback offers, late delivery compensation and goodwill gestures. Refund credits expire 180 days after the date they are credited, and promotional credits expire 30 days after they are credited unless the offer states a shorter period. A reminder is sent by SMS and app notification 7 days before any credit expires, and expired credits cannot be reinstated by support. Wallet credits are applied automatically at checkout unless you switch this off on the payment screen. Refund credits can pay for the full order value, but promotional credits can cover at most 20 percent of the item subtotal of any one order. Wallet credits can be used for restaurant orders and tiffin plans but not to buy or renew a Thali Club membership. The maximum wallet balance is ₹10,000; refunds that would take you above this limit are sent to the original payment method instead. Wallet balances cannot be transferred to another account and cannot be withdrawn to a bank account, except through the refund to source option available within 48 hours of a refund.

title: Application fees and deadlines, 2027-28 intakes
text: These rules apply to applications for September 2027 and January 2028 and replace the 2026-27 application rules. The application fee is $85 for domestic applicants and $150 for international applicants. It is non-refundable and covers up to three programme choices on one application; choices can be changed free of charge until an offer is made. Degree programmes and the Practical Nursing diploma have a fixed deadline of 1 February 2027 for September; complete applications received by that date are given equal consideration, and later applications are considered only if seats remain after the first round of offers on 15 March. All other diploma programmes use rolling admission: files are assessed in the order they are completed, a decision is sent within 4 weeks of a complete file, and programmes close when full. International applicants for any September programme must apply by 1 May 2027 so there is time to obtain a study permit; for January 2028 the international deadline is 15 September 2027 and the domestic deadline is 1 November 2027. January intakes are offered for diploma programmes only. Applicants who were refused in the previous cycle may reapply once at a reduced fee of $25.

title: Application fees and deadlines, 2026-27 intakes (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 October 2026 by the application rules for the 2027-28 intakes; kept for reference for applications made under the old rules. For September 2026 and January 2027 the application fee was $75 for domestic applicants and $125 for international applicants, non-refundable, and each application covered one programme choice only; a second choice needed a second fee. Degree programmes had a fixed deadline of 15 February 2026. All diploma programmes, including Practical Nursing, used rolling admission and stayed open until full. International applicants for September had to apply by 15 May 2026. Decisions on complete diploma files were sent within 6 weeks. There was no reduced reapplication fee. Applications submitted before 1 October 2026 for the January 2027 intake continue to be processed under these rules, including the one-choice limit.

title: Entrance scholarships and bursaries, 2027 intake
text: Entrance scholarships are awarded automatically to domestic applicants based on the admission average used for their offer; no separate application is needed. An average of 85 to 89.9 percent receives $1,500 and an average of 90 percent or higher receives $2,500. International applicants with an equivalent average of 80 percent or higher automatically receive an International Entrance Award of $2,000. Awards are applied as a tuition credit, half in the fall term and half in the winter term, and the student must be enrolled full time in the first year. Entrance scholarships are not renewable. Bursaries are based on financial need and require an application in the student portal. The fall bursary window runs from 1 September to 30 September and the winter window from 15 January to 5 February. Bursaries are up to $1,200 per term. Domestic students must have applied for provincial student aid before applying for a bursary; international students can apply for the International Student Emergency Bursary of up to $800 once per year. Bursary results are released within three weeks of the window closing.

title: Transfer credit and prior learning assessment
text: Transfer credit is granted for courses completed at a recognised post-secondary institution with a grade of C (60 percent) or higher, where the course matches at least 75 percent of the learning outcomes of an Institute course. Programme-specific courses must have been completed within the last 7 years; general education courses such as English, psychology or sociology are accepted within the last 10 years. There is no fee for a transfer credit assessment. Requests must be made through the student portal by the end of the second week of the term in which the course is scheduled. Prior learning assessment and recognition covers learning from work and life experience. It is done by challenge exam or by portfolio, and the fee is $120 per course, payable before the assessment is booked and not refundable if the assessment is unsuccessful. Each course can be challenged once. Combined transfer credit and prior learning credit cannot exceed 50 percent of a programme's credits; at least half must be completed at the Institute to receive the credential. Practical Nursing clinical placements cannot be challenged.

title: Accepting an offer: confirmation deposit and deferral (domestic applicants)
text: Domestic applicants accept an offer by paying a confirmation deposit of $500 within 30 days of the offer date; if the deposit is not received, the seat is released to the next applicant. The deposit is credited in full to first-term tuition. It is fully refundable if you withdraw your acceptance in writing before 1 July for a September start or before 1 November for a January start; after those dates it is non-refundable. Offers to diploma programmes cannot be deferred. An applicant who wants to start in a later intake must decline the offer and reapply, paying the application fee again, and admission is not guaranteed. Offers to degree programmes can be deferred once, for up to 12 months, if the request is made before 15 August; the deposit is carried over and the original admission average is used. Entrance scholarships are not carried over when a degree offer is deferred; the applicant is reassessed in the year they start. International applicants should see the international admissions page for tuition deposit rules, which differ.

title: English language proficiency requirements, effective 1 September 2026
text: This policy applies to all applications received from 1 September 2026 and replaces the English language requirements issued in March 2024. Applicants whose first language is not English must show English proficiency unless they completed at least three consecutive years of full-time study in English in a country where English is the main language, ending no more than five years before the programme start date. Approved academic English tests scored on a nine-band scale: diploma programmes need an overall score of 5.5 with no band below 5.0; degree programmes and the Practical Nursing diploma need 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0. For approved internet-based tests scored out of 120, diploma programmes need 60 and degree and Practical Nursing programmes need 84. Applicants may also sit the Institute's own English Placement Assessment on campus or online for a fee of $60; its result is valid only for admission to the Institute. Test results are accepted if the test was taken no more than three years before the application date. Band scores from two sittings of the same approved test taken within six months of each other may be combined, using the best score in each band, to meet the requirement. Applicants who narrowly miss the requirement may be offered a place with the 12-week English Pathway term starting in May.

title: English language requirements, March 2024 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded by the English language proficiency requirements effective 1 September 2026, and kept for applicants assessed before that date. Under the March 2024 rules, diploma programmes required an overall score of 6.0 on an approved academic nine-band test with no band below 5.5, and degree programmes required 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Internet-based test minimums were 70 for diplomas and 84 for degrees. Test results were valid for two years from the test date, and every band score had to come from a single sitting; scores from different sittings could not be combined. The exemption for study in English required four years of full-time study in an English-speaking country. There was no in-house English Placement Assessment and no English Pathway term; applicants who missed the requirement were refused and asked to reapply with new scores.

title: Diploma programme admission requirements, 2027 intake
text: These requirements apply to all two-year and three-year diploma programmes starting in September 2027 or January 2028. Applicants need a high school diploma or an equivalent such as a high school equivalency certificate, with an overall average of at least 62 percent in their top six Grade 12 courses. Grade 12 English with a final grade of 60 percent or higher is required for every diploma. Additional course requirements by programme: Civil Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering Technology and Computer Systems Technology need Grade 12 mathematics (any stream) at 60 percent or higher. The Practical Nursing diploma needs Grade 12 Biology at 65 percent or higher and Grade 11 Chemistry at 60 percent or higher, and admitted students must provide a vulnerable sector police check dated within 6 months before the first clinical placement. Business Administration, Culinary Arts and Early Childhood Education have no additional course requirements, although Early Childhood Education students also need a vulnerable sector police check. Applicants who are missing one required course can be given a conditional offer if they complete the Institute's free Academic Upgrading module for that subject before 15 August. Current Grade 12 students are assessed on their midterm or Grade 11 final grades and receive a conditional offer; the final transcript must reach the admissions office by 15 July. The Practical Nursing diploma admits 48 students per year at the Fallowmere campus only.

title: Bachelor's degree admission requirements, 2027 intake
text: These requirements apply to the four-year applied degrees starting in September 2027: the Bachelor of Applied Technology in Construction Management, the Bachelor of Business Administration (Applied), and the Bachelor of Applied Science in Environmental Monitoring. Degree programmes start in September only; there is no January intake. Applicants need a high school diploma with an overall average of at least 72 percent in their top six Grade 12 courses, and Grade 12 English at 65 percent or higher. Construction Management and Environmental Monitoring also need Grade 12 pre-calculus mathematics at 65 percent or higher; Environmental Monitoring also needs one Grade 12 science (Biology, Chemistry or Physics) at 65 percent or higher. Business Administration (Applied) needs Grade 12 mathematics in any stream at 60 percent or higher. Unlike diploma programmes, degree programmes do not give conditional offers to applicants who are missing a required course; the course must be completed before the application deadline. Graduates of a related two-year diploma from the Institute with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher can enter the third year of the matching degree directly through a bridging term held in May and June. Graduates of related diplomas from other colleges are assessed course by course for transfer credit instead.

title: Tuition fees and instalment plans, 2027-28
text: Annual tuition for 2027-28, covering the fall and winter terms: domestic diploma programmes $4,380; domestic degree programmes $6,950; international diploma programmes $16,800; international degree programmes $19,400. Practical Nursing carries an additional clinical fee of $650 per year. Ancillary fees of $1,120 per year cover the student association, the town transit pass and the health and dental plan; students with equivalent coverage may opt out of the health and dental part ($310) by 20 September. Fall term fees are due 15 August and winter term fees are due 10 December. Domestic students may pay each term in three instalments, at registration, on 15 October and on 15 November for fall (or at registration, 15 February and 15 March for winter), for a plan fee of $40 per term; no interest is charged. International students pay their first term in full through the tuition deposit and the balance due 15 August, and may use the instalment plan from their second term onward. A late payment fee of $75 per term applies to any missed due date or instalment, and a registration hold blocks timetable and transcript access until the balance is paid.

title: Residence: application, rates and campuses, 2027-28
text: Residence applications open in the student portal once you accept your offer of admission. A residence deposit of $300 is required with the application and is applied to the first term's residence fee; it is refundable less $50 if you cancel before 15 June. First-year students who apply by 1 June are guaranteed a room at the Fallowmere campus; later applicants are placed in order of application as rooms become free. Fallowmere has two halls, Riverside Hall and Quarry Hall. Rates per term are $3,100 for a shared double room and $3,950 for a single room, and a meal plan of $1,700 per term is mandatory for all Fallowmere residents. The Pine Hollow campus has 60 single rooms in Larch House at $3,300 per term with shared kitchens and no meal plan, available only to students whose programme is taught at Pine Hollow. Residence agreements are signed one term at a time, not for the full academic year: a student who gives written notice by 15 November can leave at the end of the fall term and owes nothing for winter. Residents moving in for fall can arrive from 30 August; residences stay open over the winter break for a fee of $20 per night.

title: International applicants: transcripts, tuition deposit and letter of acceptance
text: International applicants upload copies of their secondary or post-secondary transcripts with the application, and if documents are not in English, a certified English translation must be attached. The Institute evaluates all international credentials in-house, free of charge; a credential evaluation report from an outside agency is not required and is not used for admission. Decisions are normally sent within 3 to 6 weeks of a complete file. To accept an offer, international applicants pay a tuition deposit of $6,000, which is credited to first-term tuition. The official letter of acceptance needed for a study permit application is issued within 10 business days after the deposit clears. The deposit is refunded less a $500 administration fee if the study permit is refused and the refusal letter is sent to the Institute before the end of the second week of classes; otherwise it is non-refundable once the letter of acceptance has been issued. If the study permit has not been approved in time, an international student may defer once to the next intake of the same programme at no cost, including diploma programmes, and the deposit is held. International students must be in Canada and attend classes by the end of the second week of term, or their registration is cancelled.

title: Mature applicant entry, conditional offers and admission appeals
text: Applicants who do not have a high school diploma can apply as mature applicants to diploma programmes if they will be at least 20 years old by the first day of classes and have been out of full-time secondary school for at least one year. Mature applicants complete an academic placement assessment in English and mathematics, which costs $45 and can be taken once every 30 days; the result replaces the Grade 12 course requirements for most diplomas. Mature entry is not available for degree programmes or for the Practical Nursing diploma, which require the listed courses. Conditional offers are withdrawn if final grades are below the required level or the final transcript is not received by 15 July. Applicants who are refused or whose offer is withdrawn may request a reconsideration within 10 business days of the decision. Requests are made in writing to the Registrar with a $40 fee, which is refunded if the decision is changed. Reconsideration is only granted for a procedural error in the assessment or for new information, such as updated grades, that was not available at the time of the decision. A decision is given within 15 business days and is final.

title: Orientation dates, admissions office hours and campus visits
text: Fall 2027 orientation: international students attend a mandatory international orientation on Wednesday 1 and Thursday 2 September 2027, and all new students attend New Student Day on Friday 3 September. Classes begin on Tuesday 7 September 2027, after Labour Day. Winter 2028 orientation is on Thursday 6 January 2028 and classes begin Monday 10 January. Students who miss New Student Day must complete the online orientation module before the end of the first week. The admissions office is in Room 140 of the Student Services Building at the Fallowmere campus and is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, with extended hours until 7 pm on Thursdays from February to August. It is closed on weekends and statutory holidays. The Pine Hollow campus admissions desk is open Tuesdays and Thursdays only, 10 am to 3 pm. The admissions line is 1-888-555-0142. Guided campus tours run at 10 am on Saturdays in October and March at Fallowmere and must be booked at least 48 hours ahead; self-guided tour maps are available at the front desk on weekdays.

title: Withdrawal and tuition refund schedule
text: Students who withdraw from their programme must submit the withdrawal form in the student portal; the date the form is submitted is the withdrawal date used for refunds. Stopping attendance or not paying is not a withdrawal and does not reduce fees owed. Refunds of tuition for a term, other than the non-refundable part of any deposit, are calculated as follows. Withdrawal before the first day of classes: 100 percent. During the first week of classes: 70 percent. During the second week: 50 percent. During the third week: 25 percent. From the fourth week onward: no refund. Ancillary fees are refunded in full up to the end of the second week and not after. The Practical Nursing clinical fee is non-refundable once the first placement has started. Weeks are counted from the first scheduled day of classes in the term, not from the student's first class. International students who withdraw after classes begin receive the same percentages, and the Institute is required to report the withdrawal to immigration authorities. Refunds are paid to the original payment method within 30 days.

title: B.Tech admissions 2026: eligibility and entrance test
text: For the B.Tech batch starting in July 2026, applicants must have passed class twelve with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, along with one of Chemistry, Computer Science or Biotechnology. They need at least 60 percent aggregate in Physics, Mathematics and the best of the third subject; the minimum is 55 percent for SC, ST and OBC non-creamy layer candidates of the state. Students awaiting class twelve results may apply and take the test, but admission is confirmed only when the marksheet is submitted. The university's Admission Aptitude Test (AAT) is compulsory for all B.Tech applicants. Scores from national or state engineering entrance examinations are not accepted in place of the AAT, although they may be listed on the form for information. The AAT is a 150-minute computer-based test with 120 questions in Mathematics, Physics and logical reasoning, with negative marking of one quarter mark. Seats in each branch are filled in order of AAT rank, subject to the eligibility marks above. Candidates may take the AAT in both admission rounds; the better score is used.

title: Admissions office hours and campus visits
text: The admissions office in the Administrative Block is open from 9:30 am to 5 pm, Monday to Saturday. During the counselling weeks from 1 April to 31 July, it is also open on Sundays from 10 am to 2 pm for walk-in enquiries and document verification. Guided campus tours run at 11 am and 3 pm on working days and must be booked at least one day in advance by phone; Sunday visitors can see the campus but there are no guided tours on Sundays. The admissions helpline is open from 9 am to 7 pm daily during counselling weeks and from 9:30 am to 5 pm otherwise. Visitors' vehicles are parked at Gate 2; private vehicles are not allowed inside the academic zone. Parents attending counselling should bring the student's original documents and two sets of photocopies. The university information centre at the Meerapur railway station is open on weekdays only.

title: Documents for reporting day and provisional admission
text: On reporting day, admitted students bring originals and two sets of self-attested photocopies of: class ten and class twelve marksheets and certificates, the transfer certificate from the last institution, the migration certificate if the student studied under a board or university outside the state, the AAT scorecard where applicable, a government photo ID, six passport-size photographs, and a medical fitness certificate. Students claiming a reserved seat must produce a category certificate issued on or after 1 April 2025, even for categories where the certificate itself has no expiry. If the migration certificate is not ready, the student gets provisional admission and must submit it within 60 days of reporting, after which the provisional admission is cancelled and fees are refunded as per the refund policy. The anti-ragging undertaking by the student and a parent must be submitted online before reporting. Originals are checked and returned on the spot.

title: Tuition fees and payment rules, 2026 batch
text: B.Tech tuition for students admitted in 2026 is ₹1,85,000 per year, BBA ₹1,10,000 per year, B.Com (Honours) ₹78,000 per year, BA ₹52,000 per year, and MBA ₹2,60,000 per year. Tuition is fixed at admission: the yearly tuition fee will not change for the batch until the normal duration of the programme ends, so a 2026 B.Tech student pays ₹1,85,000 in every one of the four years. Students who need extra semesters beyond the normal duration pay the fee applicable to the batch then running. A one-time admission fee of ₹25,000 is paid with the first instalment. Tuition is paid in two equal instalments each year, due on 15 July and 15 January. A late fee of ₹100 per day is charged after the due date, up to a maximum of ₹5,000. If fees are still unpaid 30 days after the due date, the student's name is struck off the rolls and re-admission needs the Registrar's approval and a re-admission fee of ₹2,500.

title: Hostel allotment and fees, 2026-27
text: Hostel rooms for first-year students are allotted after the first fee instalment is paid, in order of distance from home, starting with students from outside the state. Students whose permanent address is within 40 km of the campus are not eligible for a first-year hostel room. Fees for 2026-27 are ₹96,000 per year for a twin-sharing non-AC room and ₹1,18,000 per year for twin-sharing AC rooms, which are limited to second year and above. The mess is compulsory for all hostel residents and costs ₹42,000 per year. A refundable caution deposit of ₹10,000 is paid once. Hostel and mess fees are paid annually by 15 July. Since July 2024 all hostels, for women and men, follow the same 10 pm curfew; the gate re-opens at 5:30 am. Late entry needs a pass from the warden issued before 6 pm. Rooms come with a bed, mattress, study table, chair and cupboard; students bring their own bedding, bucket and lock.

title: Women's hostel rules (2022 handbook, superseded)
text: This page reproduces the women's hostel section of the 2022 hostel handbook, which was superseded in July 2024 when common rules were adopted for all hostels; it is kept for reference only. Under the 2022 rules, the women's hostel curfew was 8:30 pm on weekdays and 9 pm on weekends, while the men's hostel curfew was 10 pm. Night-out permission for women residents needed a written request from a parent sent to the warden at least 24 hours in advance. Visitors were allowed only in the reception area between 4 pm and 7 pm on Sundays. The fee for a twin-sharing room in the women's hostel was ₹88,000 per year and the mess cost ₹38,000 per year. Guests of residents could not stay overnight. Residents who broke the curfew three times in a semester were reported to their parents and could lose their room for the following year.

title: Lateral entry into B.Tech second year
text: Diploma holders in engineering can join the B.Tech programme directly in the second year (third semester) through lateral entry. Applicants need at least 55 percent in the diploma, or 50 percent for SC and ST candidates of the state, in a branch that matches or is allied to the B.Tech branch applied for. Lateral entry seats are supernumerary, equal to 10 percent of the intake of each branch, and are filled on diploma marks without the AAT. B.Sc graduates with Mathematics are also eligible for lateral entry, but only to the Computer Science and Civil branches. All lateral entry students must complete a bridge course in engineering mathematics during the third semester; the bridge course fee is ₹8,000, and the course must be passed before the fifth semester. Lateral entry students pay the yearly B.Tech tuition for three years and are eligible for need-based waivers but not merit scholarships.

title: MBA admissions 2026: eligibility and selection
text: The two-year MBA programme starting in July 2026 is open to graduates in any discipline with at least 50 percent aggregate marks, or 45 percent for reserved category candidates of the state. Final-year students are not eligible: the degree must be completed, with results declared, by the last date of the round in which the candidate applies. Candidates need either an AAT management score or a valid national management entrance test score from the last two years. Shortlisted candidates attend a group discussion and a personal interview on campus. The composite score used for the merit list is made up of the entrance test score 50 percent, personal interview 25 percent, group discussion 15 percent, and work experience 10 percent. Work experience is counted in full months after graduation, with 1 mark per completed 6 months up to a maximum of 10 marks; internships do not count. The intake is 120 seats, of which 15 percent are reserved for candidates with at least 2 years of full-time work experience.

title: Withdrawal and refund policy, 2026 intake
text: A student who withdraws must submit the withdrawal form signed by the student and a parent, with the original fee receipt. Refunds are made to the bank account the fee was paid from, within 30 days of the withdrawal form. Tuition refunds depend on the date of withdrawal: before 31 July 2026, the full tuition paid is refunded minus a processing charge of ₹2,000; from 1 August to 31 August 2026, 50 percent of the tuition fee is refunded; from 1 September 2026, no tuition is refunded. The one-time admission fee of ₹25,000 is non-refundable in all cases, including withdrawal before classes start and cancellation because the student got a seat elsewhere. The hostel caution deposit is refunded in full after room handover; hostel and mess fees are refunded for complete unused months only. Original certificates are never kept by the university and are returned the same day the withdrawal form is accepted.

title: Admission rounds and application fee, 2026 intake
text: Applications for the July 2026 intake are accepted in three rounds. Round 1: applications close on 15 March 2026, the AAT is held on 5 April 2026, and results are published on 20 April. Round 2: applications close on 10 May 2026, the AAT is held on 31 May 2026, and results are published on 12 June. Round 3 is a spot round on 30 June 2026 for vacant seats only, open to candidates who already hold an AAT score from round 1 or 2. The application fee is ₹1,200 per programme, or ₹600 for SC and ST candidates. A combined form for up to three programmes costs ₹1,800, or ₹900 for SC and ST candidates. The application fee is not refundable, including when a candidate is found ineligible. Edits to a submitted form, such as changing the test city, are allowed once, until 48 hours before the round closes. This schedule replaces the two-round schedule used for the 2025 intake.

title: Admission rounds and application fee, 2025 intake (superseded)
text: This schedule for the July 2025 intake is superseded by the three-round schedule for the 2026 intake and is kept only for reference. In 2025 there were two rounds. Round 1 applications closed on 31 March 2025 with the AAT on 20 April 2025, and round 2 applications closed on 31 May 2025 with the AAT on 15 June 2025. There was no spot round; vacant seats were offered from the round 2 waiting list. The application fee was ₹1,000 per programme, or ₹500 for SC and ST candidates, and there was no combined form for several programmes. Candidates applying to more than one programme paid the full fee for each. Corrections to submitted forms could be requested by email until the round closed. Results were sent by post as well as being published online, and admitted students had 10 days to pay the first instalment of fees.

title: Merit scholarships and sibling concession, 2026 batch onwards
text: Merit scholarships for students admitted from 2026 are a waiver of tuition fee only, not of the admission, hostel or examination fees. B.Tech: AAT rank 1 to 100 receives a 50 percent tuition waiver, rank 101 to 500 receives 25 percent. BBA, B.Com and BA: class twelve aggregate of 95 percent or above receives 30 percent, and 90 to 94.9 percent receives 15 percent. MBA: the top 10 on the merit list receive 25 percent. To keep the scholarship in later years, a student must have a CGPA of 7.5 or above at the end of each year and no backlogs; scholarships lost are not restored in later years. Need-based fee waivers of up to 40 percent are available for families with an annual income below ₹4,00,000, on documentary proof. A sibling concession of 10 percent of tuition is given to the second child while both siblings are enrolled. A student can receive only one scholarship or concession at a time, whichever is highest.

title: Merit scholarships for batches admitted before 2026
text: This scheme applies only to students admitted in 2025 or earlier; it does not apply to the 2026 batch, which has its own scheme. B.Tech: AAT rank 1 to 200 received a 50 percent tuition waiver, and rank 201 to 1,000 received 25 percent. BBA, B.Com and BA: class twelve aggregate of 92 percent or above received 30 percent. To keep the scholarship, students under this scheme need a CGPA of 8.0 or above at the end of each year, but a single backlog cleared in the next supplementary examination does not cancel the scholarship. Scholarships lost under this scheme can be restored once if the CGPA returns above 8.0 the following year. Need-based waivers under this scheme were capped at 30 percent for families with an annual income below ₹3,00,000. The sibling concession was 5 percent of tuition. Students under this scheme who are on scholarship continue under these rules until they graduate.

title: Transfer from other universities and credit transfer
text: Students from other recognised universities can transfer into a matching programme only at the start of the third semester, and only when vacant seats exist in that branch. Mid-year transfers, including after the first semester, are not accepted. Applications for transfer close on 30 June each year. The student must have passed all first-year subjects with no backlogs and a CGPA of at least 6.5. A credit evaluation fee of ₹15,000 is charged, and it is not refunded if the transfer is refused. A maximum of 40 percent of the total credits of the degree can be transferred from the previous university; any remaining first-year courses that do not map to ours must be completed as additional courses without extra fee. The degree is awarded by this university, and the transcript lists transferred credits as such, without grades. Transfer students are not eligible for merit scholarships in their first year here.

title: BBA, B.Com and BA admissions 2026: eligibility
text: For the BBA, B.Com (Honours) and BA programmes starting in July 2026, applicants need to have passed class twelve in any stream with at least 50 percent aggregate, or 45 percent for SC, ST and OBC non-creamy layer candidates of the state. B.Com (Honours) additionally needs Mathematics or Accountancy in class twelve. There is no entrance test for these programmes: admission is on the basis of class twelve marks. BBA applicants are shortlisted on marks and then attend a 15-minute personal interview, held on campus or online. BA applicants choose their major in the second semester, not at admission. Students who took a gap year after class twelve must submit a gap affidavit on stamp paper explaining the gap. Lateral entry is not available for these programmes, and students cannot switch from a BA to a BBA after the first semester. The application fee and round dates are the same as for B.Tech, and the same refund rules apply after admission.

title: Registration of births and deaths, and certificate copies
text: A birth or death that happens within city limits is registered at the ward office of the ward where it happened, not the ward where the family lives. Hospitals and nursing homes report births and deaths on their premises directly, and the family only collects the certificate. Home births and deaths must be reported by the head of the household. Registration within 21 days is free, and the first copy of the certificate is issued free. Registration between 22 and 30 days carries a late fee of ₹25. From 31 days up to one year, registration needs a late fee of ₹75, an affidavit on plain paper, and the written permission of the zonal registrar, which is given only at the zone office on Tuesdays and Fridays. After one year an order from a first class magistrate is required and the late fee is ₹150. Additional copies of a birth or death certificate cost ₹50 per copy and are ready within 3 working days. Digitally signed certificates with a QR code can also be downloaded from the portal at ₹20 per download and are valid in the same way as printed ones. A child's name can be added free of charge within 12 months of registration, and for ₹50 after that, up to 15 years from the date of birth.

title: Building plan approval routes and timelines
text: Residential buildings on plots of up to 300 square metres, with no more than ground plus two floors and a height of up to 10 metres, can be approved through the self-certification route. A registered architect uploads the plans and certifies that they comply with the building bye-laws, and the approval is issued within 7 working days of the online submission. All other buildings, and any residential plot above 300 square metres, follow the regular route: a site inspection is done and the approval is issued within 30 working days of a complete application. There is no deemed approval on either route; if the time limit is missed, the application is escalated to the city engineer. The scrutiny fee is ₹15 per square metre of total built-up area, payable on submission. An approval is valid for 3 years and can be extended once for 2 more years for a fee of ₹2,000. The owner must ask for a plinth inspection within 7 days of completing the plinth, and construction above the plinth cannot continue until it is cleared. Self-certified approvals are audited at random, and if the plans are found non-compliant the architect's registration can be suspended and the building can be sealed. Occupancy certificates are issued within 15 working days of the completion certificate.

title: Grievance redressal and service timelines
text: Civic complaints can be registered on the 24-hour helpline 1800 270 4410, on the citizen portal or at any ward office, and every complaint gets a docket number by SMS. The service standards are as follows. Garbage not collected is cleared the same day. A dead animal is removed within 24 hours. A streetlight that is not working is repaired within 72 hours. A water pipeline leak or a blocked drain is attended to within 48 hours. A pothole is filled within 10 working days, except from June to September, when only temporary patching is done. A request for mosquito fogging is handled within 3 working days. If a complaint is not resolved within its service standard, it is escalated automatically to the assistant commissioner of the ward, and after 7 more days to the zonal deputy commissioner. A complaint marked as closed can be reopened by the citizen within 7 days if the work was not actually done. The zonal deputy commissioner holds an open public hearing every Monday from 11 am to 1 pm at each zone office, and no appointment is needed.

title: Marriage registration
text: Marriages solemnised within city limits, or where either spouse lives within city limits, can be registered at any zone office. Both spouses and two witnesses must appear in person with original documents: proof of age for both spouses, such as a birth certificate, a school leaving certificate or a passport; proof of address; a government photo ID for each witness; the wedding invitation card or a certificate from the person who performed the ceremony; and two wedding photographs. The registration fee is ₹200 if the application is made within 90 days of the marriage and ₹1,000 after 90 days. Appointments are booked on the portal, and walk-in applications are taken only on Thursdays. The certificate is issued on the same day if all documents are in order. Additional certified copies cost ₹100 each. If either spouse was previously married, a divorce decree or the death certificate of the former spouse must also be produced. Registration is not refused because of a delay, but marriages more than five years old need an affidavit from both spouses.

title: Ward offices, zone offices and counter hours
text: The city has 64 wards grouped into four zones. Ward offices are open from 10 am to 5:30 pm, Monday to Friday, and from 10 am to 1:30 pm on Saturdays, and they are closed on the second and fourth Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Cash counters at ward offices close at 4 pm on weekdays and at 1 pm on Saturdays. Ward offices handle property tax payments, birth and death registration, pet registration and complaints. The four zone offices are open from 10 am to 6 pm, Monday to Saturday, and are closed on the second and fourth Saturdays; they handle building plans, trade licences, marriage registration and tax objections, and their cash counters stay open until 5 pm. In July and January, when property tax instalments fall due, ward office cash counters stay open until 7 pm on the last five working days of the month and open from 10 am to 2 pm on the last Sunday of the month. Payments on the citizen portal can be made at any time, and a payment made online before midnight on a due date is treated as on time. Cash payments above ₹20,000 are not accepted at any counter.

title: Pet dog and cat registration
text: Every pet dog and every pet cat kept within city limits must be registered with the veterinary section, and the registration must be renewed every year by 30 April. Registration costs ₹500 per year for each dog and ₹150 per year for each cat. The fee is waived for indie dogs and cats adopted from a registered shelter or animal welfare group, and for sterilised strays taken in as pets. Registration must be done within 30 days of getting the pet, or within 30 days of the animal turning three months old. The owner needs a valid anti-rabies vaccination certificate, a recent photo of the animal and proof of address. A metal tag with the registration number is issued, and it must be worn on the collar in public places. Keeping an unregistered dog carries a fine of ₹1,000, and keeping an unregistered cat carries a fine of ₹300. Owners must clean up after their pets in parks and on streets, or pay a fine of ₹500. Commercial breeders and pet shops need a separate trade licence and are not covered by pet registration.

title: Property tax schedule for 2026-27, effective 1 April 2026
text: This schedule applies to all assessed properties in the North, South, East and Central zones of the city from 1 April 2026 and replaces the 2024-26 property tax schedule. Property tax is levied on carpet area at an annual base rate per square foot that depends on the location category of the street: ₹3.20 on Category A streets, ₹2.60 on Category B streets and ₹2.10 on Category C streets. The base amount is multiplied by a usage factor of 1.0 for residential, 2.5 for commercial and 1.5 for institutional use, and by an age factor of 0.8 for buildings more than 25 years old. Tax is payable in two half-yearly instalments: the first half-year instalment is due by 31 July and the second half-year instalment is due by 31 January. The early payment rebate has been withdrawn from 2026-27, so no rebate is given for paying the full year in advance, even before the first due date. Vacancy remission is not available: a residential or commercial building that is locked, empty or unlet is taxed in full, because the remission for vacant buildings was discontinued with this schedule. Owner-occupied homes of senior citizens aged 60 or above get a 10 percent concession on the residential tax for up to 1,000 square feet of carpet area. A penalty of 2 percent per month or part of a month is charged on any instalment that is unpaid after its due date. A solid waste user charge of ₹60 per month for each residential unit is collected along with property tax and shown as a separate line on the bill.

title: Property tax schedule for 2024-26 (superseded)
text: Status: superseded on 1 April 2026 by the 2026-27 property tax schedule. This page is kept only because arrears for 2024-25 and 2025-26 are still worked out on it. Base rates per square foot of carpet area were ₹2.90 on Category A streets, ₹2.35 on Category B streets and ₹1.90 on Category C streets, with the same usage factors as today. The two half-yearly instalments were due by 30 June and 31 December. A rebate of 10 percent of the year's general tax was given when the full year was paid by 30 April. Under this schedule a residential building that stayed vacant for more than 90 consecutive days could get a vacancy remission of 50 percent of the general tax, if the owner applied at the ward office within 30 days of the end of the half-year. The penalty on late instalments was 1.5 percent per month. The senior citizen concession was 10 percent for up to 750 square feet of carpet area. Penalty on arrears from these years continues to be charged at the rate in force for the year the arrears belong to, not at the current rate.

title: Self-assessment returns, survey checks and objections
text: An owner must file a self-assessment return for a new building within 60 days of completion or occupation, whichever is earlier, and must file a fresh return whenever the carpet area or the use of the building changes by more than 10 percent. Returns can be filed on the citizen portal or at the ward office, and the declared carpet area must exclude external walls, common staircases and open terraces. Survey teams check declared areas using drone maps and site visits. If the surveyed carpet area exceeds the declared area by more than 5 percent, the owner pays the difference in tax for up to the previous 3 years, plus a penalty equal to twice the difference for the current year. If a residential building is found in commercial use without a fresh return, the commercial rate applies from the date of the survey and a flat penalty of ₹5,000 is added. Objections to a revised assessment can be filed with the zonal assessment officer within 30 days of the notice, with a fee of ₹100, but the undisputed portion of the tax must be paid first. A second appeal lies to the tax appeals bench within 60 days of the zonal order. Name transfer of a property in the tax record after a sale costs 0.1 percent of the registered sale value, with a minimum of ₹500 and a maximum of ₹10,000, if applied for within 3 months of registration.

title: Trade licences: three-year licence, effective 1 April 2025
text: From 1 April 2025, trade licences are issued for a block of three financial years, and there is no annual renewal. This replaces the one-year trade licence that had to be renewed every March. The fee for the whole three-year block is paid when the licence is issued: ₹1,800 for shops and offices up to 200 square feet, ₹4,500 for 201 to 500 square feet, and ₹9,000 above 500 square feet. Eating places pay double these amounts, and trades that store LPG, chemicals or fireworks also need a fire safety certificate before a licence is issued. A licence taken out part way through a block runs to the end of that block, and the fee is reduced by one third for each full financial year already over. New licences are issued within 15 working days of a complete application. Renewal for the next block must be applied for at least 30 days before the licence expires. Trading on an expired licence attracts a penalty of 25 percent of the fee for each quarter or part of a quarter. Changing the trade name or adding a partner costs ₹500. The licence certificate must be displayed at the premises. A GST registration or a shop and establishment registration does not replace the trade licence.

title: Tree felling and road-cutting permission
text: Permission is needed to cut down any tree with a trunk girth of more than 30 cm at 1.3 metres above the ground, whether the tree stands on public land or inside a private compound. The application fee is ₹200 per tree, and a refundable deposit of ₹5,000 per tree is collected. The deposit is refunded once the applicant has planted three saplings for every tree felled and the saplings have survived for one year. The tree officer inspects the site and decides within 21 days; a tree that is dead or in danger of falling is dealt with within 72 hours. Pruning does not need permission unless more than one third of the canopy is removed. Cutting a tree without permission carries a fine of ₹25,000 per tree. Permission to cut a public road, for example to lay a private pipe or cable, is given by the zonal engineer within 10 working days, and the road restoration charge is paid in advance at ₹1,100 per running metre for tar roads and ₹1,600 per running metre for concrete roads. No road-cutting is allowed from 1 June to 30 September except for emergency repairs.

title: Household solid waste collection schedule and rules
text: Door-to-door collection vehicles cover every ward between 7 am and 11 am. Wet waste, meaning kitchen and food waste, is collected every day, including Sundays. Dry waste is collected only on Wednesdays and Saturdays, and it is not picked up on other days, so households should store paper, plastic, metal, glass and cloth until then. Sanitary waste such as diapers and sanitary pads must be wrapped in newspaper, marked with a red cross, and handed over in a separate bag with the wet waste on any day. Domestic hazardous waste, such as batteries, tube lights, expired medicines and paint cans, is collected on the first Saturday of each month. Waste that is not segregated is refused after one warning, and households are fined ₹200 for a first offence and ₹500 for each repeat. Burning waste in the open carries a fine of ₹5,000, and littering in public places carries a fine of ₹500. If the collection vehicle misses a street, a complaint made before noon gets the waste collected the same day by 5 pm. The solid waste user charge of ₹60 per month per residential unit is collected with property tax.

title: Bulk waste, garden waste and construction debris pickup
text: Households can book a bulk waste pickup for old furniture, mattresses, large appliances and garden cuttings through the helpline or the portal, at least 48 hours in advance. Each residential property gets two free bulk pickups per financial year, each of up to one cubic metre, and any further pickup costs ₹400. Construction and demolition debris is not covered by the free pickups: it is charged at ₹1,200 per tractor load of about 2.5 cubic metres and is collected within 3 working days of booking. Dumping debris on a road, drain or vacant plot carries a fine of ₹10,000 and the cost of removal. Electronic waste is taken only at the e-waste collection drive held on the second Sunday of every month at the four zone offices. Housing societies with more than 100 flats, and premises producing more than 100 kg of waste a day, are bulk generators and must compost or process their wet waste on site; they get a 5 percent rebate on the solid waste user charge once on-site processing is certified by the ward sanitary inspector.

title: Domestic water and sewer connections and tariff
text: This page covers houses and residential buildings. A new 15 mm, or half inch, domestic water connection costs ₹4,200, including the meter. A 20 mm connection, required for buildings with more than four flats, costs ₹7,500. A domestic sewer connection costs ₹2,800 per property. Where the connection needs a public road to be cut, a road restoration charge is billed separately at ₹1,100 per running metre for tar roads and ₹1,600 per running metre for concrete roads. Connections are released only in the name of the owner shown in the property tax record; a tenant can be added as a billing contact. New connections are released within 15 working days of payment. Domestic water is metered and billed monthly at ₹6 per kilolitre for the first 15 kilolitres, ₹11 per kilolitre from 15 to 30 kilolitres, and ₹20 per kilolitre above 30 kilolitres, with a minimum charge of ₹90 per month. Supply times are 6 am to 8 am in the North and East zones and 5:30 am to 7:30 am in the South and Central zones, and supply moves to alternate days from April to June. A household may not fit a booster pump directly on the service line; the fine is ₹2,000 and the pump is seized.

title: Commercial and institutional water and sewer connections
text: This page covers shops, hotels, hospitals, schools, offices and other non-domestic premises. A new 15 mm commercial water connection costs ₹9,000, including the meter, and a 20 mm connection costs ₹14,000. Connections above 20 mm need a hydraulic assessment by the water works engineer and are priced separately. A commercial sewer connection costs ₹6,500 per property, and premises that discharge kitchen or workshop waste must fit a grease trap before the sewer connection is released. Road restoration charges are the same as for domestic connections. Commercial water is billed monthly at a flat ₹40 per kilolitre, with a minimum charge of ₹600 per month, and there is no slab system. Commercial connections are released within 21 working days of payment. A security deposit equal to three months' minimum charge is collected with the connection charge and refunded when the connection is closed. Hotels and hospitals using more than 50 kilolitres a day must have a separate underground storage sump, and supply to them can be reduced during summer shortages before domestic supply is reduced.

title: Blue badge applications and renewals
text: Blue badges let disabled people park closer to where they need to go. There is no fee for a blue badge in Kestrel Bay: the council does not charge for new badges, renewals or replacements of lost or damaged badges. Apply online or with a paper form from any library. You will need proof of identity, proof that you live in the county, a recent passport-style photo, and evidence of eligibility such as an award letter for the higher rate mobility component of a disability benefit. The council aims to make a decision within 8 weeks of receiving a complete application, and applicants who need a mobility assessment are offered an appointment within 4 weeks. Badges last up to 3 years. Renewals can be submitted up to 12 weeks before the expiry date. A stolen badge can be replaced only after the theft has been reported to the police and a crime reference number has been provided.

title: Council tax charges and instalments 2026/27
text: These charges apply from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 and replace the 2025/26 charges. Average annual council tax across the county, including the county, fire and police precepts but before town and parish precepts, is: Band A £1,489.24, Band B £1,737.45, Band C £1,985.66, Band D £2,233.87, Band E £2,730.29, Band F £3,226.70, Band G £3,723.12 and Band H £4,467.74. From 2026/27 bills are payable in 12 monthly instalments from April to March by default. Residents who prefer the old pattern of 10 monthly instalments from April to January can ask for it at any time before 30 April. Direct debit customers can choose a payment date of the 1st, 10th, 20th or 28th of the month; all other methods are due on the 1st. If an instalment is missed, a reminder notice gives 7 days to bring the account up to date. If a second instalment is missed in the same year, the right to pay by instalments is lost and the whole remaining balance becomes due. Court summons costs of £85 are added if the council has to apply for a liability order.

title: Council tax charges and instalments 2025/26 (superseded)
text: Superseded on 1 April 2026 by the 2026/27 charges; kept for reference for residents checking last year's bills. Average annual council tax across the county for 2025/26, including the county, fire and police precepts but before town and parish precepts, was: Band A £1,405.67, Band B £1,639.95, Band C £1,874.22, Band D £2,108.50, Band E £2,577.05, Band F £3,045.61, Band G £3,514.17 and Band H £4,217.00. In 2025/26 bills were payable in 10 monthly instalments from April to January by default, with 12 instalments available on request. Direct debit customers could choose the 1st or the 15th of the month. The reminder and summons process was the same as now, except that court summons costs were £76. Residents who moved into the county part way through 2025/26 were billed from the date they moved in, with the first instalment due 14 days after the bill was issued. Refunds of overpaid 2025/26 council tax are still made on request, by bank transfer within 10 working days.

title: Council tax discounts, exemptions and premiums
text: Single person discount: if only one adult aged 18 or over lives in a property, the bill is reduced by 25 percent. Tell us within 21 days of becoming the only adult; the discount can be backdated by up to 6 months only, even if you lived alone for longer. Students: full-time students are disregarded when counting adults, and a property occupied only by full-time students is exempt. Care leavers: young people who left the council's care are exempt from council tax until their 25th birthday, if they live in the county. Empty homes: there is no discount for empty properties, whether furnished or unfurnished, and this includes homes undergoing major repairs or renovation; the full charge applies from the day the property becomes empty. After 12 months empty, a premium of 100 percent is added, rising to 200 percent after 5 years. Second homes: from 1 April 2026 a premium of 100 percent applies to furnished homes that are no one's main residence. Annexes used by a family member as their main home get a 50 percent discount. Council tax reduction for people on low incomes is applied for separately.

title: Libraries: membership, loans and charges
text: Library membership is free for everyone who lives, works or studies in the county. Adults and children can borrow up to 15 items at a time, and the standard loan period is 3 weeks for books, audiobooks and DVDs. Items can be renewed up to 3 times online, by phone or in person, unless another member has reserved them. Since 1 September 2025 there are no overdue fines on any items for any age, including adult loans. Items more than 6 weeks overdue are treated as lost: the replacement cost is charged to the account, and borrowing is blocked until the item is returned or paid for. If a lost item is returned within 6 months, the replacement charge is refunded. Reservations are free. Printing and photocopying cost 15p per A4 black and white page and 60p per colour page. Oldhaven Central Library is open on Sundays from 11 am to 3 pm; the other branches are closed on Sundays and Mondays.

title: Residents' and visitor parking permits, from 1 January 2026
text: These prices apply from 1 January 2026 and replace the 2024 permit tariff. A first residents' parking permit costs £68 a year, and a second permit for the same household costs £120 a year. A third permit is not available in any zone. Fully electric vehicles pay half price for a first or second permit. Permits are virtual and linked to the vehicle registration, so nothing is displayed in the windscreen. Visitor parking is booked as virtual sessions through the parking account at £1.20 per day session. Each household can buy up to 60 visitor sessions per year, counted from the date the account was opened. Residents aged 75 or over get 30 free visitor sessions a year on top of that. A permit allows parking in any permit bay in your zone when a space is available; it does not reserve a space. Permit holders who move within the same zone can transfer the permit for free; moving to a different zone needs a new permit, with a refund for complete unused months.

title: Residents' and visitor parking permits, 2024 tariff (superseded)
text: This tariff is superseded by the permit prices that took effect on 1 January 2026 and is kept for reference only. Under the 2024 tariff a first residents' parking permit cost £55 a year, and a second permit for the same household cost £95 a year. A third permit was available in zones C and F only, at £150 a year. Electric vehicles paid the same price as other vehicles. Permits were paper permits displayed in the windscreen, and a lost permit cost £15 to replace. Visitor permits were sold as books of paper scratch cards, 10 cards for £10, and each household could buy up to 100 visitor cards per year. Residents aged 75 or over received 20 free visitor cards a year. Unused scratch cards bought under this tariff remain valid until 31 December 2026 and can be exchanged for virtual sessions at the customer service centre in Oldhaven.

title: Penalty charge notices: paying and challenging
text: Penalty charges for parking contraventions are £70 for higher level contraventions, such as parking on yellow lines, and £50 for lower level ones, such as overstaying in a pay and display bay. The charge is reduced by 50 percent if paid within 14 days of the date of the notice. You can make an informal challenge online within 28 days. If your informal challenge is received within the 14-day discount period and is rejected, the council will re-offer the discount for a further 21 days from the date of the rejection letter. If you do not pay or challenge within 28 days, a notice to owner is sent to the registered keeper, and the discount is no longer available. A formal representation can then be made within 28 days of the notice to owner, and if that is rejected you can appeal to the independent traffic adjudicator. Unpaid charges increase by 50 percent with a charge certificate. Blue badge holders who forgot to display the badge can have the first such penalty in any 12 months cancelled on request.

title: Pest control service for residents
text: The council's pest control team treats rats and mice inside residents' homes free of charge, with up to 3 visits per treatment course. Rats in gardens are also treated free if there are signs of burrows. Other treatments are charged: wasps £72 per nest, bed bugs £145 for up to 3 rooms, and cockroaches £118. Fleas are treated for £95. Residents receiving council tax reduction get a 50 percent discount on charged treatments. The service does not deal with squirrels, foxes, pigeons or bees; for honeybee swarms, the council can put you in touch with a local beekeepers' volunteer list. Appointments are available Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm, and most are booked within 3 working days of the request. Payment is taken when booking, and a charged treatment cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice is refunded minus £20. Treatments for businesses and landlords with more than two properties are not offered.

title: Reporting potholes and claiming for vehicle damage
text: Potholes on council roads can be reported online with a photo and the nearest house number or lamp post number. Each report is inspected within 5 working days. Potholes rated as an emergency, deeper than 40 mm on a main road or presenting an immediate danger, are made safe within 24 hours. Other potholes that meet the repair standard are fixed within 28 days. Trunk roads and the coast road between Saltmarsh Quay and Fenwick St Mary are managed by the national highways body, not the council, so claims for those roads must go to them. To claim for damage caused by a pothole on a council road, submit the claim form within 6 months of the incident with photos of the pothole and the damage, the location, and a repair invoice or two quotes. The council is not liable where the pothole had not been reported before the incident, or where it was within the repair period when the damage happened. Decisions on claims are made within 42 days.

title: Saltmarsh Quay household recycling centre
text: The Saltmarsh Quay household recycling centre on Harbour Road is open to county residents. Summer hours, from 1 April to 30 September, are 8 am to 6 pm. Winter hours, from 1 October to 31 March, are 9 am to 4 pm. The Saltmarsh Quay site is closed on Wednesdays all year, and on Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day. Cars can visit without booking.
